topic_order: Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic States

Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.title: Positronium resonance of electric monopoles in quantum spin ice
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.authors: José Maria Cruz, Hidemaro Suwa, Masafumi Udagawa
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.abstract: Quantum spin ice attracts considerable attention due to its remarkable low-energy properties, described by the effective gauge theory, which mimics the quantum electrodynamics (QED). The ``effective" QED in quantum spin ice is beyond the ``real" QED in our universe in many respects. Above all, the effective QED hosts two kinds of gapped particles, the electric monopole, in addition to the magnetic monopole. Among the two monopoles, the electric monopole is of purely quantum origin, and its character has not been well resolved. In this work, we focus on the Rokhsar Kivelson point of the quantum dimer model, as the low-energy description of the quantum XXZ model on a pyrochlore lattice, and address the excitation spectrum of the electric monopoles, by combining the quantum Monte Carlo simulation with the stochastic analytical continuation. Most strikingly, the electric monopole spectrum exhibits clear double-peak structure, corresponding to the bound states and scattering states of electric monopoles. The lower-energy peak is attributed to the exciton-like bound state of an electric monopole pair, a signal of positronium in quantum spin ice. We found that the flippable loop operator serves as a local physical observable to excite a pair of electric monopoles, implying that monopoles can be detected through lattice or optical response.

Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.title: Unraveling square and kagome lattice frustrated magnetism by scalable tensor networks
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.authors: Xing-Yu Zhang, Jutho Haegeman, Yuchi He
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.abstract: We extend the scalability of variational infinite two-dimensional tensor network methods with application to investigate frustrated magnetism of the square-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ model and kagome-lattice Heisenberg model. In the sign-problem-free limit of the square-lattice model, we achieve high ground-state energy precision comparable to quantum Monte Carlo methods. With no obstruction beyond this limit, our method obtains direct estimates of order parameters. For the square-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ model, we determine isotropic plaquette order in the valence-bond solid region. For the model near $J_2/J_1=0.5$, and the kagome lattice Heisenberg model, our data indicate linear-dispersion gapless states. To probe the candidate spin-liquid nature of the highly frustrated cases, we go beyond inferring the absence of symmetry-breaking orders and analyze susceptibilities that characterize gapless spin liquids. By estimating scaling dimensions, our data indicate a stable gapless spin liquid on the kagome lattice, and competing scenarios for the intermediate regime of the square-lattice model. Our developments include parallelization and randomized low-rank methods and largely expand the frontier of high-precision variational numerics for quantum phases of matter.

Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.title: Electrical addressing of compensated magnetic order in artificial spin ice
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.authors: Stéphane Nilsson, Lauren J. Riddiford, Emily Darwin, Hans J. Hug, Aleš Hrabec, Laura J. Heyderman
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.abstract: Compensated magnetic systems, such as antiferromagnets, hold immense potential for spintronic devices thanks to vanishing stray fields, robustness to perturbations, and ultrafast dynamics. Yet, electrical writing and reading of their order remains a major challenge. Here we use artificial spin ice as a mesoscale platform in which compensated order can be engineered, directly imaged, and electrically controlled. Specifically, we demonstrate combined electrical writing and reading of a compensated state in a triangular artificial spin ice. Exploiting the orientation dependence of the spin-orbit torque switching current, we independently switch three nanomagnet sublattices through a single current channel, with the planar Hall effect providing sublattice-resolved readout. This grants access to all eight magnetization states of the triangular plaquette, including its fully compensated state, yielding a nonlinear, history-dependent electrical response. Our results establish an approach to electrically programmable compensated magnetic systems and provide an important foundation for reconfigurable magnetic devices and unconventional computing.

Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.title: Facilitated Relaxation Overrides Energetic Pathways in a Multiphase Square-Kagome Artificial Spin Ice
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.authors: Wen-Cheng Yue, Zixiong Yuan, Peiyuan Huang, Ziao Wang, Hangyu Liu, Tianyu Li, Nuo-Zhou Yang, Jingyue Gao, Chen Ku, Shuo Song, Jiyao Shang, Yang-Yang Lyu, Yihuang Xiong, Xuecou Tu, Liang He, Xun Cao, Ying Dong, Huabing Wang, Peiheng Wu, Cristiano Nisoli, Yong-Lei Wang
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.abstract: Relaxation in interacting many-body systems is typically assumed to follow energy minimization, yet local dynamical rules can determine which microscopic pathways are accessible. In facilitated relaxation, these pathways are enabled or blocked by neighboring configurations. However, isolating such rules in natural materials is difficult because energetics, disorder and dynamics are usually entangled. Here we realize a geometrically tunable square-kagome artificial spin ice-a lithographic nanomagnet array-that provides a clean, designable platform for facilitated relaxation. The array hosts two tunable nearest-neighbor interactions and supports multiple low-energy phases: spin crystal, spin liquid and spin foam. In the spin-foam phase, abundant facilitator configurations allow relaxation to follow Boltzmann statistics. In the spin-crystal phase, by contrast, domain-wall excitations are trapped in non-Boltzmann distributions, although energetically preferred relaxation channels exist. The ordered crystal background lacks the facilitators needed to connect topologically distinct domain-wall classes. These classes are therefore kinetically isolated, as observed in both experiment and Monte Carlo simulation. Our results show that transition-network topology can override energetic relaxation, establishing artificial spin ice as a programmable platform for constrained dynamics and nonergodic relaxation.

Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.title: Frustrated Magnetism from Dimerized $S = 1/2$ Co$^{2+}$ in Rose-Phase Na$_2$CoP$_2$O$_7$
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.authors: Shukun Li, Leon Ma, Xianghan Xu
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.abstract: We report the growth of high-quality single crystals and the magnetic, thermodynamic, and dielectric properties of rose-phase Na$_2$CoP$_2$O$_7$, a low-symmetry magnet in which corner-sharing Co$^{2+}$ dimers form an approximately triangular network. Magnetic measurements reveal dominant antiferromagnetic interactions and pronounced anisotropy among effective $S=1/2$ Co$^{2+}$ moments. Broad low-temperature maxima in the magnetic susceptibility and heat capacity suggest the development of short-range magnetic correlations below approximately 4 K. The large separation between the absolute Curie--Weiss temperatures and the characteristic correlation temperature indicates strong magnetic frustration arising from competing interactions within the coupled-dimer network. Applied magnetic fields suppress these anomalies and reduce the recovered magnetic entropy, suggesting further enhancement of frustration under field. A systematic magnetodielectric response closely follows the field dependence of the magnetization, indicating coupling between magnetic and dielectric degrees of freedom. The low lattice symmetry enables multiple inequivalent exchange pathways and anisotropic interactions while relaxing symmetry constraints on coupling among spin, lattice, and dielectric degrees of freedom. These results establish rose-phase Na$_2$CoP$_2$O$_7$ as a platform for exploring frustrated quantum magnetism and coupled functionalities in effective $S=1/2$ magnets.

Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.title: Gapless Nature of Spin Liquid in the $S=1/2$ Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet with Neural-Network Quantum States
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.authors: Andreas Raikos, Alessandro Sinibaldi, Riccardo Rende, Giuseppe Carleo, Federico Becca, Luciano Loris Viteritti
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.abstract: Whether the spin-$1/2$ kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet hosts a gapped $\mathbb{Z}_2$ or a gapless $U(1)$ Dirac spin liquid remains a central open question in frustrated magnetism. Here, we address this question by directly computing the triplet gap with a neural-network quantum state that does not presuppose any specific spin-liquid structure. Applying a time-reversal symmetric transformer-based ansatz to clusters of up to $768$ sites, we obtain state-of-the-art variational energies on two-dimensional lattices with periodic boundary conditions and estimate an energy per site of $-0.43873(12)$ in the thermodynamic limit. Finite-size scaling of the magnetic order parameter and triplet excitation gap shows that both extrapolate to zero in the thermodynamic limit. Together, these results provide independent and direct evidence of a gapless spin-liquid ground state, consistent with the $U(1)$ Dirac spin liquid. More broadly, they demonstrate that neural-network quantum states can resolve ground-state properties of frustrated quantum magnets that remain challenging for conventional numerical methods.

Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.authors: Wen-Cheng Yue, Zixiong Yuan, Peiyuan Huang, Ziao Wang, Hangyu Liu, Tianyu Li, Nuo-Zhou Yang, Jingyue Gao, Chen Ku, Shuo Song, Jiyao Shang, Yang-Yang Lyu, Yihuang Xiong, Xuecou Tu, Liang He, Xun Cao, Ying Dong, Huabing Wang, Peiheng Wu, Cristiano Nisoli, Yong-Lei Wang

Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.title: Geometry-driven magnetization reversal and spin-wave dynamics in permalloy artificial anti–spin ice lattices
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.authors: Szymon P. Oramus, Riccardo Fornari, Gianluca Gubbiotti, Adekunle O. Adeyeye
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.abstract: Antiartificial spin ice (AASI), realized through spin-ice-derived antidot lattices of stadium-shaped holes in continuous Permalloy ( Ni 81 Fe 19 ) films, provides a powerful route for embedding geometry-induced magnetic anisotropy within a connected magnonic medium. Here, homogeneous and bicomponent AASI lattices are investigated through a combined experimental and micromagnetic approach, establishing a direct link between lattice geometry, magnetization reversal, and spin-wave (SW) dynamics. Magneto-optical Kerr effect measurements, Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy, and simulations reveal that antidot size, lattice heterogeneity, and magnetic field orientation collectively govern both equilibrium states and dynamic excitations. The static response exhibits pronounced angular anisotropy in coercivity and remanence, with bicomponent lattices showing distinct reversal pathways and shifted anisotropy extrema relative to homogeneous systems. These variations are directly reflected in the SW spectra, where edge-, node-, and domain-wall-localized modes, as well as mode splitting and frequency flattening, emerge as signatures of geometry-induced magnetization textures. The excellent agreement between experiment and simulation establishes a microscopic connection between equilibrium magnetic configurations and SW excitations. These findings demonstrate a direct transfer of configurational anisotropy into tunable magnonic functionality, highlighting AASI as a versatile platform for geometry-encoded SW architectures.

Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.title: Monopoles, Scattering and Generalized Symmetries on a Quantum Computer
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.authors: Oliver O'Brien, Atsushi Ueda, Etienne Granet, Henrik Dreyer, Frank Verstraete
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.abstract: Quantum computers have advanced to the stage that interesting many-body quantum phenomena can be observed. A striking example is the magnetic monopole paradox, a problem that was only solved recently using the language of generalized symmetries. Here we demonstrate a quantum spin chain analogue of magnetic monopole scattering on Quantinuum System Model H2. We implement a novel protocol for preparing a localized quasiparticle wavepacket on top of the ground state. By combining this protocol with time evolution across a duality defect, we efficiently convert local particles into non-local string-like excitations. We demonstrate this particle-to-string conversion in the transverse-field Ising model and a symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase of the cluster model. Our results establish duality defects and generalized symmetries as practical resources for preparing and probing non-local excitations on quantum hardware.

Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.title: $^{55}$Mn-NMR/NQR study on the kagome metal Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$: Re-examining the possibility of spin-singlet paired state
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.authors: Qing-Ping Ding, Yongbin Lee, Charuni Dissanayake, Yasuyuki Nakajima, Yuji Furukawa
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.abstract: Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$ is a Mn-based kagome metal that has been proposed to be close to a ferromagnetic instability. Recent $^{55}$Mn nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) study suggested the emergence of a spin-singlet paired state below $\sim$10 K. To clarify its low-energy magnetic and electronic properties, we performed $^{55}$Mn NMR and nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR) measurements on single-crystalline Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$. From the detailed NMR/NQR spectrum measurements and the DFT calculations, a quadrupolar frequency of $ν_{\rm Q}$ = 4.6$\sim$4.8 MHz and an asymmetry parameter of $η$ = 0.45$\sim$0.48 as well as the principal axes of electric field gradient EFG for the Mn site were determined. The temperature dependence of Knight shift ($K$) shows a similar temperature dependence of the DC magnetic susceptibility $χ$ except for the low-temperature region below $\sim$ 50 K where $K$ is almost constant while $χ$ keeps increasing, which suggests that the increase in $χ$ at low temperatures is not intrinsic. $^{55}$Mn spin-lattice relaxation rate divided by temperature ($1/T_1T$) is found to be nearly constant, confirming the metallic state of Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$ from a microscopic point of view. Furthermore, no peak in $1/T_1T$ is observed near 10 K, and neither the Knight shift nor the linewidth shows any reductions at low temperatures. These results suggest no clear signature for the spin-singlet pairing around 10 K in Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$.

Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.title: Spin Structure Factor of the classical Ising Model on the Centered Pyrochlore Lattice
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.authors: L. Xu, T. Kreißel, N. Davier, L. D. C. Jaubert, L. Pollet
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.abstract: We present the spin structure factor of the Ising model on the centered pyrochlore lattice. Generalizing Henley's method [Phys. Rev. B 71, 014424] to the case of inequivalent center and vertex spins, we obtain spin correlation functions that are in excellent agreement with Monte Carlo results and can capture sharp and broadened pinch points, also at finite temperature. Our approach can be extended to other centered lattice structures in classical frustrated magnetism.

Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.title: Trapped fermions frustrate multiterminal Josephson networks
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.authors: Antonio Manesco, Karsten Flensberg
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.abstract: Coherent control of fermions has become a standard approach for engineering quantum devices. Here, we explore parity-induced frustration in multiterminal Josephson arrays. We focus on odd-parity Josephson trijunctions, where the presence of a trapped fermion induces a phase winding in each trijunction. Connecting these trijunctions constrains their shared phases, resulting in a long-distance phase coherence where the frustrated configurations dominate the low-energy physics. In the classical regime, these arrays map onto the Kagome XY antiferromagnet, whose established Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition yields algebraically decaying $6e$ phase correlations. We show that the $6e$ phase coherence is manifested as a pronounced third harmonic in the current-phase relation of these arrays. While quantum phase fluctuations suppress the $6e$ coherence, we show that through spin-orbit coupling they also lead to spin correlations and entanglement between the trapped fermions. Our results establish fermion-induced frustration as a route to composite superconducting coherence and phase-mediated spin entanglement in superconductor-semiconductor artificial quantum materials.

Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.title: Contrasting fate of holes introduced by Fe or In in kagome metal CoSn
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.authors: Véronique Brouet, Laure Thomarat, Patrick Le Fèvre, Ethan Saiman, Jean-Pascal Rueff, Oleg Rubel, Victor Balédent, François Bertran
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.abstract: CoSn is a kagome metal with well-defined flat bands 0.2 eV below the Fermi level EF. Moving them across EF would offer a rare opportunity to investigate their impact on electronic properties. Using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and X-ray absorption at the Co K-edge, we examine two routes to introduce holes in this compound, through Co/Fe or Sn/In substitutions. Substituting In for Sn produces an almost rigid upward shift of the bands toward EF, as expected for hole doping, whereas substituting Fe for Co leads to an unexpected downward shift. Density functional theory calculations reproduce these opposite trends and trace the unusual behavior of Fe to its local magnetic moment. The moment keeps the hole on the Fe impurity and imposes an attractive electrostatic potential on neighboring Co atoms. Overall, both substitutions bring weakly dispersing states close to EF, the flat bands of the Co kagome lattice upon In substitution and partly localized states around magnetic Fe impurities upon Fe substitution.

Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.title: Photon condensation driven by scalar spin chirality
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.authors: Dimitrije Stepanenko, Daniel Loss, Mircea Trif
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.abstract: Gauge invariance forbids equilibrium photon condensation for spatially uniform electric-dipole coupling, motivating alternative routes based on orbital magnetic response. We show that triangular molecular magnets coupled to a cavity support photon condensation driven by emergent scalar spin chirality. Starting from the half-filled Hubbard model in the Mott regime, we derive an effective Hamiltonian in which virtual ring exchange couples the cavity flux directly to scalar spin chirality. Mean-field theory, collective-fluctuation calculations, and finite-size exact diagonalization reveal a phase with spontaneous chirality ordering and a macroscopic cavity displacement, together with hybrid chirality-photon excitations. The condensation threshold can be tuned electrically through the molecular chirality splitting. Our results establish emergent orbital degrees of freedom in frustrated magnets as a route to equilibrium light-matter ordering beyond conventional dipolar cavity quantum electrodynamics.

Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.title: Kagome Flat Bands from Self-Assembled Water on Non-van der Waals 2D Materials
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.authors: Tom Barnowsky, Madeleine Christie, Anastasiia Nihei, Rico Friedrich
Spin Ice & Frustrated Magnetism.abstract: The properties of two-dimensional (2D) materials are governed not only by their intrinsic electronic structure but also in particular by their surface chemistry and interactions with the environment. The surfaces of non-van der Waals (non-vdW) 2D materials are intrinsically reactive and may require chemical stabilization under realistic experimental conditions. Here, we perform a systematic first-principles study of water passivation of non-vdW 2D materials and demonstrate that molecular water adsorption is energetically and dynamically favored for a wide range of systems. Rather than dissociating, water molecules frequently remain intact and form adsorbed ordered surface overlayers. These overlayers can adopt a kagome lattice geometry, leading to the emergence of flat electronic bands directly at the valence-band edge. Analysis of the electronic structure reveals a strong intermolecular coupling between neighboring water lone pairs within this kagome topology, while the locked molecular orientations simultaneously produce an electrostatically frustrated surface potential. These findings establish water not only as a stabilizing agent but also as an active element for electronic structure engineering of non-vdW 2D surfaces.

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: Canonical spin glass behavior and memory effects in van der Waals magnet (Fe0.55Ni0.45)3GaTe2
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: P. Biswal, Kakan Deb, Nitesh Kumar, D. Samal, Prabhat Mandal
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.abstract: We demonstrate the canonical spin-glass behavior and non-equilibrium dynamics in a single-crystalline Ni-doped van der Waals magnet (Fe0.55Ni0.45)3GaTe2 with a freezing temperature $T_f \approx 45.5$ K from detailed ac susceptibility and dc magnetization measurements. The temperature-dependent dc magnetization exhibits strong magnetic irreversibility and the ac susceptibility shows that the peak at $T_f$ shifts towards higher temperatures with increase in ac frequency, indicating the presence of a spin glass state. The relative shift of the freezing temperature $δT_f$ per decade of frequency in ac susceptibility is estimated to be 0.0072. Dynamic scaling analysis of the frequency-dependent freezing temperature using the power law reveals the single spin flip relaxation time $τ_0=2\times10^{-13}$ s and critical exponent $zν=8.1$, while the Vogel-Fulcher law yields Vogel-Fulcher temperature $T_0=43$ K and activation energy $E_a/k_B=81$ K with $E_a/k_BT_0=1.88$. The obtained values of these characteristic parameters lie well within the range associated with a canonical spin glass. The detailed non-equilibrium dynamics study, involving the magnetic relaxation and memory effect, further confirms the glassy behavior. The memory effect in zero-field-cooled magnetization establishes that the glassy state arises from the cooperative spin-spin interaction and not from superparamagnetism. The asymmetric response of magnetic relaxation with respect to negative and positive temperature cycle favors the hierarchical model of memory effects over the droplet model.

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: From a High-T$\rm_C$ Spin-Gapless Semiconductor to a Spin-Glass: The Role of Disorder in NiMnCrAl
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Arka Patra, Tufan Roy, Nilofar Kurawle, Tamaghna Maitra, Souvik Banerjee, Mantu Modak, Shuvankar Gupta, Sudip Chakraborty, Soumya Bhowmik, Papri Dasgupta, Rajashri Urkude, Biplab Ghosh, D. Bhattacharyya, A. Sundaresan, Sudhindra Rayaprol, Masafumi Shirai, Chandan Mazumdar
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.abstract: We combine first-principles calculations with structural, magnetic, and transport measurements to investigate the influence of chemical disorder on the quaternary Heusler alloy NiMnCrAl. For the ordered Y-type structure, density-functional-theory calculations predict a ferrimagnetic spin-gapless-semiconducting state with a total magnetic moment of $1.99\,μ_{\mathrm{B}}/\mathrm{f.u.}$ and a mean-field ordering temperature of approximately $1300~\mathrm{K}$. Polycrystalline NiMnCrAl forms in a single average cubic phase; however, combined x-ray diffraction, neutron diffraction, and extended x-ray absorption fine-structure measurements reveal substantial antisite disorder, characterized by predominantly B2-like disorder with additional cross-sublattice mixing. No long-range ferrimagnetic transition is observed up to $700~\mathrm{K}$. Instead, the compound exhibits a broad magnetic anomaly near $37~\mathrm{K}$, frequency-dependent ac susceptibility, slow stretched-exponential relaxation, and field-cooled and zero-field-cooled memory effects, establishing a glassy magnetic state. The electrical resistivity is metallic and the Seebeck coefficient is negative, consistent with the loss of the ideal spin-gapless electronic structure. Exchange-interaction calculations show that antisite disorder introduces short Mn--Mn separations and competing antiferromagnetic Mn--Mn and Mn--Cr interactions, providing a microscopic basis for magnetic frustration. These results demonstrate the strong sensitivity to the predicted spin-gapless and ferrimagnetic states of NiMnCrAl to chemical disorder.

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: Physical interpretation of spin-glass models with correlated disorder
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Hidetoshi Nishimori
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.abstract: Ising spin-glass models with a specific type of correlated bond disorder have recently been used to relate properties of spin-glass phases, such as temperature chaos and magnetic-field chaos, to ferromagnetic order. This correlated disorder has a simple physical interpretation, which underlies the sampling procedure introduced by Oshima, Arai, and Hukushima for numerical simulations: the bond configuration is obtained from the Edwards-Anderson model with the symmetric $\pm J$ distribution by drawing one of its equilibrium spin configurations and writing the model in the gauge in which this reference configuration becomes the all-up state. The construction is analogous to the Mattis model, with the roles of the ferromagnet and the spin glass reversed: whereas the Mattis model is a ferromagnet in disguise, the ferromagnetic phase of the correlated model is essentially a spin-glass phase in disguise. The frustration statistics of the correlated-disorder model are exactly those of the symmetric $\pm J$ model, and, in a generalization with an additional parameter $γ$, the probabilities of the gauge equivalence classes are determined by $γ$ alone, whereas the inverse temperature at which the reference configuration is drawn determines only the distribution within each class. The magnetization of this model is the overlap with the reference configuration. Through this correspondence, studies of its ferromagnetic phase have led to unexpected results on temperature chaos and magnetic-field chaos in the spin-glass phase of the Edwards-Anderson model. Models with correlated disorder have thus provided a new perspective on spin glasses and have proved fertile ground for highly nontrivial results on the spin-glass problem.

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge and exact solution of the $\pm J$ Edwards-Anderson model in a transverse field
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Mikhail Vasin
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.abstract: Using the Majorana representation of spin-1/2 operators, we study the $\pm J$ Edwards--Anderson model in a transverse field at $T=0$. We show that, in this representation, the quantity describing the coupling between neighboring spins commutes with the Hamiltonian and, unlike in the Kitaev model, is not subject to any Gauss law. The resulting $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge freedom allows the disorder in the signs of the exchange integrals to be eliminated by an exact gauge transformation, so that the spectrum of the system coincides with that of the model with uniform couplings. The resulting theory is quadratic in the Majorana fields. Computing the local Green's functions, we find that the Edwards--Anderson order parameter vanishes for $Δ>J\sqrt{Z}$ and equals $1/4$ for $Δ<J\sqrt{Z}$, which signals a second-order transition from a paramagnetic phase to a spin-glass ground state that is degenerate over spin configurations and replica symmetric at $T=0$.

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: Thermodynamics of Forgetting in a Bounded Hopfield Network
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Andrea Lepre
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.abstract: A memory that keeps learning must also forget. The Hopfield network does not: beyond a critical number of stored patterns it falls into a state of total confusion and retrieves none of them. Parisi showed in 1986 that bounding the synaptic strength cures this pathology, since the clipping of the couplings gradually erases the oldest memories and leaves room for the new ones. In this paper we provide a thermodynamic description of the resulting network, known as the Hopfield-Parisi model. Starting from the learning rule, we show that the network is equivalent to a Hopfield model whose patterns are weighted according to their age, superimposed on a Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass, both governed by the synaptic bound: a larger bound makes the memory longer, but also noisier. The theory of nonlinear networks developed in the eighties already provides, through the heuristic replica method, the equations that govern this model at any temperature, but to the best of our knowledge they have been solved only at zero temperature. We rederive them at the replica symmetric level through Guerra's interpolation and solve them at finite temperature, obtaining the phase diagram of the model together with its memory horizon, namely the largest age at which a pattern can still be retrieved. The solution shows that forgetting acts on the signal alone, the noise being the same for patterns of every age, and that the horizon is maximal at an intermediate bound which is essentially insensitive to temperature. Monte Carlo simulations of networks trained with the original learning rule support these predictions.

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: Parisi Energy before Parisi Geometry in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Maxime Dupont, Bhuvanesh Sundar
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.abstract: The fractured low-energy landscape of spin glasses presents a notorious barrier to optimization. While high-depth calculations indicate that the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can approach the Parisi ground-state energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass, how it does so remains elusive. Here, we treat the QAOA distribution as a statistical-physics object and probe its geometry directly in the thermodynamic limit. We draw two independent bitstrings from the same problem instance and couple them through their macroscopic similarity. We find that typical QAOA samples remain macroscopically uncorrelated, even as their sensitivity to this coupling grows with circuit depth $p$. By contrast, the low-energy tail shows a much stronger tendency to overlap and reveals a Parisi-like phase with the same critical behavior as the thermal spin-glass transition. The onset of this organization moves toward the typical output as the circuit deepens, consistent with the separation vanishing only as $p\to\infty$. Together, these findings suggest a route distinct from structure-exploiting classical algorithms and thermal sampling, one in which the QAOA approaches the Parisi energy before Parisi geometry becomes typical.

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: How Path Integral Diffusion Decides a Finite Spin Glass
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Michael Chertkov
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.abstract: When an AI diffusion-type generator samples a frustrated spin glass, which macroscopic alternatives does it decide first, and when? We study this for bridge-diffusion models of the Path Integral Diffusion (PID) type started from a point source. We show that every isotropic PID is a time-changed Gaussian stochastic localization, and conversely every signal-to-noise schedule is realized by a PID protocol. What a continuous-time generator decides therefore does not depend on the protocol, which only sets when and at what cost. We describe the generator's state by its partial commitments: the probabilities it assigns, at each moment, to nested classes of configurations fixed by the target. The partial commitments are martingales that move only along class contrasts. Their ensemble average gives the information about each level at an exact rate set by squared magnetization contrasts. In the balanced, effectively binary approximation, a split reaches half of its class information near γ=1.044/λ_P, where λ_P is the leading eigenvalue of the parent covariance. The theory is applied to Bethe-lattice and Sherrington--Kirkpatrick (SK) glasses with up to 24 spins. It is observed generically that a trajectory first shifts its weight to one of the two mirror halves of the zero-field measure and then to the glassy classes inside it. These classes appear near the glass transition, keep their identity on cooling and are absent in a ferromagnet on the same graphs. Sparse (Bethe) and dense (SK) glasses differ in how often and how strongly such classes exist, not in how trajectories commit to them. For a generator that takes finitely many steps, the protocol matters through the late, local stage rather than the macroscopic decisions. Sampled posteriors at N=32,64 and small trained denoisers show the same sequence.

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: Spin-glass order in a field requires magnetic-field chaos in XY gauge glasses for $d\leq 4$
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Manaka Okuyama, Masayuki Ohzeki, Hidetoshi Nishimori
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.abstract: The XY gauge-glass model is believed to exhibit a spin-glass phase in dimensions $d\geq 3$. In this paper, we prove that, in dimensions $d\leq 4$ and at any finite temperature, a magnetic field applied in a fixed direction, with amplitudes that fluctuate from site to site according to the Rayleigh distribution, must either induce magnetic-field chaos in the spin-glass phase or destroy spin-glass order altogether, whenever a spin-glass phase exists at zero field. In particular, if a spin-glass phase persists under such a field, as predicted by the replica-symmetry-breaking (RSB) picture, it must exhibit magnetic-field chaos. This conclusion follows from our proof that, for any fixed nonzero field strength, the disorder average of the squared overlap between equilibrium spin configurations at zero field and those at nonzero field vanishes in the thermodynamic limit. By gauge transformations, the overlap statistics are identical to the magnetization statistics of an XY gauge glass with correlated bond disorder in a Gaussian random field. Our proof combines this exact identity with quantitative estimates on the suppression of ferromagnetic order by random fields in continuous-spin systems, due to Dario, Harel, and Peled [Commun. Math. Phys. 405, 212 (2024)] and building on the work of Imry and Ma [Phys. Rev. Lett. 35, 1399 (1975)] and of Aizenman and Wehr [Phys. Rev. Lett. 62, 2503 (1989); Commun. Math. Phys. 130, 489 (1990)]. We extend these estimates to bond-dependent interactions. Although our result provides a rare rigorous constraint on the nature of spin-glass phases in finite-dimensional systems, it does not determine whether spin-glass order survives in a field, and therefore does not distinguish between the droplet and RSB pictures. The case of a strictly uniform field remains open.

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: Blanket theory for dense networks
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Simone Franchini
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.abstract: We show how Blanket theory provides a constructive method for calculating cavity functionals in dense spin networks. Building on the description through interfaces and magnetization shells, we develop the calculation from the low-temperature fluctuations around the ground state. In this regime, dilute defects reveal the mechanism of random energy model (REM) universality for linear energies, while their sharing and renewal across layers organize the energies and Gibbs weights into a hierarchy. Because the same configurations determine the covariances of the fresh cavity fields, this construction identifies the fields and weights with an Aizenman-Sims-Starr random overlap structure. The cavity contributions can then be evaluated through recursive fractional means, yielding an explicit free-energy functional parametrized by layer magnetizations and hierarchical exponents, with coefficients determined by the interaction variances and the network normalization. Under the stated moment and normalization conditions, comparison of pressures transfers the limiting mean pressure from the Gaussian representative to networks with independent centered non-Gaussian couplings having the same variances. We illustrate the method with the deterministic Curie-Weiss model, recover the Parisi functional for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, and derive the functionals for restricted and deep Boltzmann machines, including the full replica symmetry breaking (fullRSB) limit.

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: Ferroelastic domain wall driven glassy dynamics and photoresponse in a SrTiO 3 (111) two-dimensional electron gas
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Jyotirmay Maity, Manav Beniwal, Pranab Hazra, Sumit Tomar, Srimanta Middey

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: Disorder-driven emergence of spin glass states in ZnFe 2 O 4 particles
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: M Viswanathan, D Venkateswarlu, F. Stromberg, J. Landers, W. Keune, H. Wende, P. S. Anil Kumar

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: Quantum transport reveals spin-glass correlations in a two-dimensional network of TbPc 2 single-molecule magnets grafted on graphene.
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Nianjheng Wu, Jules Lefeuvre, Andrew Mayne, Stéphane Campidelli, Jérôme Lagoute, Cyril Chacon, Sophie Guéron, Richard Deblock, Hélène Bouchiat

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: Semiclassical picture of the Heisenberg spin glass in two dimensions
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Giacomo Bracci Testasecca, Jacopo Niedda, Aldo Coraggio, Roderich Moessner, Antonello Scardicchio

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: A Simple Approach to the Complexity of Mean Field Ising Spin Glasses
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Benjamin McKenna, Qiang Wu
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.abstract: The geometry of spherical spin glasses is relatively well understood, thanks in large part to the Kac-Rice formula. However, this formula does not directly apply to discrete spin systems, and much less is known mathematically about the geometry of Ising spin glasses. In this paper, we present a simple method for counting local optima and gapped states in a broad class of discrete spin glasses. To illustrate its scope, we compute the annealed complexities ("configurational entropies," in the physics language) of mixed Ising spin glasses with potentials, such as external fields, and of the Ghatak-Sherrington model. These computations recover several existing results in the mathematics and physics literature as special cases. We can also compute energy-constrained complexity, finding a critical energy threshold analogous to the spherical case, but for gapped states of pure Ising spin glasses. Finally, we use our method to establish a form of disorder persistence for gapped states, identifying a transition between $3$-spin and $4$-spin glasses.

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: Guerra Interpolation and Optimal Transport: Kantorovich Bounds, Brenier Maps and the Replicon
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Elena Agliari, Adriano Barra, Andrea Ladiana, Andrea Lepre, Diego Pallara
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.abstract: Since Guerra's work, mean-field spin glasses have been studied through Hamilton--Jacobi equations. Here, using the Curie--Weiss and the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick models as prototypical examples, we show that his celebrated interpolation method is itself an optimal transport computation. After a linear change of variables the finite-$N$ pressure becomes an action $u$ with $\partial_t u = -A/2$ and $\partial_x u = -B$, where $B^2 \le A$, so $u$ is a classical subsolution of $\partial_t u+\frac12(\partial_x u)^2 \le 0$. Integrating along a straight segment gives Guerra's sum rule, and dropping its remainder makes $u(0,\cdot)$ and $u(t,\cdot)$ an admissible pair for the dual Kantorovich problem with quadratic cost. For the Curie--Weiss model and $t > 0$, $T_t(y) = y-t\tanh y$ is an optimal transport map from every source with finite first moment if and only if $t \le 1$, and the Kantorovich potentials are the limiting pressures. For the replica-symmetric Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, the cavity map is injective on the physical half-line and the curvature of its Brenier potential is the longitudinal eigenvalue, which exceeds the replicon eigenvalue $Λ_{\mathrm{AT}}$: transport of Dirac masses does not detect the de Almeida--Thouless line. The replicon appears along the $\mathcal{W}_2$ geodesic that splits a Dirac mass into two atoms, as the second variation of a second-order surrogate of the two-atom Parisi functional. From a Dirac initial datum, Guerra's $K$-step bound takes Hopf--Lax form, and the Parisi formula becomes a Hopf--Lax formula over atomic measures. With a $\mathcal{W}_1$-Lipschitz bound for its initial datum, proved by comparing Cole--Hopf layers, we let $K\to\infty$ and recover at Dirac data the Hopf--Lax form of the Parisi formula due to Mourrat and to Mourrat and Panchenko, with a rate for equal-mass approximations.

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: From compressed- to stretched-exponential dynamics in metallic glasses
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Birte Riechers, Achraf Atila, Reza Rashidi, Fabian Westermeier, Michael Sprung, Robert Maaß
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.abstract: The microscopic dynamics of metallic glasses are fundamentally governed by their out-of-equilibrium state. In this study, we combine synchrotron x-ray photon correlation spectroscopy with atomistic simulations to track the evolution of structural dynamics from the out-of-equilibrium glassy solid into the metaequilibrium state. The experiments reveal a clear transition from compressed- to stretched-exponential dynamics driven by physical aging. In contrast, the simulations consistently exhibit stretched-exponential behavior across all tested conditions, including zero pressure and applied hydrostatic stress. Despite these qualitatively different initial responses, we demonstrate here that both experimental and computational approaches converge toward a common metaequilibrium stretched relaxation shape with β ≈ 0.8 . Further, in this regime both experiment and simulation exhibit de Gennes narrowing in the relaxation timescale and shape parameter, a behavior that emerges in the experiments even before the metaequilibrium state is reached. Ultimately, the absence of compressed-exponential dynamics in simulated quenched-in and pressurized states indicates that the experimental as-cast state possesses a distinct dynamical fingerprint whose exact structural origin continues to remain unresolved.

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: Zeroth persistent homology of ground-state correlations at clean and disordered quantum transitions
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Francisco Belchí, Nahuel Statuto
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.abstract: The antiferromagnetic Ising chain in transverse and longitudinal fields exhibits a continuous critical point, a mixed-order transition line and, with quenched disorder, an infinite-disorder fixed point and reentrant order. Using exact free-fermion solutions and the density-matrix renormalization group, we examine what the zeroth persistent homology of staggered ground-state correlations adds to conventional responses. Its barcode records the merge scales of the single-linkage hierarchy, and the maximum of its persistence-landscape velocity defines a threshold-free pseudocritical point. This point locates the clean critical point and the mixed-order line with an accuracy comparable to conventional responses. In the reentrant regime, the global velocity misplaces the entry, which is recovered only by restricting the filtration to the ordering scale, and none of the tested estimators locates the exit. A domain wall forced by the boundary conditions suppresses the disorder-averaged reentrant lobe. For individual disordered realizations, the labelled merge tree recovers most strong-disorder renormalization-group clusters, including noncontiguous ones missed by lattice-restricted hierarchies, with increasing agreement at stronger disorder. This information resides in the full correlation matrix, while zeroth homology provides a stable, threshold-free hierarchy.

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: From dynamic strain aging to Alessandro--Beatrice--Bertotti--Montorsi dynamics of propagating Portevin--Le Chatelier bands
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Tero Mäkinen, Mikko J. Alava
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.abstract: Type-A Portevin--Le Chatelier bands are propagating strain localizations whose velocity exhibits strong intermittent fluctuations. We derive a coarse-grained connection between the dynamic-strain-aging model of Hähner and Rizzi and the Alessandro--Beatrice--Bertotti--Montorsi (ABBM) mean-field model of avalanche dynamics. A propagating band is reduced to a single phase coordinate while retaining the elastic feedback of the tensile machine. This feedback generates the increasing drive and restoring terms of the ABBM description. A finite-time adjoint calculation determines the stress mobility of the band and is checked independently by direct stress continuation. The mobility is approximately proportional to the hardening parameter, whereas the band speed scales approximately as its square root. Short-range heterogeneity in the plastic strain deposited by the band is converted by the global machine feedback into a Brownian effective force. The resulting reduction provides a microscopic route from dynamic strain aging to ABBM-like avalanche dynamics of propagating PLC bands.

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: Pressure-induced superconductivity in 2 H -TaS 2 with dilute magnetic Mn intercalation
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Xiangzhuo Xing, Na Zuo, Xiangyu Li, Jiajia Feng, Guanghao Liang, Xiaolei Yi, Yan Meng, Nan Zhou, Xin Chen, Xiaofeng Xu, Xuan Luo, Bin Chen, Yuping Sun, Xiaobing Liu

Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.title: Posterior alpha/beta oscillations reflect oculomotor dynamics underlying subsequent memory effects
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.authors: Xiongbo Wu, Tzvetan Popov, Tara Beilner, Nicholas Fearns, Christian Vollmar, Elisabeth Kaufmann, Jan Remi, Tobias Staudigl
Spin Glass & Disordered Magnetism.abstract: Neural activity and eye movements are well-established predictors of human memory performance. Successful memory formation is associated with reduced alpha/beta power and increased eye movements. However, their coupling and combined contribution to memory formation remain largely unknown. Across four experiments combining eye tracking with scalp or intracranial electroencephalography during free or constrained viewing, we identify the degree of visual exploration, rather than subsequent memory performance, as consistent modulator of posterior alpha/beta power. Going beyond correlations, manipulating eye movements dissociated alpha/beta power reductions from memory. Together with the finding that saccade parameters predicted alpha/beta dynamics, our results directly link posterior alpha/beta activity to the oculomotor system. Moreover, the accumulation of saccades over time accounted for reduced alpha/beta power, resembling the canonical post-stimulus alpha/beta pattern. Our work demonstrates that posterior alpha/beta activity strongly reflects eye movements, supporting alternative perspectives on alpha/beta subsequent memory effects and the general function of posterior alpha/beta activity.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Thermal Hall sign reversal from competing magnons and magnon pairs in pyrochlore spin-nematic magnets
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Tetsuya Sato, Emika Takata, Masahiro Sato
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: Bound magnon pairs are central to spin-nematic order, yet experimentally distinguishing them from single magnons remains challenging. We show that their Berry-curvature-driven heat transport provides a characteristic signature in the thermal Hall response. For a spin-$3/2$ pyrochlore antiferromagnet with ferromagnetic biquadratic exchange in the magnetic-field-induced fully polarized phase, we construct single-magnon bands together with magnon-pair bands, include the Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interaction, and evaluate their intrinsic thermal Hall conductivities. The lowest magnon and magnon-pair bands carry Berry curvatures of opposite sign. Because the gaps of the two quasiparticles respond differently to magnetic field, their competing contributions can drive both magnetic-field- and temperature-induced sign reversals of the thermal Hall conductivity. Estimates for chromium spinel oxides indicate that the effect can approach experimentally accessible magnitudes. We also find that the hybridization between the one- and two-magnon sectors induced by the DM interaction preserves this qualitative signature. These results suggest that a broad class of frustrated magnets with both magnons and magnon pairs provides a possible route to tuning the sign of the thermal Hall conductivity and probing bound magnon pairs through thermal transport experiments.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Flat-band driven bipolar anomalous Nernst effect towards volt-scale transverse thermoelectric conversion
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Haofu Wen, Xiaodong Guo, Xiaokang Xu, Peng Di, Xuebiao Ji, Ruoqi Wang, Shijun Yuan, Kunquan Hong, Qionghua Zhou, Qian Chen, Taishi Chen, Jinlan Wang
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: Unipolar anomalous Nernst thermopiles are critically plagued by metallic interconnects, which induce heavy Joule dissipation and compromise the module's packing density, ultimately capping voltage generation. Here, we circumvent these limitations by establishing an intrinsic bipolar anomalous Nernst effect (BANE) paradigm, enabling seamless series integration analogous to Seebeck n-p pairs without passive metallic bridges. Focusing on flat-band topological systems, through machine learning assisted screening across multiple target properties, we identified 249 BANE materials, exhibiting near-room-temperature polarity switching. Guided by this predictive framework, we experimentally realized this phenomenon in single crystals of the Weyl ferromagnet, Co$_2$TiGe. Strikingly, while its intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) remains rigorously temperature-invariant up to the Curie temperature, the anomalous Nernst signal undergoes a sharp polarity inversion across $T \approx 225$ K. First-principles calculations attribute this behavior to the interplay between flat bands and Weyl nodes, where thermal depopulation shifts the chemical potential across the band edge, inverting the sign of $\partial σ_{xy} / \partial ε$ via the Mott relation. This work opens an avenue toward compact, monolithic transverse thermopiles capable of volt-scale generation free from interfacial parasitic dissipation.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Orientation-Tunable Interfacial Thermal Conductance in Lateral MoSe2/MoS2 Heterostructures: A Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics Study
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Shirin Sabokdast, Pedram Mirchi, Ali Rajabpour
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: Managing heat flow across interfaces in lateral 2D transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) heterostructures is a key challenge for next-generation nanoelectronic and optoelectronic devices. To tackle this, we trained a deep learning interatomic potential (DLP) using DeePMD-kit on density functional theory (DFT) data, then paired it with non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) simulations to study interfacial thermal conductance (ITC) in lateral MoSe$_2$/MoS$_2$ heterostructures, considering both armchair and zigzag interface orientations. The potential we trained closely matches DFT energies, forces, and phonon dispersion relations, which confirms its reliability for thermal transport simulations. Examining cell lengths from 10 to 40 nm and extrapolating to infinite length, the armchair interface shows a higher ITC (473 MW/m$^2$K) than the zigzag interface (387 MW/m$^2$K), and the armchair interface remains higher at every length considered. Both increase further as temperature rises. At 300 K, the vibrational density of states shows greater phonon spectral overlap at the armchair interface than at the zigzag interface. Together, these results offer a solid machine-learning framework for studying heat transport in lateral TMD heterostructures, and identify interface orientation as an effective means of controlling heat dissipation at these junctions.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Orientation-Tunable Interfacial Thermal Conductance in Lateral MoSe₂/MoS₂ Heterostructures: A Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics Study
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Shirin Sabokdast, Pedram Mirchi, Ali Rajabpour
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: Managing heat flow across interfaces in lateral 2D transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) heterostructures is a key challenge for next-generation nanoelectronic and optoelectronic devices.To tackle this, we trained a deep learning interatomic potential (DLP) using DeePMD-kit on density functional theory (DFT) data, then paired it with non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) simulations to study interfacial thermal conductance (ITC) in lateral MoSe₂/MoS₂ heterostructures -looking specifically at both armchair and zigzag interface orientations. The potential we trained closely matches DFT energies, forces, and phonon dispersion relations, which confirms its reliability for thermal transport simulations. At room temperature, the armchair interface shows notably higher ITC (218 MW/m²•K) compared to the zigzag interface (188 MW/m²•K), and both increase further as temperature rises. Looking at the vibrational density of states, we found greater phonon spectral overlap at the armchair interface -this is what drives its better thermal transport performance. Together, these results offer a solid machine-learning framework for studying heat transport in lateral TMD heterostructures, and identify interface orientation as an effective means of controlling heat dissipation at these junctions.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Ternary-composition tuning of the anomalous Nernst effect in amorphous-like Gd–Co–Pt films
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Tomohiro Koizumi, Mojtaba Mohammadi, Hiroto Imaeda, Hiroyuki Awano, Kenji Tanabe
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: We report composition tuning of the anomalous Nernst effect in amorphous-like Gd–Co–Pt ternary films. Using the ternary alloy design introduces additional degrees of freedom for controlling the transverse thermoelectric response and thermal transport. Pt incorporation into Gd–Co films modifies the anomalous Nernst coefficient and induces a sign reversal of SANE, whereas Gd incorporation into Co–Pt films suppresses SANE but reduces thermal conductivity. Owing to the balance between transverse thermoelectric response and thermal transport, the heat-flux sensitivity reaches approximately 0.24 μm/A. Composition maps reveal that the magnitude and heat-flux sensitivity of the anomalous Nernst effect can be systematically tuned in the Gd–Co–Pt ternary composition space. These results demonstrate that ternary alloying provides a route toward partially decoupled control of transverse thermoelectric and thermal-transport properties beyond conventional binary-alloy optimization.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Low-temperature vibrational anomalies and thermal transport in polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon crystals
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: V. Sokolenko, A. I. Krivchikov, A. Jeżowski, V. Boiko, O. A. Korolyuk, D. Szewczyk
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: The boson peak is an excess of low-frequency vibrational states over the Debye prediction and is commonly associated with structural disorder. Similar heat-capacity anomalies also occur in ordered molecular crystals, but their dependence on molecular structure and their relation to heat transport remain incompletely understood. Here we compare six polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) crystals -- pyrene, tetracene, perylene, pentacene, coronene and corannulene -- using low-temperature heat capacity, low-frequency Raman spectroscopy and thermal conductivity measurements. For compounds with well-resolved maxima, the rising side of the heat-capacity excess is consistent with a raised-cosine scaling function with no adjustable shape parameter, whereas the decay is compound-dependent. The number and widths of resolved lattice-mode Raman bands vary across the series, although their assignment is constrained by spectral background and resolution. Thermal conductivity ranges from crystal-like to glass-like behaviour. An activated contribution is resolved in the five planar compounds but is not required to describe the corannulene data within the sensitivity of the present measurements. These results show that glass-like thermal and vibrational signatures are not unique to amorphous materials and are associated with differences in molecular structure and crystal packing; they do not, by themselves, isolate packing as the sole causal variable.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Structure and Thermal Conductivity of Epoxy-Graphene Oxide Composites from 4.5 to 300 K
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: A. Jeżowski, A. I. Krivchikov, O. A. Korolyuk, V. V. Sagan, Y. V. Horbatenko, S. V. Cherednychenko, D. Szewczyk
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: The microscopic mechanisms of heat transport in structurally disordered polymer-carbon composites remain incompletely understood, particularly over the broad temperature range extending from cryogenic to ambient conditions. Here, we investigate the relationship between structural organization and thermal transport in epoxy-graphene oxide (GO) composites with nominal GO contents of 0.25-10 wt.% relative to the resin (0.21-6.1 wt.% of the total composite mass). X-ray diffraction reveals predominantly amorphous scattering without a detectable GO(001) reflection, suggesting substantial suppression of ordered GO stacking within the cured epoxy matrix. Raman spectroscopy confirms the increasing contribution of the carbon phase while revealing no pronounced changes in the characteristic vibrational bands of the epoxy network. Thermal-conductivity measurements (4.5-300 K) demonstrate that GO incorporation modifies the temperature dependence of heat transport rather than producing a simple conductivity enhancement. The experimental data are described by a phenomenological multichannel model comprising a temperature-independent plateau term and two or three effective Arrhenius-type contributions characterized by distinct temperature scales ranging from a few to several hundred kelvin. The low-temperature conductivity plateau observed at lower GO concentrations is no longer resolved in GO-6 and GO-10, indicating a qualitative change in the temperature dependence of heat transport. These results establish a correlation between structural organization and the redistribution of effective thermal-transport contributions in epoxy-GO composites, providing an experimental basis for further microscopic interpretation within the framework of unified vibrational thermal-transport theory.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: A Monte Carlo study of thermal conductivity in black phosphorene
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: L. O. Vilyaev, D. V. Zavyalov, V. I. Konchenkov
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: In this work the electronic thermal conductivity of black phosphorene is studied. Using the Monte Carlo method together with the Green-Kubo relations, a statistical modelling of the motion and scattering of electrons on acoustic and optical phonons is performed to estimate the electronic thermal conductivity. The scattering probability is expressed analytically. The obtained results show a pronounced anisotropy of the thermal conductivity: the thermal conductivity values along the armchair direction are an order of magnitude larger than those along the zigzag direction, in agreement with the experimental data for related materials. In addition, the modelling allowed a more rigorous justification of some results of previous theoretical works on the anisotropic thermal conductivity of black phosphorene.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Thermal conductivity of α-Ga2O3 thin films
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Gustavo A. Alvarez, Jacob Steele, Jonathan P. McCandless, Yuichi Oshima, Zhuoqun Wen, Amelia Schaeffer, Chen Li, Elaheh Ahmadi, Huili Grace Xing, Debdeep Jena, Darrell G. Schlom, Zhiting Tian
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: Increasing attention is focused on moving beyond Si for next-generation optoelectronics, communication systems, and high-power electronics. The corundum polymorph α-Ga2O3, with its ultrawide bandgap (∼5.3 eV), is a promising candidate. Using frequency-domain thermoreflectance, we experimentally measure the cross-plane thermal conductivity (k⊥) of α-Ga2O3 films grown on α-Al2O3 by multiple epitaxy methods. We report the first thickness-dependent k⊥ values for these films and obtain a maximum k⊥ of 9.5 ± 2.3 W/m-K for thicknesses under 200 nm. These results establish a critical experimental benchmark and reveal pronounced size-dependent thermal transport in α-Ga2O3, with important implications for thermal management in thin-film, high-power devices.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Lower Bound of Thermal Conductivity in Graphene
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Yan Gao, Yafei Ding, Hongbin Xu, Zhaoxuan Tang, Fuqing Duan, Wenmei Luo, Zhensheng Zhang, Xiaohang Zhang, Guimei Zhu, Yahui Xue, Baowen Li
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: The intrinsic thermal conductivity ($κ$) of graphene remains highly controversial because of physical and metrological complexities. Although the thermal bridge method enables reliable measurements, sample fabrication remains challenging. Here, we develop a highly efficient patterning and transfer technique to systematically fabricate and characterize suspended bilayer graphene (BLG) thermal bridges with lengths of 1-30 $μ$m. Suspended BLG with unavoidable polymer residues exhibits length-independent thermal conductivity of approximately 570 W/(m K) at room temperature, remaining nearly constant from 250 to 350 K and robust to rigorous surface cleaning and amorphous silicon nitride substrates. Homogeneous non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (HNEMD) simulations show that amorphous carbon coverage of only approximately 0.01 monolayer is sufficient to suppress out-of-plane flexural acoustic (ZA) phonons. These findings challenge the prevailing view that rigid substrates suppress ZA phonons more strongly than surface contamination and identify a robust lower bound of $κ$ governed by amorphous surface scattering. This lower bound reflects heat conduction in graphene under realistic device conditions and provides a reference for fundamental phonon transport studies and the integration of graphene into thermal management applications in electronic devices and chips.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Universal Multichannel Coherence-Mediated Thermal Transport in Carbon Allotropes: Experimental Evidence and Scaling Laws
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: A. Jeżowski, A. I. Krivchikov, O. A. Korolyuk, V. V. Sagan, Y. V. Horbatenko, S. V. Cherednychenko, A. V. Dolbin, N. A. Vinnikov, O. Bezkrovnyi, D. Szewczyk
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: Understanding thermal transport in structurally disordered carbon materials remains a fundamental challenge because conventional models based on a single coherence contribution cannot accurately describe heat conduction over a broad temperature range. In this work, the thermal conductivity of graphene oxide (GO), thermally reduced graphene oxide (trGO), GO-hydrated fullerene composites (GO-HyFn), expanded graphite (EG), and EG-multiwalled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) composites was measured between 4.5 and 300 K. Despite substantial differences in density, porosity, graphitic ordering, and microstructure, all materials exhibit glass-like temperature dependence of thermal conductivity. The experimental results demonstrate that the conventional two-channel model, comprising a Peierls contribution and a single thermally activated coherence term, systematically fails to reproduce the observed temperature dependence. To resolve this discrepancy, we propose a generalized multichannel phenomenological model in which the coherence contribution consists of up to three Arrhenius-type channels with distinct activation energies. Depending on the structural state, two or three coherence channels are required to accurately describe the thermal conductivity. A key finding is the reproducible hierarchy of activation energies across diverse carbon allotropes, following approximately (E2 ~ 4E1 and E3 ~ (12-25)E1). While the channel amplitudes increase with material density, the activation energies remain nearly invariant, indicating universal vibrational energy scales. The proposed framework also consistently describes published data for other disordered carbon materials. These results provide experimental evidence for multichannel coherence-mediated heat transport and establish a unified phenomenological bridge between structural hierarchy with thermal transport in disordered carbon solids.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Pressure-enhanced thermoelectric transport in layered Bi2Se3 through band structure optimization
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Yuqi Gao, Dianzhen Wang, Shijie Hu, Dan Han, Jing Zou, Qiang Tao, Lu Wang, Yan Li, Pinwen Zhu
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: In general, the pressure-optimized thermoelectric transport of 2D layered materials is attributed to strengthened interlayer interactions that reduce the bandgap. However, this also introduces a pronounced bipolar effect and band edge sharpening, thereby limiting thermoelectric performance. In this study, taking layered Bi2Se3 as an example, we observed the onset temperature of the bipolar effect from approximately 387 K at 1 GPa to 459 K at 5 GPa. First-principles calculations show that pressure-induced interlayer compression modifies the coupling between band edge pz orbitals, leading to an increase in the bandgap from 0.21 eV at ambient pressure to 0.292 eV at 5 GPa. This suppresses the bipolar effect and is accompanied by conduction band flattening, which increases the density-of-states effective mass and enhances the Seebeck coefficient. Additionally, the native Se vacancies in Bi2Se3 introduce donor levels, and pressure-induced modulation of these donor levels promotes carrier thermally excited, leading to an increased carrier concentration. This not only suppresses the bipolar effect but also compensates for the reduction in carrier concentration caused by the pressure-widened bandgap, maintaining high electrical conductivity, consequently resulting in a record-high power factor of 2663 μW·m−1·K−2 at 5 GPa, 580 K, and an estimated maximum ZT value of 0.804 at 5 GPa, 580 K. This study provides insights into pressure-induced band structure optimization for enhanced thermoelectric performance under high pressure.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Dynamic Scaling and Aging in Hydrodynamic Coarsening of Vapor Bubbles in a Lennard-Jones Fluid
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Sutapa Roy
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: We investigate the coarsening and aging dynamics of vapor bubbles during liquid-vapor phase separation in a three-dimensional single-component Lennard-Jones fluid using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. Following a temperature quench from a homogeneous high-temperature state into the two-phase coexistence region, vapor bubbles nucleate and grow in the liquid background. The characteristic bubble size follows a power-law growth, $\ell(t)\sim t^α$, with a growth exponent $α\simeq 2/3$, characteristic of inertial hydrodynamic coarsening. We also investigate the two-time autocorrelation function $C_{ag}(t,t_w)$ which follows waiting-time dependent relaxation, revealing aging. Furthermore, data at different waiting times collapse onto a scaling function when plotted as a function of the length ratio $\ell(t)/\ell(t_w)$, demonstrating dynamical scaling during aging. The corresponding scaling function exhibits an algebraic decay with an exponent $λ\simeq 3$. Interestingly, bubble and droplet growth exhibit distinctly different domain-growth and aging exponents despite both being disconnected morphologies.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Superconducting decoherence and thermal quenching of the Josephson diode effect in low-dimensional Josephson systems
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: F. Yang, C. Y. Dong, Joshua A. Robinson, L. Q. Chen

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Anti-Kibble-Zurek behavior driven by dichotomous Markov noise in a quantum Ising chain: Generalized stochastic resonance in the defect density
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Mingwei Yang, Peng Li
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: The anti-Kibble-Zurek behavior may arise under noise, adding a noise-induced contribution to the defect density beyond the conventional Kibble-Zurek term. Most investigations of such behavior have so far been restricted to Gaussian noise. For Gaussian colored noise (GCN), the power spectrum dictates a monotonic variation of this term with the correlation time. Here, we focus on dichotomous Markov noise (DMN), a prototypical non-Gaussian colored noise, in the quantum Ising chain. We show that the noise-induced defect density, taken as the response function, exhibits generalized stochastic resonance: it is nonmonotonic in the correlation time, growing in the fast-noise regime and decreasing in the slow-noise regime. This resonance stems from the anomalous AKZ behavior in the slow-noise regime, where the DMN-induced trend is nonmonotonic, in contrast to the monotonic GCN case. The underlying mechanism lies in the sparse realizations of DMN in the slow-noise regime, a feature not captured by the power spectrum. Our work thereby reveals a fundamental distinction between Gaussian and non-Gaussian noises in the nonequilibrium critical quench dynamics of the quantum Ising chain.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Boosting thermoelectric performance of hydrothermal SnSe2 via Br doping-induced high carrier concentration and low thermal conductivity
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Chunlu Wu, Xinxin Wang, Zhuoming Xu, Ning Chen, Min Zhang, Zi-long Zhang, Yue-Xing Chen, Zhuang-Hao Zheng
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: Anion-site doping represents a potent approach to tailor the electronic structure and transport properties of SnSe2. Herein, Br-doped SnSe2 bulk materials were successfully fabricated through a hydrothermal–annealing–sintering route, and the thermoelectric transport mechanisms were systematically investigated. Due to the valence electron discrepancy between Br and Se, the incorporation of Br into the matrix acts as a high-efficiency donor, triggering a degenerate semiconductor behavior. Consequently, the carrier concentration reached 2.38 × 1020 cm−3. Crucially, Br doping facilitates the microstructural texturing alignment during the consolidation process, thereby mitigating grain boundary potentials. This synergistic effect significantly boosts electrical conductivity, yielding a room-temperature power factor of 5.2 μW cm−1 K−2. Furthermore, the intensified point defect phonon scattering induced by Br substitution outweighs the weakened boundary scattering from grain growth, thereby suppressing the κ. As a result, a maximum ZT value of 0.47 is achieved in SnSe1.87Br0.13 at 773 K, which stands as a highly competitive performance among hydrothermally processed SnSe2. This work provides deep insights into the transport optimization of layered chalcogenides for green energy applications.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Four-phonon scattering suppresses low-temperature anomalous lattice thermal conductivity and enhances thermoelectric performance in layered X CuSe ( X = K , Rb )
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Jiawei Cui, Yinchang Zhao, Jun Ni, Zhenhong Dai

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Real-Space Theory of Nonequilibrium Orbital Magnetization in Inhomogeneous Solids
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: João M. Alendouro Pinho, Henrique P. Veiga, Alessandro Veneri, Daniel Passos, Ivo Souza, Bruno Amorim, João M. Viana Parente Lopes, Aires Ferreira
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: We put forward a real-space linear-response theory of orbital magnetization induced by a dc electric field in bulk materials lacking translation invariance. Starting from the current response to a slowly varying electromagnetic field, we show that the linear-in-wavevector conductivity tensor of non-interacting electrons in terms of single-particle Green's functions and the velocity and position operators. This provides a gauge-invariant real-space formulation of the long-wavelength non-equilibrium orbital magnetization of both perfect crystals and disordered systems. In the translationally invariant limit, the formalism recovers the established Bloch picture of orbital magneto-electric effects. We implement the formalism using large-scale Chebyshev expansions and illustrate its capabilities on a Haldane model in the presence of spatially uncorrelated disorder.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Angular dependence of the low-temperature skyrmion state in Cu$_2$OSeO$_3$
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Christian Oberleitner, Andreas Bauer, Lukas Heindl, Lin Chen, Aisha Aqeel, Christian H. Back, Hans Huebl, Christian Pfleiderer
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: In the cubic chiral magnet Cu$_2$OSeO$_3$, a low-temperature skyrmion state (LTS) and a metastable tilted conical state emerge for magnetic field along $\langle 100\rangle$, both stabilized by magnetocrystalline anisotropies. We report how these states evolve when the magnetic field is rotated from $\langle 100\rangle$ via $\langle 111\rangle$ to $\langle 110\rangle$. Measurements of the magnetization and the AC susceptibility are combined with broadband microwave spectroscopy on the same cuboid sample at 5\,K. In the microwave spectra, the characteristic gigahertz excitations, notably the counterclockwise gyration mode of the skyrmions, provide a direct indicator of the character of the magnetic states and a qualitative measure of their volume fractions. Both techniques consistently show that signatures of the LTS decrease in strength under rotation and are observed only for field directions within ${\sim}20^{\circ}$ of $\langle 100\rangle$. In this range, the field values at which the skyrmions unwind remain essentially unchanged. In contrast, signatures of the tilted conical state persist up to ${\sim}40^{\circ}$, beyond which the conventional sequence of helical, conical, and field-polarized states is recovered. Thus, the tilted conical state, while being a prerequisite for the nucleation of the LTS under field sweeps, is not sufficient for its formation.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: The often overlooked role of sound in liquid thermal transport
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Kamran Behnia
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: Formulated a hundred years ago, the Bridgman formula for thermal conductivity of liquids postulates a proportionality between sound velocity and thermal conductivity. This designates phonons as heat carriers in a liquid. Its empirical success has been under-appreciated and its conceptual implications overlooked. Here, we review its origin, its links to hydrodynamic Euler equations and to the fundamental paradox surrounding the parabolic heat equation and its fate across the quantum–classical crossover.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Measurement of Magnonic Quantum Geometry
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: S. Kim, M. Stone, S. E. Nagler, A. D. Christianson, Jiabin Yu, S. Okamoto, H. Miao
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: Quantum geometry plays a fundamental role in macroscopic quantum phenomena, including quantum Hall effects and flat-band superconductivity. However, since quantum geometry is encoded in wavefunctions rather than energy spectra, direct experimental characterization remains a formidable challenge. This challenge is particularly acute for quasiparticles in quantum materials, whose wavefunctions are generally inferred from effective low-energy models rather than measured directly. Here, we establish an experimental framework for characterizing the quantum geometry of magnons, a ubiquitous Bosonic quasiparticle of magnetically ordered states. We show that the inelastic neutron scattering (INS) cross-section measures geometric parameters of the spinor wavefunctions of ferromagnets. By tracking the energy- and momentum-dependent INS intensity, we extract the quantum geometric tensor without requiring detailed knowledge of microscopic spin-spin interactions. Our results establish magnons as an ideal arena for experimentally probing quantum geometry and open new avenues for exploring geometry-driven magnon transport and quantum Fisher information in magnetic materials.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Directed Domain Wall Motion by Radio-Frequency Currents
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Lukas Fischer, Rouven Dreyer, Simon Arnold, Jae-Chun Jeon, Georg Woltersdorf, Stuart S. P. Parkin
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: Magnetic domain walls (DWs) are central to emerging spintronic technologies for memory, logic and neuromorphic computing, where their controlled displacement is a key functionality. While current-induced DW motion driven by spin-orbit torques is well established under direct currents, it remains unclear how radio-frequency (RF) currents couple to DWs and whether they can generate directed motion under a symmetric periodic drive. Here we show that RF currents drive DW oscillations, which can be rectified into directed motion through symmetry breaking.
