Polarized Neutron Reflectometry.title: Effects of probe size, shape, and probe-surface interactions in imaging multilayer island growth, coalescence, and formation of a smooth film
Polarized Neutron Reflectometry.authors: Ismael S. S. Carrasco, Tiago J. Oliveira, Fábio D. A. Aarão Reis
Polarized Neutron Reflectometry.abstract: Recent studies of deposition onto weakly interacting substrates have revealed multilayer island growth, followed by smooth-film formation upon island coalescence. However, for C60 films, the roughness peak measured by atomic force microscopy (AFM) was significantly lower than that obtained by X-ray reflectometry (XRR), suggesting tip-sample convolution effects. We investigate this problem using kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulations of such films and models of probe-surface interactions for AFM imaging modes. To model the non-contact mode, surface profiles are transformed by averaging heights over regions matching the probe-tip width. A roughness peak remains if the probe width L is smaller than the average island distance, but its height decreases with L and its position is slightly displaced. In the contact-mode model with cylindrical probes and hard-core interactions, the peak also decreases and shifts significantly to smaller thicknesses, indicating apparently faster island coalescence. Thus, SPM images under these conditions may underestimate film-thickness nonuniformity in deposits with coalescing islands. Instead, models of sharp pyramidal or conical probes with hard-core interactions produce deviations in the roughness peaks only for large L, although such sharp tips are difficult to realize experimentally. A geometric model of cuboid island growth and coalescence quantitatively confirms the effects of contact modes and probe shapes observed in the simulations. The results suggest that post-growth processes, such as island coarsening and dewetting, may have occurred in the recently studied C60 film between the XRR and AFM measurements.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Vestiges of magnon fractionalization in the quasi-two-dimensional quantum magnet rouaite Cu$_2$(NO$_3$)(OH)$_3$ with alternating ferro- and antiferromagnetic $S=\frac{1}{2}$ chains
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Darren C. Peets, Satoshi Nishimoto, Denys Y. Kononenko, Oleg Janson, Aswathi Mannathanath Chakkingal, Anton A. Kulbakov, Kaushick K. Parui, Harald O. Jeschke, Ellen Häußler, James P. Tellam, J. Ross Stewart, Dmytro S. Inosov
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: Ferro- and antiferromagnetic quantum spin chains host qualitatively distinct elementary excitations --- magnons ($S=1$, bosonic quasiparticles) and spinons ($S=\frac{1}{2}$, fractionalized quasiparticles), respectively. Weakly coupled networks of both chain types therefore provide an ideal platform for exploring spinon-magnon coupling and the hybridization of sharp magnon modes with spinon continua. Here we investigate the spin-excitation spectrum of the frustrated quantum magnet rouaite, Cu$_2$(NO$_3$)(OH)$_3$ --- a model realization of weakly coupled ferro- and antiferromagnetic Cu$^{2+}$ spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ chains. The frustrated interchain interactions, while weaker than the dominant intrachain exchange, are sufficient to stabilize a long-range-ordered state that is not reproduced by classical calculations. Neutron spectroscopy reveals a spectrum of well-defined spin waves associated with both types of chains, with clear signatures of hybridization but no observable spinon continuum. Certain magnon branches resulting from this hybridization exhibit substantial broadening near the zone center. We attribute this to vestiges of spinon fractionalization persisting partway through the dimensional crossover from isolated quantum spin chains to a 2D network of frustrated spins.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Robust Antiferromagnetic Ordering above 500 K in a Family of Bilayer van der Waals Materials
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Tengda Rong, Linxin Wu, Xingke Fu, Anqi Huang, Feiran Shen, Zixian Dong, Jianwei Huang, Hao Li, Benyuan Cheng, Lunhua He, Long Jiang, Kun Cao, Zhen Chen, Meng Wang, Xiang Chen
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: Stabilizing magnetic order above room temperature in layered materials is highly desirable for low-dimensional spintronics applications. However, realizing room-temperature antiferromagnetism in layered magnets remains challenging. Here, we present a layered semiconducting oxyhalide material family, Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$X$_2$ ($X$ = F, Cl, Br), which exhibits robust high-temperature antiferromagnetic ordering. The two-dimensional nature and scalability of this system are demonstrated by atomically resolving the van der Waals gap of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$Br$_2$ and synthesizing centimeter-scale single crystals of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$Cl$_2$. Temperature-dependent neutron scattering and magnetization measurements determine their G-type magnetic structure and transition temperature. Remarkably, the Néel temperature of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$F$_2$ ($\sim$580 K) is the highest among all reported layered antiferromagnets. Density functional theory calculations demonstrate that strong nearest-neighbor superexchange interactions along both out-of-plane and in-plane directions, particularly the magnetic couplings along lattice $c$ direction within the bilayer motif, are primarily responsible for the high Néel temperatures in Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$X$_2$. In contrast, inter-bilayer spin couplings are negligibly weak, without much influence on the stabilization of the antiferromagnetic order. Therefore, theoretical calculations predict that this robust antiferromagnetic order could persist or even strengthens at room-temperature even at the monolayer limit. Our results highlight iron-based layered oxyhalides as a promising platform for exploring beyond-room-temperature antiferromagnetism in the two-dimensional limit, holding immense potential in areas like information storage and spin-based devices.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Odd-Parity Magnons in the Haldane-Hubbard Model from Topological Exciton Condensation
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Rintaro Eto, Johannes Knolle
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: Collective excitations in condensed matter can carry nontrivial topology and provide information about quantum phases beyond their ground-state properties. At the same time, the recent emergence of altermagnetism and related nonrelativistic spin-split electronic states raises the question of how unconventional magnetic symmetry is encoded in their collective excitations. Here, we uncover a continuous evolution from topological excitons to odd-parity magnons across an interaction-driven magnetic transition in the paradigmatic Haldane-Hubbard model. In the paramagnetic phase, our newly found sharp topological excitons soften and condense into a collinear Néel state, where they evolve into Goldstone magnons displaying characteristic f -wave spin splitting. The topology of these collective modes is tied to the underlying electronic topology, such that an electron bandgap closing enforces a magnon bandgap closing, changing the magnon topology. Our results establish a direct connection between topological collective excitations and nonrelativistic odd-parity spin splittings, with potential realizations in Floquet-driven materials and cold atomic gases.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Excitonic magnetism and competing valence bond solid instabilities in $d^4$ ruthenium compounds
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Aleksandra Krajewska, Tomohiro Takayama, Hidenori Takagi
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: Spin-orbit entangled $d^4$ Mott insulators serve as a rich playground for unconventional magnetism and competing quantum electronic ground states. Intra-ionic spin-orbit coupling $λ_{\rm{SOC}}$ generates a non-magnetic $J_{\rm{eff}} = 0$ singlet ground state separated from an excited $J_{\rm{eff}} = 1$ triplet. The effective intra-atomic gap $Δ_{\rm{eff}}$ between the ground state and lowest excited state is determined by $λ_{\rm{SOC}}$ and non-cubic crystal field $Δ_{\rm{cf}}$. The intersite magnetic exchange $J_{\rm{ex}}$ induces dispersion of the excited $J_{\rm{eff}} = 1$ triplet. When the triplet bandwidth $W_{\rm{t}}$ overcomes $Δ_{\rm{eff}}$, the system undergoes long-range magnetic ordering which is viewed as a condensation of spin-orbit excitons and called excitonic magnetism. In this review, we systematically survey representative $d^4$ ruthenium compounds across four distinct structural connectivities of Ru-ligand octahedra, from K$_2$RuCl$_6$ with isolated octahedra, corner-sharing perovskite Ca$_2$RuO$_4$, edge-sharing honeycombs, to corner-sharing pyrochlores, and map them onto a conceptual parameter axis of $W_{\rm{t}} / Δ_{\rm{eff}}$. We demonstrate that $d^4$ ruthenium compounds not only represent evolution from a $J_{\rm{eff}} = 0$ Mott state to excitonic magnetism but encompass a broader competition of diverse electronic phases arising from spin-orbit coupling, exchange interactions, electron hopping, crystal field and bond covalency inhabiting similar energy scales. Near excitonic quantum critical point, where $W_{\rm{t}} \sim Δ_{\rm{eff}}$, lattice geometry and chemical bonds of constituent atoms play a decisive role in selecting the electronic ground state, frequently driving valence bond solid formation that pre-empts excitonic quantum criticality.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Finite-time quenches across first-, second-, and infinite-order transitions in XXZ spin chains
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Luiz Felipe Santos Dittberner, Luigi Berber, Maria C. O. Aguiar, Krissia Zawadzki, Helena Bragança
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: We investigate how equilibrium quantum phase transitions manifest themselves in small systems driven out of equilibrium by quantum quenches. We consider linear ramps of the anisotropy in spin-1/2 and spin-1 XXZ chains, which host transitions of first, second, and infinite (Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless, BKT) order. We consider system sizes available in current quantum simulators and investigate how the order of the transition, the symmetries, and the ramp duration affect the decomposition of the time-evolved state into the instantaneous eigenbasis. The order of the transition determines the dynamics: across the BKT transition, moderately slow ramps already keep the system close to its ground state, corresponding to an adiabatic evolution, whereas for the second-order Haldane-Néel transition a ramp roughly three times slower is required to reach the same regime. Across the first-order transition, since the dynamics conserves the magnetization of the initial state, we observe the formation of ferromagnetic domains, separated by a single domain wall for slow ramps and by multiple walls for faster ones. Interestingly, shortly after the transition, the state evolves as a coherent beating between domain-wall states, a behavior captured by the recently proposed quantum-state texture.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Bridging Gaps with Tensor Networks: From the Haldane Gap and Beyond
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Sirui Lu
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: Proofs generated by large language models are often difficult to understand, generalize, or formalize directly. Here we verify, digest, and formalize OpenAI's computer-assisted proof of a uniform gap in the periodic spin-1 Heisenberg chain using tensor-network diagrams and Lean 4. Reading the partition-function network along space and imaginary time shows how finite-ring bounds propagate across doubled lengths and inverse temperatures to all longer even rings, sharpening the spin-1 bound from the same finite inputs by a factor of 19 to $Δ_L > 0.0729$ for all even $L \geq 36$. We identify reflection positivity as the general condition behind the proof and certify uniform gaps in seven additional spin chains and ladders. More broadly, digesting machine-generated proofs into transparent physical mechanisms yields sharper bounds, broader theorems, and reusable formal verifications.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Spin supersolid in triangular lattice easy-axis spin-1/2 antiferromagnet: a fermionic parton perspective
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Meng Zeng, Roderich Moessner, Shu Zhang
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: We study the supersolid order of the spin-1/2 easy-axis XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice using a fermionic parton mean-field theory built on the $π$-flux Dirac spin liquid, with the mean-field order generated by an on-site spinon interaction term and nearest-neighbor (anisotropic) spin couplings. The collective modes are obtained using the random-phase approximation (RPA). In a finite parameter region, we find the Y state as a self-consistent solution, together with the competing Y' state, which is a $90^\circ$-rotated Y state inside the order plane. The mean-field energy favors Y', even though the two states are exactly degenerate in the classical limit. However, the Y state can become lower in energy when higher-order corrections due to the fluctuations of the collective modes are considered. The Y state can also be stabilized on the mean-field level by applying small external fields, which we do in two different ways: moment-aligned local field and uniform field along the easy axis. In both cases, the RPA calculation for the stabilized Y state gives a roton minimum at the $M$ point in the excitation spectrum. A gapped pseudo-Goldstone mode above the gapless Goldstone mode is obtained as well, which has also been observed experimentally. Furthermore, we investigate the effects of tuning the spinon interaction strength and the anisotropy in spin couplings in our phenomenological model. Comparison with the recent numerical and experimental results is also discussed.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: What Hall Measures in Strongly Correlated Metals
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Emily Z. Zhang, Thomas P. Devereaux
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: The Hall effect provides a sensitive probe of electronic correlations in strongly interacting metals, yet its microscopic interpretation beyond quasiparticle transport remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a Liouvillian formulation of the Hall conductivity that organizes the response into different classes of flux-sensitive many-body interference operators. Using a Schrieffer-Wolff transformation of the Hubbard model, we identify how projected charge motion and virtual hopping processes contribute to oriented trajectories enclosing magnetic flux. A high-temperature expansion reveals a hierarchy of inverse-temperature contributions associated with these interference processes. This framework provides a possible microscopic interpretation of the integer power laws previously observed in determinant quantum Monte Carlo calculations, which emerge at temperatures below the regime where the expansion is formally controlled. Our results highlight the sensitivity of Hall transport to coherent many-body dynamics and establish a connection between lattice geometry, electronic correlations, and transverse charge response.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Dimensional Crossover and Correlated Spin Dynamics in the Chain-Like van der Waals Antiferromagnet AgCrP$_2$S$_6$
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: C. S. Saramgi, Y. Shemerliuk, S. Selter, S. Aswartham, B. Buechner, H. -J. Grafe, K. M. Ranjith
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: We report a comprehensive investigation of the magnetic properties and spin dynamics of the chain-like van der Waals antiferromagnet AgCrP$_2$S$_6$ using magnetization, magnetic susceptibility, and $^{31}$P nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). The magnetic susceptibility exhibits a broad maximum near 250 K, characteristic of strong short-range antiferromagnetic correlations in a low-dimensional system. A classical Fisher-chain analysis gives an effective intrachain exchange scale $J/k_B\approx 140$ K, while a quantum $S=3/2$ nearest-neighbor-chain calculation yields $J/k_B\approx 114$ K. A constrained AF-FM zig-zag-chain calculation is also compatible with the susceptibility, supporting a dominant quasi one dimensional antiferromagnetic exchange scale of order 100 K. $^{31}$P NMR measurements provide microscopic insight into both static and dynamic spin correlations. The $K-χ$ relation displays two distinct linear regimes separated near $T^\ast\approx 250$ K, with different slopes indicating a change in the effective transferred hyperfine couplings. Below $T_{N}$, the relaxation follows $1/T_1\propto T^5$, consistent with magnon-mediated relaxation in the ordered state. The temperature dependence of the internal hyperfine field yields a critical exponent $β\approx 0.36$, consistent with three-dimensional universality. Together, these results establish AgCrP$_2$S$_6$ as a quasi-one-dimensional $S=3/2$ antiferromagnet embedded in a layered van der Waals host, in which local probes directly resolve the crossover from correlated intrachain spin dynamics to anisotropic three-dimensional magnetic order. More broadly, AgCrP$_2$S$_6$ provides a useful van der Waals platform for studying dimensional crossover, correlated spin dynamics, and hyperfine-coupling evolution in low-dimensional antiferromagnets.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Field-induced magnetic quantum phase transitions in a bilayer triangular lattice antiferromagnet K$_2$Co$_2$(HPO$_3$)$_2$(C$_2$O$_4$)(H$_2$O)$_2$
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Yiqiu Liu, Chengcheng Yin, Xinyu Shi, Xiaohui Bo, Kefan Du, Zhanlong Wu, Rui Bian, Shuo Li, Jun Luo, Jie Yang, Yanhong Wang, Weiqiang Yu, Rui Zhou, Jinshan Zhang, Yi Cui, Hongcheng Lu
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: We present a $^{31}$P nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) study on the spin-$1/2$ bilayer triangular-lattice antiferromagnet K$_2$Co$_2$(HPO$_3$)$_2$(C$_2$O$_4$)(H$_2$O)$_2$. Measurements were performed at temperatures down to 0.06 K and magnetic fields up to 26 T. In the field range of 0.5 T to 4 T, the low-temperature spin-lattice relaxation rate $1/T_1$ exhibits a peak, signaling the onset of a magnetically ordered state. Within this ordered phase, $1/T_1$ shows gapless behavior, suggesting a spin supersolid phase. This ordering is suppressed around 4 T. Between 6 T and 18 T, clear splittings of the NMR spectra are observed, indicating the emergence of a second ordered magnetic phase. The field derivative of the low-temperature Knight shift $K_{\rm n}$ reveals changes in slope at approximately 10 T, 15.5 T, and 18 T. The first two features correspond to bulk magnetizations of $1/3$ and $2/3$ of the fully saturated moment, respectively, while the last one marks a quantum phase transition from the second ordered phase to the fully polarized state. These results establish the studied compound as a platform for investigating field-induced quantum phase transitions and emergent phases in frustrated bilayer triangular-lattice antiferromagnets.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Anisotropy lifts topological protection of transport in pumped spin chains
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Mainak Pal
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: We investigate the prospect of topological spin pumping and transport in a dimerized spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ anisotropic XY chain with tunable in-plane anisotropy. Through a Jordan-Wigner transformation, the system maps onto an extended Rice-Mele-type fermionic model whose momentum-space band structure exhibits gapped regions characterized by nonzero Chern numbers ($\pm 1$) as well as trivial and gapless regimes. Conventional momentum-space analysis therefore predicts quantized Thouless-type spin pumping in parts of the Chern number diagram. However, real-space time evolution under open boundary conditions reveals that the spin transport is generally not quantized away from the isotropic limit. In the anisotropic regime, eigen-energy states within the transporting subspace hybridize during the driving cycle, leading to a transport that depends on details of the driving protocol. Quantized pumping and transport survive only in the isotropic limit, where the Hamiltonian reduces to decoupled Rice-Mele sectors and the transported spin component is conserved. Our results demonstrate that momentum-space topological invariants alone do not guarantee quantized spin transport in anisotropic spin chains. More broadly, they show that the conventional Thouless-pumping framework does not straightforwardly extend to situations where the transported quantity is not conserved, highlighting the importance of real-space diagnostics in topological transport phenomena.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Magnon-Phonon-Polariton Optomechanics in a van der Waals Magnet
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Jens-Christian Drawer, Vladislav Yu. Shishkov, Bo Han, Vita Solovyeva, Iva Plutnarová, Zdeněk Sofer, Christian Schneider, Anton V. Zasedatelev, Martin Esmann
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: The layered anti-ferromagnet CrSBr hosts self-hybridized exciton-polaritons that couple parametrically to coherent magnons and phonons. In this work, we explore the tripartite optomechanical interaction between these quasiparticles in suspended CrSBr membranes supporting high-$Q$ breathing-type acoustic phonon modes. Using resonant pump-probe spectroscopy on the polariton state, we resolve the coupled dynamics in the $\simeq 20$ GHz range while sweeping the magnon mode across the phonon resonance with an external magnetic field. We observe an attractive magnon-phonon interaction of strength $V/2π= -43$ MHz, which primarily leads to phonon amplification. At the magnon-phonon resonance, we find predominantly unidirectional energy flow from magnons to phonons while the possible back-action is limited by kinetic losses of coherent magnons. Our study enables direct interfacing of collective magnetic excitations with sound and light in layered van der Waals materials, paving the way for quantum-coherent transduction in the GHz range with optical readout.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Particle-hole asymmetry and a fluctuating pair-density-wave state in a lightly doped Mott insulator on the square lattice
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Hao-Xin Wang, Zheng-Yuan Yue, Wen-Yuan Liu, Zheng-Cheng Gu
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: Whether a lightly doped Mott insulator on the square lattice supports robust $d$-wave superconductivity remains a central question in strongly correlated physics and in the microscopic theory of cuprate superconductivity. Experiments and numerical studies reveal a pronounced particle-hole asymmetry, pointing to a delicate competition among $d$-wave superconductivity, pair-density wave (PDW), stripe, charge-density wave (CDW), and antiferromagnetic correlations. Here we combine large-scale DMRG and finite-size PEPS to study the square-lattice $t$-$J$ model at low doping, $δ\leq 0.1$, while tuning the next-nearest-neighbor hopping $t'$ from the electron-like ($t'>0$) to the hole-like ($t'<0$) regime. The electron-like side supports robust, nearly uniform $d$-wave pairing, whereas decreasing $t'$ induces a period-two plaquette modulation and ultimately produces, on the hole-like side, a charge-dominated state with a strongly suppressed static pairing amplitude. DMRG calculations on open strips and squares, together with PEPS calculations on open squares up to $16\times16$ sites, support this evolution. On squares with $C_4$-symmetric Hamiltonians, both methods find that the pair correlations of the hole-like state select the plaquette momenta $(π,0)$ and $(0,π)$ and decay within a few lattice spacings, while the dominant charge-density modulation forms a bidirectional checkerboard whose period extrapolates to about $4a_0$, close to that observed in lightly doped Bi-2201. These observations establish a fluctuating plaquette PDW in the lightly doped hole-like regime, in which local pairs carry finite momentum but lack phase coherence. Our results firmly establish particle-hole asymmetry as a central organizing principle for competing pairing tendencies in the lightly doped $t$-$J$ model.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Thermodynamic Properties of the S=1/2 Zigzag Spin Ladder
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Nobuya Maeshima, Toshiya Hikihara, Kouichi Okunishi
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: We investigate finite-temperature properties of the spin-1/2 zigzag Heisenberg ladder with an anisotropic off-diagonal $Γ$ interaction. Thermal states are calculated by an infinite time-evolving block decimation method combined with purification, while exact diagonalization is used to analyze low-lying excitations. The entropy is strongly suppressed at low temperatures inside the gapped phases, whereas it remains enhanced near several ground-state phase boundaries. For the Néel phase at $J_2/J_1=0$, the model can be mapped by spin rotations onto the exactly solvable XYZ chain. The thermal gap extracted from the low-temperature specific heat agrees with the exact one-spinon gap, while the finite-size excitation gap obtained by exact diagonalization is consistent with a two-spinon excitation.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Study of the frustrated SU(3) Heisenberg chain with SU(3)-symmetric matrix product states
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: O. R. Hryniv, I. V. Lukin, A. G. Sotnikov
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: We study the SU(3) Heisenberg chain with nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor antiferromagnetic exchange $J_1$ and $J_2$. Field theory predicts that the trimerized valence-bond solid of this chain has a finite extent in $α=J_2/J_1$, followed by a gapless SU(3)$_1$ phase, but earlier numerical estimates of the upper boundary range from $α\approx2.1$ (exact diagonalization) to $α\approx3.8$ (iDMRG). We use the variational uniform matrix product state (VUMPS) algorithm with the full non-Abelian SU(3) symmetry imposed on the virtual bonds, reaching bond dimensions up to $D\approx8000$, and locate the phase boundaries by finite-entanglement scaling. Resolving the transfer-matrix spectrum and the entanglement spectrum by SU(3) irreducible representation, we find that the trimerized phase extends to $α_{c2}\gtrsim3.5$ and end below $α\approx5$, excluding a boundary near $α\approx2$. At larger $α$ our numerical analysis of the effective central charge is consistent with the predicted massless flow from SU(3)$_2$ to SU(3)$_1$.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Native point defects in rock-salt and wurtzite MnSe: formation energies across the growth window and spin splitting in the A-type order
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Tomás Rojas Solorzano, Dale Igram
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: Manganese selenide grows both as rock-salt $α$-MnSe, a type-II antiferromagnet, and as metastable wurtzite w-MnSe, whose magnetic order has not been measured. We compute the neutral Mn and Se vacancies and the two antisites of both polymorphs with density functional theory plus a linear-response Hubbard $U$, between the Se-rich limit bounded by MnSe$_2$ and the Mn-rich limit set by the measured formation enthalpy. In $α$-MnSe the Mn vacancy is lowest over most of the window (0.92 eV under Se-rich conditions), consistent with its p-type conduction. In w-MnSe, the Se antisite is lowest under Se-rich conditions, narrowly in the A-type order and clearly in the stripe order, and the Se vacancy is lowest under Mn-rich conditions. The Se vacancy has nearly the same formation energy in both polymorphs, whereas defects that change the number of Mn atoms differ by 0.4-1.1 eV, although DFT+$U$ places wurtzite below rock salt, contrary to experiment. A spin-degenerate stripe order lies 14 meV per formula unit below the altermagnetic A-type order of w-MnSe, and the formation energies shift between these orders by up to 0.24 eV, most for the Mn vacancy. Three of the four defects leave an uncompensated moment of 3-5 $μ_\mathrm{B}$. In the A-type order, band unfolding shows that the sign-reversing splitting of the most strongly split band, about 230 meV and 3 eV below the valence-band maximum, keeps its peak height within the 8% scatter of the analysis at 3% defects, while points on its shoulders move by up to about 70 meV. Band-edge states are not resolved.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Atomic density optimization of quasi-one-dimensional diffuse laser cooling under a two-dimensional magnetic-field gradient
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Xiaolei Guan, Mengyuan Han, Jia Zhang, Xun Gao, Yu Wang, Wei Zhuang, Tiantian Shi, Jingbiao Chen
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: Diffuse laser cooling (DLC) provides a compact, robust, and scalable approach to generating cold-atom ensembles, offering significant potential for ground-based and spaceborne microwave atomic clocks. However, the performance of DLC systems remains limited by the weak atom-light interaction arising from their relatively low atomic density. This limitation is characterized by the optical density (OD), which quantifies the effective interaction strength between the atomic ensemble and the probe light and strongly influences the achievable signal-to-noise ratio. Although quasi-one-dimensional (quasi-1D) DLC extends the probe interaction length and improves atomic utilization, increasing the local atomic density within the interrogation region remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate a magnetically enhanced quasi-1D DLC system that simultaneously maintains the extended interaction length and increases the atomic density through a two-dimensional magnetic-field gradient. By spatially compressing and accumulating atoms near the probe axis, we enhance the OD of a 70-cm-long cold rubidium ensemble from 2.49 to 3.94, representing a 58% enhancement and an equivalent increase in the local atomic density. The dependence of the OD on the magnetic-field gradient, probe intensity, beam size, and cooling-light polarization is systematically investigated. This work establishes a practical pathway for enhancing optical interrogation efficiency and could pave the way for the development of high-performance DLC-based cold-atom clocks and quantum sensing systems.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Ground-state phase diagram of the spin-1/2 Heisenberg zigzag ladder with anisotropic $Γ$ term revisited
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Toshiya Hikihara, Nobuya Maeshima, Kouichi Okunishi
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: We study the spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet with an anisotropic $Γ$ term on a zigzag ladder, which can be exactly mapped to the spin-1/2 XYZ zigzag ladder by a spin rotation. This model has recently attracted considerable interest as an effective model for the quasi-one-dimensional magnetic semiconductor YbCuS$_2$. For the model, the ground-state phase diagram was previously proposed by Saito and Hotta [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 166701 (2024); Phys. Rev. B 110, 024409 (2024)]. We systematically reexamine the phase diagram through complementary numerical and analytical approaches, including exact diagonalization, the density-matrix renormalization group method, and low-energy effective theories. We thereby demonstrate that when the anisotropic $Γ$ term is present, the model exhibits the Néel, dimer, ferromagnetic, and double-Néel phases, all of which have a finite excitation gap. The gapless Tomonaga-Luttinger-liquid (TLL) phase appears only in the isotropic case where the $Γ$ term is absent. We also confirm that the transitions between the Néel and dimer phases and between the Néel and ferromagnetic phases are continuous transitions governed by Gaussian criticality with central charge $c=1$. The TLL parameter characterizing the critical states at the Gaussian transitions is estimated numerically.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Deconfined Quantum Critical Point in a Dissipative Spin-1/2 Chain
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Longye Lu, Shifeng Cui, Wenan Guo

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Simulating the Haldane model in ultraclean GaAs heterostructures
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Francesco Cioni, Lorenzo Cavicchi, Fabio Taddei, Marco Polini
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: The Haldane model represents the minimal lattice-based realization of a Chern insulator, exhibiting a quantized Hall conductance in the absence of Landau levels. Despite its conceptual elegance, the implementation in crystalline solids of the requisite pattern of Peierls phases breaking time-reversal symmetry remains experimentally demanding. In this work, we theoretically investigate the possibility to simulate the Haldane model in ultraclean GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructures. Our proposal relies on recent experiments in which a high-mobility two-dimensional electron gas is subject to a gate-defined honeycomb electrostatic potential and a laterally periodic magnetic field generated by patterned ferromagnetic structures. The combined electrostatic and magnetic superlattices furnish a viable route to emulate the topological properties of the Haldane model.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Negligible Kitaev interaction in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiBr$_2$ revealed by neutron spectroscopy
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Hao Xu, Shufan Cheng, Yanyan Shangguan, Song Bao, Junbo Liao, Bo Zhang, Zihang Song, Shuai Dong, Maofeng Wu, Shinichi Itoh, Daichi Ueta, Jinsheng Wen
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Using time-of-flight neutron spectroscopy, we have mapped out the magnetic excitations in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiBr$_2$ over a broad range of energies and momenta. The observed well-defined magnon dispersions are quantitatively reproduced by linear spin-wave theory based on a minimal bilinear Hamiltonian that includes Heisenberg exchange interactions up to third-nearest neighbors, interlayer couplings, and a single-ion anisotropy term, with no need to invoke a Kitaev interaction. This finding is consistent with the fact that bromine is lighter than iodine, leading to weaker ligand-mediated spin-orbit coupling in NiBr2 than in NiI2, and consequently a reduced Kitaev interaction. Our results establish NiBr$_2$ as a Heisenberg-dominated van der Waals antiferromagnet and support the view that the ligand spin-orbit coupling governs the strength of the bond-dependent interactions within the NiX$_2$ (X = halogen) family.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Synthesis-route-dependent state selection in the frustrated spinel ZnV$_2$O$_4$
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Jem Pitcairn, Jennifer N. Graham, Jacob L. Brownlee, Shruti Chakravarty, Joya A. Cooley, Giorgia Confalonieri, A. Dominic Fortes, David W. Tam, J. Ross Stewart, Lucy Clark
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: The emergent properties of strongly correlated materials can be highly sensitive to how they are made, yet synthesis pathway is rarely treated as a fundamental variable governing their ground states. The spinel ZnV$_2$O$_4$ provides a model system in which to test this idea: its pyrochlore lattice of antiferromagnetically coupled V$^{3+}$ $S=1$ moments hosts competing spin and orbital degeneracies, while different synthesis routes yield markedly different low-temperature behaviour. Here, we show that changing the solid-state synthesis pathway reproducibly selects a distinct structural and magnetic ground state. Microwave-assisted solid-state synthesis (MASS) stabilises the cubic spinel structure to low temperature, suppressing the conventional cubic-to-tetragonal transition and preserving the highly frustrated $S=1$ pyrochlore lattice. Combining high-resolution diffraction, magnetometry and inelastic neutron scattering, we find a magnetic ground state exhibiting persistent spin-liquid-like dynamics together with partial spin freezing. Our results establish synthesis pathway as an experimental variable for selecting between competing emergent states in strongly correlated materials, revealing a route to accessing ground states not realised by conventional synthesis.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Controlled Magnon Chirality and Its Reversal by Anisotropy in Altermagnetic FeF$_2$
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: E. M. Smith, V. O. Garlea, D. Lederman, J. M. Tranquada, I. A. Zaliznyak, J. Sears
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: In altermagnets, the exchange symmetry of two mutually compensating magnetic sublattices permits spin-polarized electronic bands and chirality-split magnon bands. Because these effects have opposite signs in domains related by time reversal, magnetic-domain control is essential for their observation and utilization. Using half-polarized neutron diffraction, we demonstrate that we can control magnetic domain imbalance in a single crystal of FeF$_2$ by field cooling, and we relate this response to the established piezomagnetism in this material. Our half-polarized inelastic neutron scattering measurements directly resolve the altermagnetic splitting of chiral magnon bands. Strikingly, we observe a clear reversal of chirality near $\mathbf{Q}=(0.5,0.5,1)$, where the altermagnetic exchange splitting vanishes and no chirality is expected in a nonrelativistic exchange model. This reversal of the chirality is well explained by the presence of a transverse component of the single-ion anisotropy tensor, which rotates between Fe sublattices related by the crystal's altermagnetic $4_2$ screw symmetry. These results allow us to resolve fine features of the spin Hamiltonian for FeF$_2$ and show how symmetry-governed relativistic anisotropy can reshape altermagnetic spin dynamics, as well as providing an avenue for control of magnetic domains and the net chiral response.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Reduced vortex descriptors linking polycrystallinity in magnetic nanoparticles with polarized magnetic small-angle neutron scattering
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Michael P. Adams, Jonathan Leliaert, Andreas Michels, Elizabeth M. Jefremovas
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Analytical vortex models reduce polarized magnetic small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) from nanoparticle ensembles to a small set of texture descriptors. In this work, we apply this reduction to micromagnetic simulations of polycrystalline iron oxide nanoflowers at a fixed particle size and examine how a controlled parametrization of multigrain disorder is reflected in the remanent descriptors. The particles are represented by explicit Voronoi microstructures, and intraparticle disorder is varied through the intergrain exchange coupling and anisotropy-axis coherence. Fitting each remanent magnetization state to a hyperbolic vortex model reveals a predominantly two-channel organization: The intergrain exchange coupling is associated mainly with the radial vortex profile, whereas the anisotropy-axis coherence is associated mainly with the orientational moment of the vortex-axis distribution. The normalized spin-flip SANS cross sections are accurately represented by independent fits of the analytical linear-vortex SANS expression obtained from the first-order expansion of the hyperbolic profile. The fitted orientational descriptor agrees closely with its independent real-space estimate, whereas the corresponding radial descriptors exhibit a strong global nonlinear relation. This separation identifies which information from the micromagnetic vortex textures is robustly retained by the reduced analytical representation.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Key role of orbital exchange in CoO magnetism
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Leonid V. Pourovskii, Yuriy Mokrousov
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Co ions in the antiferromagnetic phase of CoO are known to possess a substantial orbital moment, making this material promising for orbitronic applications. However, intersite exchange interactions involving these orbital degrees of freedom remain poorly quantified, and their role in CoO magnetism is unclear. Here, we derive a full low-energy effective Hamiltonian for CoO, including orbital exchange terms, using an ab initio force-theorem approach based on DFT+dynamical mean-field theory. We find sizable orbital interactions, with quadrupolar orbital exchange emerging as the dominant nearest-neighbor term. The collinear antiferromagnetic order obtained from the effective Hamiltonian features magnetic moments tilted away from the pseudocubic <001> direction and an orbital contribution amounting to about one-third of the total moment, in agreement with experimental estimates. We show that the moment tilting originates from the combined effect of orbital and spin-orbital exchange interactions. The same interactions also produce a prominent splitting of the lowest excitation band. By directly modeling the inelastic neutron scattering (INS) intensity, we further show that the characteristic column-like structures previously observed in CoO INS provide a clear fingerprint of orbital exchange. We also discuss possible impact of our findings for further advances in the field of complex collective excitations, their transport properties and applications in the realm of orbitronics.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: TASCopilot: A provenance-preserving assistant for triple-axis neutron scattering
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Carina Jacobson, Aditya Purohit, Srikar Kovvali, Lekhnath Poudel, Jeffrey W. Lynn, William D. Ratcliff
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Experimental decisions often depend on evidence scattered across papers, instrument logs, data files, and specialist software. A scientific assistant must connect that evidence without turning a plausible interpretation into an unsupported conclusion. TAS Co-pilot addresses this problem for triple-axis spectroscopy (TAS), which uses neutrons to probe material structure and excitations. It preserves provenance: the sources, processing steps, and review decisions behind each result. Independently maintained scientific tools communicate through structured requests and results; validation rules and human review govern how evidence can support a claim. Language models extract information and explain outcomes but do not approve scientific claims or control the instrument. Dependency-aware reduction executes existing scientific routines and reuses unchanged intermediate results. A retrospective SrMn$_2$Sb$_2$ study connects literature on a related material and historical alignment records to modeling of magnetic excitations in 20 measured scans. A live BT-7 study uses a dedicated instrument interface for fine alignment and 40 adaptively selected measurements. Agreement with a conventional measurement of the same crystal at shared conditions supports the acquisition and analysis chain. These cases demonstrate a methodology for maintaining inspectable evidence across literature, numerical analysis, and measurement at a user facility.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Orbital differentiation in a rare earth ion near half filling
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: D. W. Tam, Ø. S. Fjellvåg, B. Gonano, E. X. M. Trewick, M. Månsson
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: In the electronic structure of rare earth ions, details can be crucial for understanding the origin of correlated states. Currently, state-of-the-art wavefunction-based methods (e.g. CASSCF) can capture single-ion properties of molecular magnets and some band insulating systems, but are expensive to perform, and cannot be applied to metallic systems. Here, we carry out full multiplet calculations for SmN with the cubic rock-salt structure using the crystal field software Quanty. The calculated experimental observables from our model agree precisely with magnetic susceptibility and inelastic neutron scattering experiments, and the spatially resolved spin density also agrees with DFT predictions. By tuning the crystal field parameters, our full multiplet-derived wavefunctions reveal the presence of orbital differentiation of the ground $J=\frac{5}{2}$ manifold into two groups, which are distinct subspaces with different orbital stiffness. This violation of Hund's rule, observed with a fast and inexpensive calculation tool, represents a step forward for microscopic models of rare earth materials, and may provide support for the claim of unconventional triplet superconductivity in SmN.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Softening of low-energy anharmonic phonon modes in rutile TiO 2 investigated by inelastic x-ray and neutron scattering
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Kota Moriguchi, Koji Kimura, Yujiro Hashimoto, Dinh Ngoc Dung, Satoshi Tsutsui, Taishun Manjo, Hiroshi Fukui, Daisuke Ishikawa, Alfred Q R Baron, Yoichi Ikeda, Harry Handoko Halim, Akitoshi Nakano, Yoshitada Morikawa, Hiroki Taniguchi, Koichi Hayashi
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Low-energy anharmonic phonons in rutile TiO 2 were investigated by inelastic x-ray and neutron scattering (IXS and INS) techniques. Owing to the different sensitivities of IXS and INS to phonon modes, the transverse optical branches corresponding to the B 1u and A 2u modes at the Γ point were selectively observed in the respective spectra. It was found that the lowest-energy B 1u mode exhibits pronounced softening with decreasing temperature, while the A 2u mode also shows softening, as previously reported. The observed temperature-dependent softening was well reproduced by density functional theory calculations based on the stochastic self-consistent harmonic approximation, although the magnitude of the softening was quantitatively underestimated. The pronounced softening of the B 1u mode, as well as its finite linewidth, is discussed in terms of possible higher-order phonon interactions between the B 1u and A 2u modes. The implications of this strong anharmonicity for lattice-related physicochemical properties, including dielectric response, thermal transport, Li-ion insertion, and polaron-related photocatalytic phenomena, are also addressed.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Site-selective substitutions and magnetic structures in ( Fe , Co ) 2 ( P , Si ) compounds probed by x-ray linear dichroism and neutron diffraction
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: L. L. Bao, W. Wei, H. Yibole, Jiazheng Hao, Lunhua He, F. Wilhelm, A. Rogalev, F. Guillou

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Crystal and magnetic structures of MnSi in zero magnetic field: Neutron diffraction and symmetry analysis
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Vladimir Pomjakushin, Igor Plokhikh, Douglas H. Fabini, Ekaterina Pomjakushina
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Combining high-resolution wide-angle neutron powder diffraction with magnetic-superspace symmetry analysis, we refine the crystal structure and present, to our knowledge, the first systematic refinement of cubic $P2_13$ MnSi's zero-field magnetic structure across multiple magnetic satellite families. We compare single-arm rhombohedral 3+1D and cubic four-arm 3+4D magnetic superspace-group (MSSG) descriptions with propagation vectors along $\langle111\rangle$. Simultaneous extinction of the two satellite groups around $\{100\}$ dictates a transverse circular-helix model. This suppression and refinements of 18 separately varied satellite-group intensities support this ideal limit with only one adjustable magnetic amplitude. In the ideal single-arm model with MSSG $R3.1'(0,0,g)ts$, the moment has constant magnitude 0.535(3) $μ_B$ per Mn. An explicit four-arm 3+4D cubic superspace construction presented here combines four interpenetrating helices and, for the illustrated phase choice, has moments ranging from zero to 0.874(5) $μ_B$ per Mn, with the same root-mean-square moment as the 3+1D structure. Their identical powder profiles prevent the present measurements from distinguishing them. The average crystal structure remains cubic within experimental resolution, providing structural motivation for the cubic magnetic model. The mean lattice parameter, determined with formal relative precision $σ_a/a \lesssim 10^{-5}$, exhibits nonmonotonic temperature dependence below the Néel temperature.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Finite temperature and pressure structural relaxations including zero-point motion and anharmonicity
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Henricus R. A. ten Eikelder, Florian Knoop, Florian Trybel
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: At finite temperature and pressure, the equilibrium structure of a crystal minimizes the Gibbs free energy rather than the static Born-Oppenheimer energy. We present WARP (Wyckoff-constrained Anharmonic Relaxations at Pressure and temperature), a symmetry-constrained, variable-cell relaxation based on the stochastic temperature-dependent effective potential method, including anharmonicity and zero-point motion. Every position update is projected onto Wyckoff positions and every strain onto symmetric strains, so a relaxation can raise the symmetry but never lower it. For aluminum, the thermal expansion follows measurements at cryogenic temperatures, including the quantum plateau below 50 K. For lanthanum hydrides at megabar pressures, equations of state agree with phonon-based and path-integral calculations, and LaH$_{10}$ relaxes from its rhombohedral static minimum to the observed cubic phase, also with a machine-learned potential fine-tuned on 150 supercells. For brucite, Mg(OD)$_2$, lattice parameters, bond distances and thermal expansion agree with neutron diffraction, and the O-D isotope effect is captured.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Coupled magnetic and lattice excitations in multiferroic Ba 3 HoRu 2 O 9 : Insights from neutron scattering, Raman spectroscopy, and machine-learned phonon calculations
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: E. Kushwaha, S. Ghosh, G. Roy, M. Kumar, M. D. Le, J. Shannigrahi, S. D. Kaushik, D. T. Adroja, T. Basu

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Design of nSPIRAL: a Neutron Spectrometric Position-Weighted Radial Array Long-Counter
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: E. Mendoza, J. Guerrero-Cánovas, D. Bachiller-Perea, C. Ballesteros, D. Cano-Ott, J. García, J. Llanes Gamonoso, T. Martínez, A. Pérez de Rada Fiol, J. Plaza, L. Romero, R. Santorelli, D. Villamarín, O. Alonso-Sañudo, G. Auñón, M. J. G. Borge, J. A. Briz, F. Calviño, G. Cortés, A. De Blas, B. Fernández, L. M. Fraile, G. García, R. García, V. García-Tavora, C. Guerrero, A. Illana, N. Mont-Geli, V. Martínez-Nouvilas, E. Nácher, A. Nerio-Aguirre, M. Pallàs, A. Perea, D. Soler, J. L. Taín, A. Tarifeño-Saldivia, O. Tengblad, J. M. Udías
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: We present here the design of a neutron long counter intended to measure neutrons originating from radioactive decays or nuclear reactions. Like other similar detectors, it relies on a moderator (polyethylene) and $^{3}$He tubes. A novel feature of our design is the use of the weighting technique to achieve an efficiency that is virtually independent of the energy spectrum of the neutrons being measured; a property known as \textit{flat efficiency}. This approach offers two primary advantages: it yields a flatter efficiency response than conventional analysis methods, and it provides greater flexibility regarding the geometry of the long counter. The latter has enabled us to design the detector with almost every $^{3}$He tube positioned at a different distance from the neutron source, which allows us to perform not only neutron counting but also neutron spectroscopy.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: The microscopic origin of the hysteretic hydrogen adsorption in Double Wall Carbon Nanotubes bundles
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Carlos Cabrillo, Ricardo Fernández-Perea, Felix Fernández-Alonso
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: In a recent study we reported large hysteretic hydrogen adsorption in samples made out of Double Wall Carbon Nanotubes (DWCNT) at supercritical temperatures (50 K, 77 K and 150 K), a physical behavior of practical interest. Here, we center our efforts in elucidate its physical origin by means of neutron diffraction (ND) and computer simulations. After a detailed theoretical modeling of the ND signal we were able to quantitatively study how the nanostructure of the material reacts to the hydrogen loads. An expansion of the bundle structure with increasing hydrogen load was found. Taking advantage of the translational symmetry of a DWCNT bundle along the nanotube axis, a two dimensional numerical analogue of the system helped us to clarify the microscopic origin of the hysteresis. Two microscopic mechanisms are identified as responsible for the metastable hydrogen adsorption, one structurally static in character, namely, H$_{2}$-load dependent effective energy barriers between interstitials, the other related to the structural deformation, namely, the opening/closing of the channels between interstitials with increasing/decreasing H$_{2}$ loads owing to the concomitant bundle expansion/contraction.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Pair distribution function oscillations at electrostatically stabilized nanocrystal surfaces reflect nanocrystal lattice periodicity
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Vivian R. K. Wall, Andrew Yang, Bryan A. Sanchez Monserrate, Ahhyun Jeong, Christian P. N. Tanner, Joshua Portner, John P. Davis, Tim B. van Driel, Burak Guzelturk, Gihan Kwon, Olaf J. Borkiewicz, David T. Limmer, Dmitri V. Talapin, Karena W. Chapman, Simon J. L. Billinge, Naomi S. Ginsberg
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Nanocrystals (NCs) stabilized electrostatically by short, multivalent inorganic ligands exhibit rich interactions and phase behavior believed to hinge on the configuration of ions at the NC surface, yet these molecular details have not previously been measured. Here we use double-difference pair distribution functions (ddPDFs) of total X-ray scattering to determine the configuration of Sn$_2$S$_6^{4-}$ ligands on PbS NCs suspended in multivalent electrolyte. The measured ddPDFs exhibit a $\sim$3-$\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ wavelength oscillation that extends $\sim$10 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$. Comparison with a PbS NC model decorated with Sn$_2$S$_6^{4-}$ ligands indicates ligands are aligned $\sim$radially, suggesting bidentate binding. Calculated partial PDFs show that the oscillatory signal is dominated by nanocrystal-Pb to ligand-Sn correlations. A simplified model that replaces the ligand with a strongly scattering Pt atom near the NC surface confirms the oscillation period in the ddPDF originates from the NC lattice constant. Nanocrystal lattice periodicity therefore merits consideration when interpreting ddPDFs of colloidal NCs.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Irena and pyIrena : 25 years of small-angle scattering analysis for complex materials, now with an AI-ready Python successor
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Jan Ilavsky
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: I describe Irena and pyIrena , a paired family of open-source packages for the analysis of small-angle X-ray and neutron scattering data from complex hierarchical materials. Irena was developed at the ultra-small-angle X-ray scattering instrument of the Advanced Photon Source in the early 2000s in response to a lack of analysis software for polydisperse multi-scale multi-phase systems in applied research – hierarchical polymer structures, polydisperse pores or precipitates in metals, soils, woods, coals, biological tissues, food microstructures and beyond. Twenty-five years of community-driven growth followed. Now, pyIrena (v1.0, July 2026) reimplements the most commonly used algorithms in pure Python on Linux, macOS and Windows, and presents them through a Qt graphical interface that mirrors the Irena graphical interface. Additionally, pyIrena provides a scriptable batch API designed for automated beamline pipelines and a Model Context Protocol server enabling large-language-model agents to interact with pyIrena data and tools. Bidirectional interoperability – Igor Pro .h5xp export from pyIrena and NXcanSAS HDF5 import in Irena – lets users move freely between the two environments. The contribution reported here is architectural rather than algorithmic: a platform-independent reimplementation, bidirectional interoperability between the Python and Igor Pro ecosystems, and several coequal access surfaces over a single analytical core.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: diffpy.morph: Python tools for model-independent comparisons between sets of one-dimensional functions
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Andrew Yang, Christopher L. Farrow, Pavol Juhás, Luis Kitsu Iglesias, Chia-Hao Liu, Samuel D. Marks, Vivian R. K. Wall, Joshua Safin, Sean M. Drewry, Caden Myers, Dillon F. Hanlon, Nicholas Leonard, Cedomir Petrovic, Ahhyun Jeong, Dmitri V. Talapin, Linda F. Nazar, Haidong Zhou, Samuel W. Teitelbaum, Tim B. van Driel, Soham Banerjee, Emil S. Bozin, Michael F. Toney, Katharine Page, Naomi S. Ginsberg, Simon J. L. Billinge
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: addresses a need to gain scientific insights from one-dimensional (1D) scientific spectra in model-independent ways. A powerful approach for this is to take differences between pairs of spectra and look for meaningful changes that might indicate underlying chemical, structural, or other modifications. The challenge is that the difference curve may contain uninteresting differences such as experimental inconsistencies and benign physical changes such as the effects of thermal expansion. allows researchers to apply simple transformations, or “morphs,” to one of the datasets to remove the unwanted differences, revealing, when they are present, nontrivial differences. is an open-source Python package available on the Python Package Index and conda-forge. Here, we describe its functionality and apply it to solve a range of experimental challenges on diffraction and pair distribution function data from x-rays and neutrons, though we note that it may be applied to any 1D function in principle.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Generation of neutron Bessel beams
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Owen Lailey, Dusan Sarenac, Nir Emelianenko, Charles W. Clark, David G. Cory, Huseyin Ekinci, Michael G. Huber, Jeremy W. Paster, Anna Sokolova, Diego Alba Venero, Dmitry A. Pushin
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Matter waves can exhibit structured wavefields analogous to those of light, offering new means of controlling the spatial and angular-momentum degrees of freedom of massive particles. Bessel beams are a fundamental class of structured waves that exhibit non-diffracting propagation, self-healing, and well-defined orbital angular momentum (OAM). Here, we experimentally realize neutron Bessel beams by imprinting a nanoscale conical phase gradient onto a neutron wavefront. By incorporating azimuthal phase gradients, we generate zeroth-, third-, and sixth-order Bessel beams, demonstrating direct control of both the OAM and radial structure of a massive particle. We also propose a neutron Bessel-grating interferometer, complementary to established optical and electron interferometric methods, in which varying the radial grating period by approximately 100 nm yields a controlled Gouy phase shift of $π$. These results establish neutron Bessel beams as a new platform for diffractive neutron focusing and provide an experimental foundation for theoretical studies of Bessel beams in neutron scattering, decay, and OAM characterization.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Dipole-exchange spin waves and mode hybridization in magnetic nanoparticles
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Fedor Shuklin, Khristina Albitskaya, Sergei Solovyov, Alexander Chernov, Mihail Petrov

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Evolution of magnetic structure from amplitude-modulated to Néel order in Ho 2 Re 3 Si 5
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Vikash Sharma, Denis Sheptyakov, Anup Kumar Bera, A. Thamizhavel

Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.title: Scintillator-Based Event-Mode Neutron Imaging with Timepix4 Readout
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.authors: Wenqin Yang, Xingfen Jiang, Junan Geng, Yang Liu, Qicai Li, Hongbin Liu, Xiaojuan Zhou, Yanfeng Wang, Li Yu, Xiuku Wang, Peixun Shen, Jiayi Ren, Yubin Zhao, Jianrong Zhou, Zhijia Sun, Yuanbo Chen
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.abstract: Scintillator-based event-mode neutron imaging is emerging as a powerful approach to neutron radiography. Unlike conventional integrating-mode neutron imaging, which accumulates scintillation light during an exposure, event reconstruction estimates neutron-event positions and arrival times from time-stamped optical responses. We investigated this approach using a self-developed Timepix4-based optical readout system, image-formation analysis, and beam experiments at the China Spallation Neutron Source under different scintillator and optical configurations. The analysis explains how event localization can reduce image blur associated with the spatial extent of individual scintillation responses. Under the same 0.35$\times$ optical configuration, event reconstruction improved the spatial resolution from 164.2 to 91.9 $μ$m at 10% modulation transfer function (MTF), while a 2.1$\times$ configuration with a $\mathrm{Gd_2O_2S:Tb}$ scintillator achieved 26.1 $μ$m at the same MTF threshold. Following event reconstruction and rejection of single-photon reconstructed events, the mean peak-normalized spectral response in the 6-8 angstrom out-of-band interval decreased by 85.4% relative to the raw-pixel wavelength-count spectrum, indicating reduced afterglow-related spectral background. Under the tested pulsed-beam conditions, the maximum instantaneous pixel-hit rate per pixel was approximately four times its time-averaged value, providing an experimental basis for assessing readout requirements at higher neutron flux. Conventional radiography resolved structural details, while energy-selective imaging enhanced the contrast between materials with similar broadband transmission and Bragg-edge imaging revealed crystallographic features in steel. These results demonstrate the imaging-quality benefits and capabilities of scintillator-based event-mode neutron imaging.

Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.title: Development of Sapphire-Based Solid-State Neutron Detectors for Fusion Environments
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.authors: Matteo Hakeem Kushoroa, Stephanie Cancelli, Gabriele Croci, Benno Margesin, Federica Mantegazzini, Enrico Perelli Cippo
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.abstract: Single-crystal diamond is the reference solid-state technology for fast neutron detection in fusion devices. Despite this, its complex manufacturing increases their costs and puts limitations on their geometry. Moreover, the limits in their long-term stability and their behaviour in harsh environments further constraint its applications. Synthetic sapphire (Al2O2) is a promising alternative as a solid state detector material: it is available in large, low-cost wafers and features both a wider bandgap and a higher displacement energy compared to diamond. Despite this, it has so far received little-to-no attention as a neutron detector. This work presents the first steps of a development programme for sapphire-based fast neutron detectors. Eight prototypes with 4.5 x 4.5 mm2 and 9 x 9 mm2 active areas and 625 um thickness were fabricated from commercial wafers with Al-Si electrodes and coupled to different electronic configurations. All prototypes detected 5.47 MeV alpha particles from a 241Am source, confirming the viability of both the fabrication process and the use of sapphire as an active material. The small signals (30-40 mV over a peak-to-peak noise of about 8 mV) and the count rate increasing with bias indicate that sapphires will require higher electric fields than the ones experimented in the work (up to about 2.5 kV). Geant4 simulations were also used to estimate the response of a sapphire detector to 14.06 MeV (DT) neutrons, highlighting the perspectives of the detector as a fusion diagnostic.

Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.title: Construction and performance evaluation of a meter-scale monolithic scintillator tracker with embedded scatterers
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.authors: N. Otani, S. Han, E. Abad Díaz, S. Aoki, D. Barčot, C. Bronner, T. Fukuda, M. Ghosh, L. Halić, K. Hasegawa, T. Hayakawa, Y. Hayasaka, K. Hayashi, D. Hirata, K. Indo, M. Jakkapu, A. Kasumi, T. Katori, T. Kawahara, M. Kawaue, T. Kikawa, B. Kliček, H. Kobayashi, B. Kovač, J. McKean, T. Matsuo, S. Mikado, A. Minamino, Y. Morimoto, Y. Nakamura, T. Nakaya, H. Oaira, N. Onda, H. Oshima, O. Sato, for the NINJA Collaboration
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.abstract: A meter-scale Fiber-Readout mOnolithic and Scatterer-embedded scintillator Tracker (FROST) was constructed and operated in the NINJA experiment to enable muon-track matching between the nuclear emulsion detectors and the downstream muon detector. The detector consists of a 1.32 m $\times$ 1.40 m plastic scintillator plate assembled from optically bonded scatterer-embedded plates, with wavelength-shifting fibers arranged at a pitch of 10 mm. During J-PARC neutrino-beam operation, FROST achieved a data acquisition efficiency of 99.59% and a detection efficiency of 99.946$\pm$0.006% for selected neutrino-induced muons well within the active area. A position reconstruction method based on the light-yield distribution was developed for both single- and multi-particle events. In a neutrino-interaction simulation, muon position resolutions of 1.77 mm and 1.61 mm were achieved in the two orthogonal readout directions, assuming correct muon identification. Using a beam-data sample dominated by single-muon events, upper limits on the position resolution of 2.20 mm and 2.03 mm were obtained for track angles below 20°. These results demonstrate that the FROST concept can be scaled up to a meter-scale active area while maintaining high detection efficiency and a position resolution well below the readout pitch under actual experimental conditions.

Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.title: The physical design of the superfluid helium-4 UCN source at CSNS
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.authors: Xue-Fen Han, Bin Zhou, Song-Lin Wang, Xiao-Xiao Cai, Dong-Dong Zhou, Yi-Jie Cai, Fei Shen, Tian-Jiao Liang, Robert Golub
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.abstract: Ultracold neutrons (UCN) play a crucial role in fundamental physics research, enabling investigations into new sources of CP violation, neutron lifetime measurements, and the exploration of non-Newtonian forces. However, these experiments are often limited by the intensity of UCN sources. The China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS) is developing a UCN source utilizing superfluid helium-4 at Beamline 12. This paper focuses on enhancing UCN density and total UCN number by analyzing various parameters that impact the UCN system, including the influence of different wavelengths of cold neutrons, incident beam size, converter length, wall and reflector materials, extraction method, extraction guide radius, and guide material composition. A preliminary design of the UCN source at CSNS is presented based on this analysis. For a Be-coated converter, the predicted saturated UCN density is 315 UCN/cm^3, with a UCN production rate of 12,055 UCN/s and an extraction efficiency of 84%, yielding approximately 1.3 x 10^6 extracted UCNs per cycle in accumulation mode. The UCN source design presented in this study forms part of the overall physical design of the Neutron Physics and Application Spectrometer at CSNS, which successfully passed its physical design review on March 25, 2025.

Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.title: Study of neutron flux redistribution and shadowing effect in rod worth measurements with the rod drop experiment
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.authors: Giovanni L. Stefani, Guilherme E. S. Carvalho, Daniel A. P. Palma, Marcelo V. Silva, Cesar Raitz
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.abstract: This study investigates neutron flux redistribution and the shadowing effect between control rods during rod-worth measurements using the rod-drop experiment. A simulation-based instrumental calibration methodology is proposed to account for spatial effects on neutron detector responses and improve the accuracy of reactivity measurements. The IPEN/MB-01 research reactor was modeled using the MCNP Monte Carlo neutron transport code. Reactivity behavior during the initial transient of the rod-drop experiment (t < 10 s) was evaluated and compared with experimental measurements using the source-jerk method. The methodology quantifies control rod shadowing and detector-dependent neutron flux redistribution, allowing correction factors to be established for the measured reactivity. Control-bank worth values obtained through the stable-period method were adopted as reference measurements. The reported maximum deviations from the reference values were 0.5% and 11.3%, respectively. The results demonstrate the relevance of spatial neutron flux effects, control rod interactions, and detector calibration in rod-drop experiments, providing a computational and experimental basis for improving control rod worth measurements in research reactors.

Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.title: Characterization of the fast neutron response of liquid scintillator detectors at NFS
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.authors: A. Pérez de Rada Fiol, G. del Río, T. Martínez, X. Ledoux, V. Alcayne, C. Ballesteros, D. Cano-Ott, I. Matea, P. Miriot-Jaubert, J. Plaza, A. Sánchez-Caballero, M. Vandebrouck, D. Villamarín
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.abstract: The fast neutron response of MONSTER and sTED liquid scintillation detectors was investigated using time-of-flight measurements at the Neutrons For Science facility at GANIL-SPIRAL2. A continuous neutron beam produced by 40 MeV deuterons on a thick beryllium converter was used to obtain pulse height distributions for selected incident neutron energies. Digital pulse shape analysis was used to distinguish neutron-induced events and reduce pile-up effects. For MONSTER, the response and detection efficiency were studied up to 40 MeV using Geant4 with previously obtained light output functions and PHITS in SCINFUL mode. The comparison examines the increasing importance of carbon reaction channels and the divergence between the calculated efficiencies above 20 MeV. For sTED, light output functions for recoil deuterons and alpha particles were determined for the first time for this detector. The measured and calculated efficiencies were compared up to 20 MeV. The sTED efficiency shows a good overall agreement with the simulations. These results provide experimentally constrained detector response information for nuclear data measurements and identify limitations that must be considered when extending the simulations to higher neutron energies.

Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.title: Characterization of a Large-Area HRPPD MCP-PMT Coupled to LYSO for TOF-PET
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.authors: Yingjie Wang, Mark A. Popecki, Heejong Kim, Alexey V. Lyashenko, Stefan Cwik, Mythra Varun Nemallapudi, Jeffrey S. Souris, Michael J. Minot, Chien-Min Kao, Chin-Tu Chen
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.abstract: Large-area microchannel-plate photomultipliers (MCP-PMTs) such as the High-Rate Picosecond Photon Detector (HRPPD) are attractive for time-of-flight positron emission tomography (TOF-PET). They offer excellent single-photon time resolution, low dark count rate, and large monolithic active areas. However, the coincidence time resolution (CTR) reported so far with PET scintillators falls short of expectations based upon their single-photon time resolution. We characterized a 104x104 mm$^2$ HRPPD coupled to LYSO crystals and read out through a custom high-frequency amplifier. With a 2x2x3 mm$^3$ LYSO crystal we measured a CTR of 107 ps full width at half maximum (FWHM) against a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM)-based reference detector. After subtracting the calibrated reference detector's contribution of 42 ps, the single HRPPD detector was found to contribute 98 ps, corresponding to 139 ps for two identical HRPPD detectors in coincidence. With clinical 3x3x20 mm$^3$ crystals the CTR against the reference SiPM detector was 160 ps, corresponding to 218 ps for two identical HRPPD detectors. Timing and gain were uniform across output pads within measurement precision. Summing the four pads under a 3x3x10 mm$^3$ LYSO crystal, the energy resolution for 511 keV gamma ray was 14.6% FWHM, and the 1275 keV line of the $^{22}$Na source was within 1% of its proportional position relative to the 511 keV peak. Flood maps resolved the individual 3 mm elements of a 4x4 array despite the 25 mm pad pitch. To the best of our knowledge the observed timing resolution improves substantially on what has been reported for large-area MCP-PMTs coupled to PET scintillators, and the crystal array identification has not been demonstrated before on such a device. These results indicate that this device class deserves renewed consideration as a photodetector technology for high-performance TOF-PET systems.

Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.title: Cancellation of cryocooler-induced vibration in trapped-ion systems
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.authors: Alexandra Plocki, Kyle Debry, Agustin Valdes Martinez, Isaac L. Chuang, Robert McConnell, Colin D. Bruzewicz
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.abstract: Mechanical cryocoolers offer numerous benefits for the operation of vacuum systems containing trapped atomic ions. However, the fidelity of laser-based gates can be degraded by phase noise induced by the cryocooler vibrations. We present a feed-forward vibration-cancellation system that directly measures inner shield displacement with an auxiliary interferometer and applies a compensating phase correction to the laser drive. The interferometer signal is demodulated, and a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) system unwraps the displacement measurement signal, computes the required correction phase, and updates the RF drive of an in-line acousto-optic modulator (AOM) to correct for the vibration-induced dephasing. With cancellation active, the qubit coherence time improves from $3.0\pm0.4$ ms to $35\pm5$ ms, consistent with a simulation based on the measured vibration spectrum. We further validate the cancellation by artificially increasing the mechanical coupling of the cryocooler to the vacuum chamber. The vibration-induced decoherence rate is suppressed by a factor of approximately 70 at an RMS (root mean square) displacement of 0.65 $\mathrmμ$m.

Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.title: A near-quantum-limited diamond maser amplifier operating at millikelvin temperatures
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.authors: Morihiro Ohta, Ching-Ping Lee, Vincent P. M. Sietses, I. Kostylev, J. R. Ball, P. Moroshkin, T. Hamamoto, Y. Kobayashi, S. Onoda, T. Ohshima, J. Isoya, Hiroki Takahashi, Yuimaru Kubo
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.abstract: Current microwave quantum technologies require the amplification of weak signals with minimal added noise at millikelvin temperatures. To date, this stringent requirement has been met exclusively by superconducting technologies, such as Josephson or kinetic-inductance parametric amplifiers. A fundamentally distinct alternative approach could be offered by masers, the microwave counterpart of lasers, which were predicted as early as the 1950s to achieve quantum-limited noise performance under ideal conditions. However, their dependence on cryogenic operation historically limited further advancement. Here we demonstrate the first-ever non-superconducting, near-quantum-limited maser amplifier operating at millikelvin temperatures utilising nitrogen impurity spins (P1 centres) in diamond. Population inversion is achieved via microwave pumping, exploiting a four-spin cross-relaxation mechanism. We realise a maximum power gain exceeding 30 dB, an added noise of approximately 2.55 quanta above the standard quantum limit, and a maximum 1 dB output compression point of −63 dBm at 6.595 GHz. The ability to operate in strong static magnetic fields of arbitrary orientation may offer a complementary, non-superconducting route for applications such as semiconducting spin-qubit readout, magnetic-resonance spectroscopy, and dark-matter axion searches.

Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.title: Oversampled Filter Bank Channelizer for Cryogenic Detectors
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.authors: L. H. Arnaldi, D. Dellavale
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.abstract: We present the field programmable gate array (FPGA) implementation of an oversampled gener- alized DFT (GDFT) filter bank, optimized for its usage in the readout of cryogenic detectors, such as the microwave kinetic inductance detectors (MKID). A polyphase structure is derived underlin- ing the efficiency of complex valued subband processing, raised by a GDFT modulation. For the latter, a fast Fourier algorithm realization may be used, yielding a highly efficient polyphase imple- mentation for arbitrary integer decimation ratios. The filter bank is tested through a 16-channel GDFT channelizer. The implementation is based on the Xilinx Zynq family of FPGAs and aims to show the data reuse and flexibility offered by the GDFT channelizer structure. General design criteria are summarized for the 16-channel polyphase filter bank channelizer. The performance in hardware resource usage is also presented, taking into account one of the main objetives of the current physics experiments, aiming to have extremely large readout format.
