The combined effect of spin-orbit coupling, exchange interactions, and orbital hybridization gives rise to a large MAE with maximum in-plane values of $-$3.5 meV for 2V$_\text{2Mo}$ and $-$3.2 meV for 2Mn$_\text{2W}$. Monte Carlo simulations estimate T$_\text{c}$ $\simeq$ 440 K for 2Fe$_\text{2Mo}$ and ensure its high-temperature stability in 2D-MoSe$_2$. Our results establish dopant clustering as an effective route to engineer high-temperature ferromagnetism in 2D-TMDs and highlight their potential for nano-spintronic applications.

Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.title: Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics-Guided Machine-Learning Potentials for Mapping Nitric Oxide Interactions with Oxygen-Covered Graphite
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.authors: Yaideny Rodriguez Linares, Gilberto A. Alou Angulo, Samuel Del Fré, Maurice Monnerville, Alejandro Rivero Santamaría
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.abstract: Exploratory ab initio molecular dynamics is used to construct machine-learning interatomic potentials for NO interactions with highly oriented pyrolytic graphite at 33\% bridge-site oxygen coverage. Representative configurations sampled across surface temperatures and incidence energies provide reference energies and forces for training and validation. The selected potential enables relaxation of 300 adsorption configurations and construction of spatial and angular interaction maps. These maps reveal increasingly restricted attractive regions during vertical approach and reduced short-range repulsion upon molecular reorientation. The resulting adsorption geometries and interaction landscapes guide further first-principles sampling toward refining potentials for NO oxidation dynamics.

Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.title: Uncovering the Structural, Electronic, and Electrostatic Landscapes of SrTiO$_3$ Grain Boundaries via Grand Canonical Monte Carlo with a Machine-Learning Interatomic Potential
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.authors: Xing He, Kairi Masuda, Aaron M. Schankler, Songsong Zhou, Andrew M. Rappe
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.abstract: Grain boundaries in perovskites exhibit a rich variety of electronic, polar and magnetic properties, yet identifying their atomic structures and compositions remains challenging. Here, we combine the Grand Canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) method with a universal machine-learning interatomic potential to explore the coupled compositional and structural phase space of $Σ$5(310)[001] SrTiO$_3$ grain boundaries. The resulting chemical potential phase diagram identifies ten stable structures belonging to four motif families: large Sr kite, small Sr kite, incomplete Sr large kite, and Ti-rich structures. Extending the GCMC method to the Sigma5(210)[001] and Sigma17(410)[001] grain boundaries reveals how grain boundary plane and inclination angle influence the competition between small- and large-kite motifs. Density functional theory calculations of the predicted Sigma5(310)[001] grain boundaries show that the composition and atomic structure strongly govern the spatial distribution of conduction and valence band edge states, interfacial band alignment, and carrier localization. Four distinct electronic regimes emerge: localized electron-doped, delocalized electron-doped, insulating, and hole-attracting states. Our electrostatics analysis reveals the coexistence of the short-range electric fields at the reconstructed GB core associated with local atomic density and bonding, and the longer-range fields outside the core arising from the space charge. These fields can also couple to local polar distortions and generate composition-dependent polarization patterns. These results establish an efficient framework for exploring oxide perovskite grain boundary structures and reveal how stoichiometry and atomic reconstruction couple to electronic structure, electrostatics, and local polarization, providing a route toward predictive grain boundary engineering in functional perovskites.

Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.title: Realization of Repulsive Polarons in the Strongly Correlated Regime
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.authors: R. Henke, J. Levinsen, M. M. Parish, J. Boronat, G. E. Astrakharchik, H. Moritz, C. R. Cabrera
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.abstract: Mobile impurities interacting with a quantum medium form quasiparticles known as polarons, a central concept in many-body physics. While the quantum impurity problem has been extensively studied with ultracold atomic gases, repulsive polarons in the strongly correlated regime have remained elusive. Typically, the impurity atoms bind into molecules or rapidly decay into deeper-lying states before they can acquire an appreciable dressing cloud. Here, we report on the realization of polarons in a strongly repulsive two-dimensional quantum gas. Using a superfluid of Li 6 dimers, we introduce impurities by promoting a small fraction of the dimers into higher levels of the transverse confining potential. These novel synthetic-spin polarons give access to the strongly repulsive regime where common decay channels are suppressed. We extract key polaron properties—the energy, quasiparticle residue, and effective mass—using trap modulation and Bragg spectroscopy. Our measurements are well captured by a microscopic T -matrix approach and quantum Monte Carlo simulations, revealing deviations from mean-field predictions. In particular, we measure a significant enhancement of the polaron mass, with values exceeding twice the free-dimer mass. Our demonstration of a stable repulsive Bose polaron establishes a platform for studying impurity physics in low-dimensional and strongly correlated systems.

Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.title: Assessing the expressive power of a gauge-invariant PEPS ansatz across a topological phase transition
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.authors: Etsuko Itou, Tsuyoshi Okubo
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.abstract: We investigate the expressive power of the gauged Gaussian fermionic projected entangled pair state (GGFPEPS) ansatz, which is a manifestly gauge-invariant tensor network ansatz for $(2+1)$-dimensional lattice gauge theories. In the GGFPEPS ansatz, the gauge field on each link is represented by coupling its configuration to the fermion number of virtual fermions placed at both ends of the link. This ansatz has been studied by variational Monte Carlo (VMC) methods in previous work~\cite{Emonts:2022yom}. However, the statistical error of VMC makes a precise determination of the variational parameters difficult, so that the expressive power of the ansatz could not be examined accurately. In this work, we reformulate the computation as a Grassmann tensor network (TN), in which the whole network is contracted deterministically, and introduce the higher-order tensor renormalization group (HOTRG), which allows us to perform calculations in large volumes up to $L=34$. We also evaluate the infinite volume system using the corner transfer matrix renormalization group (CTMRG). We find that the ansatz with only eight complex variational parameters accurately describes the pure $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory including the region of the topological phase transition, not only in the energy but also in the topological entanglement entropy. The critical coupling obtained from the peaks of their susceptibilities agrees quantitatively with the one predicted by continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo simulations~\cite{wu2012phase}. Furthermore, near the transition point, we show that the ansatz represents a state outside the plaquette product family, which is a one-parameter family of states assumed in the construction of the ansatz as a simple interpolation between the strong and weak coupling limits.

Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.title: Strain-dependent Dynamics of Interactions of Iodine-vacancy pairs in CsPbI3: A DFT and Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Study
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.authors: Donggeun Kang, Seongju Lee, Yonggoon Jeon
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.abstract: Iodine-vacancy migration and association are important factors in the structural stability of halide perovskites. Although neighboring vacancies have been suggested to form energetically favorable pairs, their stability and reconfiguration under finite-temperature lattice deformation remain unclear. Here, we combine machine-learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) and density functional theory (DFT) to investigate neighboring iodine vacancies in tilted CsPbI3 under isotropic and biaxial strain. The MLMD trajectories reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of short-time hopping fractions on strain, with strong isotropic compression favoring point-like separation and tension promoting pair-preserving relay hopping. Notably, biaxial compression produces distinct orientation-dependent responses: vacancy pairs initially aligned with the compressed plane preferentially undergo separation, whereas those perpendicular to the plane predominantly exhibit relay hopping. Complementary static calculations using DFT and the SevenNet-0 potential yield repulsive interactions for all configurations examined. These findings highlight the importance of finite-temperature dynamics and strain-dependent local geometry in understanding vacancy-pair stability and reconfiguration in halide perovskites.

Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.title: Disentangling Multiple Scaling Dimensions via Operator Covariance in Critical Quantum Spin Systems
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.authors: Zhi Lin, Anders W. Sandvik
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.abstract: We present a general proof of different power-law decays versus distance of the eigenvalues of two-point covariance matrices in critical lattice quantum models, allowing extraction of multiple scaling dimensions. We demonstrate the practical utility of this method in the context of a spin-1/2 chain with critical ground state described by the SU(2)_1 Wess--Zumino--Witten field theory. Using quantum Monte Carlo simulations to compute covariance matrices in different symmetry sectors, we resolve the expected relevant and marginal primary operators as well as some descendants. The covariance method can be integrated into many existing numerical schemes and promises to significantly enhance computational studies of quantum criticality.

Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.title: Critical aging and relaxation dynamics in long-range systems
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.authors: Valerio Pagni, Friederike Ihssen, Nicolò Defenu
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.abstract: We study the dynamical scaling of long-range O ( N ) models after a sudden quench to the critical temperature, using the functional renormalization group approach. We characterize both short-time aging and long-time relaxation as a function of the symmetry index N , the interaction range decay exponent σ , and the dimension d . Our results substantially improve on perturbative predictions, as demonstrated by benchmarks against Monte Carlo simulations and the large- N limit. Finally, we demonstrate that long-range systems increase the performance of critical heat engines with respect to a local active medium.

Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.title: Lefschetz-Thimble Method to the Sign Problem in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.authors: Yin-Hao Fang, Yang Qi
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.abstract: The sign problem in path integrals severely limits the application of quantum Monte Carlo methods to strongly correlated systems, whereas the Lefschetz-thimble method offers a rigorous framework to mitigate this issue. In this paper, we establish a numerical framework based on the Lefschetz thimbles for the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model. By introducing continuous auxiliary fields via the Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation, the partition function is formulated as a high-dimensional complex integral. We employ the complex Langevin equation to explore the saddle-point distribution of the effective action in the complex plane. Monte Carlo integration is then performed to compute the partition function and Green functions. Our numerical results exhibit excellent agreement with high-temperature expansions, infrared-limit solutions, and determinantal quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) simulations, confirming the validity of our framework. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our complex Langevin search successfully captures the relevant dominant saddle points governing the SYK model in the large-N limit. Our work deepens the understanding of the sign problem in the SYK model and provides a viable non-perturbative avenue for addressing sign problems in more complex strongly correlated systems.

Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.title: Topological signatures of criticality: the Ising case
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.authors: Tak-Shing Chan, Paweł Dłotko, Jacek Gulgowski, Biagio Lucini, Mateusz Masłowski, Davide Vadacchino
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.abstract: Topological properties of microscopic configurations may provide additional insight into phase transitions beyond conventional thermodynamic observables. We investigate this idea in the two-dimensional Ising model on square and triangular lattices by associating cell complexes with the positive and negative spin domains and constructing an Euler-characteristic observable from their difference. We provide the expression relating this quantity to conventional observables of the Ising model. This derivation allows us to understand its expected behavior physically. As a byproduct, we show that at any finite positive temperature the expectation of the Euler characteristic exceeds a positive, lattice-size-independent bound, hence disproving a previously suggested conjecture. Monte Carlo simulations combined with multihistogram reweighting show that this spin-odd topological observable exhibits order-parameter-like behavior near the ferromagnetic transition. Finite-size scaling of its susceptibility yields pseudocritical temperatures that converge to the known critical temperature for both lattice geometries. On the square lattice, the leading-order estimate of the critical exponent obtained from the topological observable depends more strongly on the fitting range than the magnetization estimate. This behavior is consistent with stronger subleading finite-size corrections, as supported by fits including an additional correction term. On the triangular lattice, the corresponding estimate remains consistent with the theoretical Ising value. Our study suggests that topologically defined quantities such as the Euler characteristic can provide an alternative way to locate order-disorder phase transitions in the systems considered here. Since the definition of these observables is purely geometrical, they can provide useful insights in cases in which order parameters cannot be constructed.

Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.title: Decoding SO(5) Deconfined Multicriticality: Conformal Bootstrap and Fuzzy-Sphere Spectroscopy
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.authors: Zhijin Li, Tinghong Shen
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.abstract: The nature of the deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) remains unsettled: competing explanations invoke a real multicritical conformal field theory (CFT) or pseudocriticality governed by nearby complex fixed points. We use the conformal bootstrap and fuzzy-sphere regularization to compute $SO(5)$ CFT data and compare our results with large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) data to investigate these scenarios. Using mixed correlators of the lowest vector $φ$, singlet $s$, and traceless symmetric scalar $t$, we characterize the bootstrap cone whose tip lies remarkably close to the position indicated by large-scale QMC. We extract an extensive spectrum across $SO(5)$ irreducible representations, together with operator product expansion (OPE) coefficients. We study a fuzzy-sphere realization of the $SO(5)$ nonlinear sigma model with a level-1 Wess--Zumino--Witten term. Using the special conformal generators, we identify 52 conformal primaries in a system with \(N=10\) Landau orbitals, including 31 not previously classified as primaries in the earlier fuzzy-sphere study. Symmetry projection extends fuzzy-sphere exact diagonalization to $N=12$. The bootstrap spectrum and OPE coefficients show close agreement with fuzzy-sphere data, including 16 of the newly identified primaries in channels accessible to the mixed-correlator bootstrap. The lowest $SO(5)$ singlet scalar is relevant in the bootstrap and QMC results; its fuzzy-sphere data is $Δ_s=2.816$ at $N=12$ and decreases with system size. Our results suggest that the mixed-correlator bootstrap solution represents a unitary CFT with a relevant $SO(5)$ singlet scalar and is closely connected to the QMC and fuzzy-sphere data for the DQCP. The conformal bootstrap, fuzzy-sphere, and QMC together provide comprehensive evidence for an $SO(5)$ multicritical CFT and critical data to decode the phases in two-dimensional quantum magnets.

Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.title: Micromagnetic modelling and simulation of inertial magnetization dynamics in ferromagnets
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.authors: Massimiliano d'Aquino
Monte Carlo & Computational Methods.abstract: Magnetization dynamics at sub-picosecond time scales can exhibit inertial effects beyond the conventional Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert description, giving rise to nutational motion at terahertz frequencies. Following its theoretical prediction and experimental observation in ferromagnets, magnetic inertia has attracted increasing interest for understanding and controlling ultrafast spin dynamics. In this topical review, we discuss the theoretical modelling and micromagnetic simulation of inertial magnetization dynamics in ferromagnetic nanostructures. Starting from the mechanical analogy underlying the inertial Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, we introduce its spatially inhomogeneous micromagnetic formulation and discuss its main properties, including magnetization-length conservation, angular-momentum relaxation, and the generalized free-energy balance. We then review the linear dynamics of inertial spin waves, highlighting the coexistence of GHz precessional and THz nutational branches, the inertial redshift of precessional modes, spectral linewidths, and the effects of exchange, magnetostatic interactions, confinement, curvature and torsion. Particular attention is devoted to the large-wavenumber regime, where magnetic inertia leads to a finite limiting spin-wave propagation velocity. Finally, we address frequency- and time-domain micromagnetic simulation techniques for spatially nonuniform inertial dynamics, including geometric midpoint integrators preserving the fundamental constraints and energy properties of the continuous dynamics. Applications to the excitation and propagation of ultrashort nutational spin waves and ultrafast inertial magnetization switching illustrate the role of micromagnetic modelling in connecting inertial Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert theory with experimentally accessible nanoscale magnetization dynamics.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: Scalable Bayesian Optimization for Efficient Exploration of Moire Patterns
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Panagiotis Krokidas, Christos Lazaridis, Vassilis Sioros, Efi-Maria Papia, Vassilios Constantoudis, George Giannakopoulos
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: Large materials design spaces often contain rare high-performing configurations that are difficult to identify through trial-and-error exploration or purely representative machine-learning (ML) sampling. In this work, we present FruBO, a flexible Bayesian Optimization framework for accelerating the discovery of optimal configurations in computationally demanding materials design problems. As a case study, we investigate multilayer Moiré patterns generated by the superposition of six rotated hexagonal lattices, where the objective is to identify the rotational conformation that maximizes pore-size uniformity, quantified using the Jain fairness index. The resulting benchmark contains 600,000 unique configurations and exhibits a highly skewed objective distribution, making the global optimum difficult to locate by random sampling. We compare random exploration, Gaussian Process-based Bayesian Optimization, and Bayesian Optimization using a lightweight CatBoost surrogate with committee-based uncertainty estimation. Random sampling identifies the global optimum only after 533,012 evaluations, requiring approximately 31 hours, while Gaussian Process-based BO becomes impractical due to GPU memory exhaustion after 290 acquired samples. In contrast, FruBO with CatBoost identifies the global optimum after 1,470 acquired samples and approximately 1.15 hours. These results demonstrate that scalable surrogate models can substantially improve the feasibility and efficiency of BO in large nanomaterials design spaces.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: Revisiting spin Hamiltonian parameters in a Kitaev material via Bayesian optimization of magnetization curves
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Takahiro Misawa, Ryo Tamura, Kazuyoshi Yoshimi, Youhei Yamaji

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: Physics Informed Priors for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials with Uncertainty Quantification
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: George I. Simmons, Thomas D. Swinburne, Thomas Hudson, James R. Kermode
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: Standard uncertainty quantification methods for machine learning interatomic potentials often fail to quantify the effects of model misspecification despite its prominence as a source of error. To combat this, misspecification-aware uncertainty schemes have been gaining attention, pointwise optimal parameter set regression (POPS-Regression) among them. However, no guarantees on the physicality of the posterior distribution are given and uncertainty estimates can be conservative compared to the true error. To combat this, we present a model misspecification aware scheme that builds on POPS-Regression by allowing users to specify physical priors that are enforced across the obtained ensemble of models. This allows the user to incorporate misspecification-aware uncertainties without compromising on physical properties. The scheme is applicable to any physical quantity that can be represented by a convex set of parameters and so is robust for a wide variety of static properties which can help inform dynamical simulations. Here, we demonstrate the scheme for phononic vibrations and elastic properties. The scheme is also applied to both linear and message-passing neural network potentials by exploiting the linearity available in both architectures; for neural network potentials we approximate the readout layer as a linear model based on fixed non-linear features. The versatility of the method provides an alternative to hand-crafted or active learning approaches to data-set construction to correct physical failures by adding data thus reducing the computational overhead for designing potentials for specific applications.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: Parameterized Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Efficient Simulation of Embedded Microfluidic Chip Cooling
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Weiheng Li, Zhiyao Jiang, Bai Song
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: Embedded microfluidic cooling is a promising technology for dissipating the intense heat generated by high-performance electronic chips. However, the design and optimization of such coolers impose prohibitive computational costs when using conventional numerical solvers. Here, we present a parameterized physics-informed neural network (PINN) as a deep learning framework for rapidly and accurately predicting the thermohydraulic performance of embedded manifold microchannels. By incorporating four geometric dimensions along with three spatial coordinates as the network inputs, the proposed model enables multiphysics prediction across a continuous design space. Remarkably, our predicted velocity and temperature fields differ from finite-element simulations by relative errors of only 8.1% and 5.6%, respectively, while reducing the computational time and cost by over four orders of magnitude. Key to this framework is a composite strategy combining geometric ansatz embedding, the SOAP optimizer, and a thermal-conductivity-based curriculum learning scheme, which helps overcome the convergence challenges inherent in training PINNs for complex three-dimensional flows. Notably, by leveraging a highly optimized JAX backend, the network achieves convergence on a single consumer-grade GPU in less than four hours. Our approach offers a physics-consistent, real-time surrogate model that can substantially accelerate innovations in advanced microfluidic cooling of future electronics.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: A Practitioner's Guide to Materials Theory and Computation in the Age of Big Data and Artificial Intelligence
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Jack Yang
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: Computational modelling has become a cornerstone of materials science, with advances in atomistic simulations, high-throughput computation, and artificial intelligence transforming how materials are understood, discovered, and designed. These developments build upon generations of theoretical innovations that have translated complex mathematical and physical principles into practical predictive tools. However, the growing diversity of computational methods presents challenges for practitioners seeking a coherent understanding of their theoretical foundations. Drawing upon the author's research experience, this monograph provides a practitioner-oriented, pedagogical overview of computational materials science, unified through the concepts of potential-energy landscapes and statistical sampling. It explores how these concepts underpin structural stability, phase behaviour, and electronic and magnetic properties, through a systematic treatment of empirical force fields, density-functional theory, many-body electronic-structure methods, statistical sampling, and property prediction. It further examines high-throughput workflows, materials databases, and the probabilistic foundations of artificial intelligence. Particular emphasis is placed on atomistic representations, graph neural networks, and generative models, highlighting the roles of symmetry, group theory, differential geometry, and stochastic processes in modern materials modelling. By connecting established physical theories with emerging data-driven approaches, this monograph offers a unified perspective on computational materials science and identifies opportunities and challenges toward physics-informed, efficient, and reliable materials discovery.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: Systematic Evaluation of Training Data Generation Strategies for Machine Learning-Based Molecular and Materials Property Prediction
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Minh Nghia Nguyen, Beate Paulus, Akhil S. Nair
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: Machine-learning (ML) models for molecular and materials property prediction are often trained on large datasets curated through arbitrary or generic sampling strategies. Such approaches can lead to the over- or under-representation of regions of chemical and materials space that are most relevant to the prediction task. An important challenge is therefore how to efficiently curate training data to maximize predictive performance while minimising the number of labelled examples required. Here, we systematically compare training data acquisition strategies for molecular and materials property prediction, ranging from random sampling to various active learning approaches. We evaluate their performance across different model classes, representations, datasets, and target properties. Our results show that the effectiveness of data acquisition strategies depend strongly on the interplay between the model, dataset, and prediction task, although uncertainty-based sampling generally outperforms alternative strategies. Based on these findings, we derive guidelines for selecting data acquisition strategies under a given labelling budget.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: Machine learning techniques for understanding pattern formation and self-assembly in active colloidal systems
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Josue D de la Cruz, Rubicel Trujillo-Acatitla, Edson Mendoza Flores, Haret C Rosu, Daniel Ignacio Salgado-Blanco
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: Active colloidal matter provides a rich setting for the emergence of nonequilibrium patterns, dynamic aggregates, and self-assembled structures. Understanding how such organization arises from microscopic interactions, fluctuations, and sustained external driving remains a central challenge in soft-matter physics. This is largely because traditional theoretical and computational approaches often struggle with nonlinear dynamics, multiscale behavior, and high-dimensional parameter spaces. In this context, machine learning (ML) is increasingly used to identify relevant order parameters, classify dynamical regimes, predict emergent structures, infer assembly pathways, and guide the design and control of target states. This review examines how ML methods are incorporated into the study of pattern formation and self-assembly across both equilibrium and active colloidal systems. The discussion is organized around the analysis and representation of data pertaining to complex nonequilibrium systems, the prediction of dynamical and structural outcomes, the inference of latent variables and assembly pathways, and the design or control of target states through generative models andreinforcement learning strategies. We also discuss hybrid approaches that incorporate physical constraints to improve interpretability, robustness, and generalization. By focusing on the interplay between machine learning and nonequilibrium soft-matter physics, we highlight both the opportunities and the open challenges of the field, including the connection between learned representations and physical variables, limited extrapolation capability across state space, and the need for reproducible benchmarks and high-quality datasets. Overall, we argue that ML is emerging as an important complement to theory and simulation in the study of active colloidal self-assembly, not as a replacement for physical modeling, but as a means to accelerate discovery and deepen understanding of emergent nonequilibrium organization.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: Defects and Structural Evolution in CrSBr: Machine-Learning Potentials for Atomistic Simulations
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Arsalan Hashemi, Daniil Kruklinskii, Xiaoya Chang, Tapio Ala-Nissila, Mikko Karttunen, Arkady V. Krasheninnikov, Mahdi Ghorbani-Asl
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: The layered van der Waals semiconductor CrSBr combines intrinsic magnetic order with semiconducting and optical properties, making it a promising material for multifunctional electronic and photonic applications. Understanding how defects and structural transformations affect its properties under experimentally relevant conditions, however, remains challenging for first-principles simulations due to the relevant length and time scales. Here, we develop and benchmark machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for the Cr-S-Br system, enabling large-scale atomistic simulations of CrSBr with accuracy approaching that of density functional theory (DFT). The charge-aware variant qNEP achieves near-DFT accuracy in predicting lattice constants, formation enthalpies, vacancy energetics, and the anisotropic pressure response of o-CrSBr. Nudged elastic band calculations reveal that pre-existing S vacancies lower the Cr Frenkel-pair migration barrier by up to 1.1 eV, providing an atomistic mechanism for beam-induced Cr redistribution and structural transformations. Displacement threshold calculations further show that Br is the most susceptible species to electron-beam-induced displacement, identifying the relative ease of removing different atomic species. Together, these results establish a validated computational framework for investigating atomic-scale disorder and structural transformations in CrSBr, providing a basis for defect engineering in materials for future magneto-optoelectronic applications.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: Physics-Guided Crystal Structure Elucidation from Powder X-Ray Diffraction with Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Yunsung Lim, Seungwoo Hwang, Seungwu Han
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: Determining unique atomic coordinates from powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) remains challenging because peak overlap, weak scattering from light elements, limited scattering contrast between elements with similar atomic numbers, and experimental noise render the inverse problem underdetermined. Here, we present XCAPE (XRD-Constrained Accelerated Prediction Engine), a crystal structure prediction (CSP) framework that integrates experimentally derived composition, unit cell parameters, space group, and PXRD data into a symmetry-aware evolutionary search. XCAPE explores Wyckoff-site configurations using tailored mutation operations, evaluates candidates by both energetic stability and diffraction agreement, and accelerates geometry optimization using a universal machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP). The framework recovered 71 of 77 database-derived benchmark structures (92.2%) from simulated PXRD patterns and all 12 reference structures from experimental PXRD patterns. It further identified 12 candidate structure assignments that are consistent with experimental PXRD patterns, lack matching entries in the Inorganic Crystal Structure Database (ICSD), and are thermodynamically competitive at the MLIP level. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations showed that 10 of these 12 candidates lie within 10 meV/atom of the convex hull. By bridging experimental diffraction data and physically plausible atomistic models, XCAPE can provide structural insight into previously unresolved materials and support accelerated materials discovery in automated research workflows.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: Application of Pretrained Universal Machine Learning Force-Fields for Phase Transitions Prediction in ZrO2
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Rajan Khadka, Axel van de Walle, Patrick Tepesch
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: Pretrained universal machine-learning force fields can reduce the cost of finite-temperature molecular dynamics relative to density functional theory. However, most benchmarks test only static properties and do not assess whether these models reproduce the correct phase-transition sequence. Here, we benchmark ten open-source universal machine-learning force fields for zirconia (ZrO$_2$) using phonon dispersion calculations and variable-cell isothermal-isobaric molecular dynamics. Zirconia is a useful test because it has three thermodynamically stable crystalline phases prior to melting, following the sequence monoclinic-tetragonal-cubic. Four models reproduce this sequence: 7net-l3i5, MatterSim-v1.0.0-1M, MACE-mpa, and MACE-D3. Models with orthorhombic-tetragonal energy errors above about 10 meV/atom (7net-0, CHGNet, and MACE) instead produce an orthorhombic intermediate and predict monoclinic-orthorhombic-tetragonal-cubic-liquid upon heating. ORB-based models fail to sustain stable variable-cell dynamics because their phonon frequencies are compressed by 30-60% relative to the density functional theory reference. Across all ten models, two ground-state diagnostics predict finite-temperature behavior. Relative polymorph energetics should agree with the matched density functional theory reference within about 6 meV/atom, and the phonon spectrum should not show systematic softening. These diagnostics are practical screening metrics for assessing pretrained force fields for phase-transition predictions.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: Weight-Space Programming for Materials Science
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Sk Md Ahnaf Akif Alvi, Raymundo Arróyave
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: A materials discovery campaign often begins with almost no measurements of the property it is searching for, and the models that rank candidates or screen the output of a generator then have to be built from those first few labels. Following recent work on weight-space programming, in which a language model writes the weights of a small network directly as text, we show that a general-purpose model, given the task in words, the names of the inputs and a network of 16 hidden units with every weight set to zero, can provide this starting point by filling in all of the weights from what it has learned about materials. With no labels, the networks of the strongest model rank experimental alloys at Spearman co-efficient = 0.64 to 0.79, where the best of five simple descriptors reaches 0.47 to 0.62. They rank the bulk modulus of crystals added during generative discovery loops at 0.95, where the inverse volume per atom reaches 0.89, and 35 phase-equilibrium targets computed with Thermo-Calc at a mean of 0.67, close to the 0.70 of an extrapolation from calculated binary and ternary data. As the prior mean of a Gaussian process they raise the ranking at five labels from 0.35 to 0.69 on alloys and from 0.15 to 0.95 on crystals, and they lower the regret of Bayesian optimization significantly on 4 of 5 experimental tasks and on 13 to 16 of 33 computed targets, depending on how multiple tests are corrected, without raising it significantly on any. The same networks also serve as the mean of a Bayesian neural network and as a screen for the samples of two crystal generators, where they do as well as standard models trained on 400 labeled structures. The gain is confined to the first tens of labels and to targets that no rule or sub-system extrapolation already ranks.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: Grain-size distribution characterization from single-shot x-ray diffraction using hierarchical Bayesian multi-emitter analysis
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Hyun Sang Park, Gannon Murray, Rohit Berlia, David Elbert, Timothy P. Weihs, Todd C. Hufnagel
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: The distribution of grain sizes in a polycrystalline material can be determined from a 2D x-ray diffraction pattern by counting and characterizing diffraction spots, so long as the spots are discrete. This approach breaks down if there is substantial overlap of the reflections due to either a large number of grains in the scattering volume or crowding of spots caused by crystallographic texture. As a result, the spot-counting approach to grain size determination is infeasible for many situations of practical interest. We address this limitation by applying hierarchical probabilistic learning using a reversible-jump Markov chain Monte Carlo framework to jointly infer diffraction spot populations and their intensity distributions. Using synthetic diffraction patterns, we show how this hierarchical model allows recovery of diffraction peak intensities across a wide variety of grain-size distributions and crystallographic textures. From the recovered peak intensities we infer grain-size distributions themselves and characterize the regimes of grain size and texture for which this approach is practical. Finally, we demonstrate the application of our technique by comparing grain-size distributions in Cu-Ti alloy specimens obtained from 2D x-ray diffraction patterns with those from electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD). This method of grain-size distribution determination is expected to be particularly useful in the context of high-throughput experimentation, where the minimal sample preparation requirements and short exposure times of single-shot x-ray diffraction are substantial advantages relative to microscopy techniques.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: Machine learning interatomic potentials and orientational defects in polymers
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Arnold Kiv, Volodymyr Soloviev, Andrii Tuzhykov, Andrii Bielinskyi, Taras Kavetskyy, Nataliia Hoivanovych, Ondrej Šauša, Jaroslav Rusnák, Helena Švajdlenková, Jolita Ostrauskaite, Mykola Slusarenko
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: Photopolymerization of acrylated epoxidized soybean oil (AESO) is a convenient model of a self-organizing process in a soft, bio-based material: ultraviolet light starts a free-radical chain reaction, the growing network releases heat, and the mobility of molecular groups changes on several time scales at once. We follow this process from two sides. Experimentally, the real and imaginary parts of the dielectric permittivity of an AESO:VDM (1:0.5) mixture with 3 mol% of the photoinitiator DMPA were recorded at 500-5000 Hz under an intermittent on/off illumination protocol, and the resulting time series were analysed with a sliding-window Shannon entropy and the Grassberger-Procaccia correlation integral. Both measures show that short light pulses at the start of curing trigger strongly correlated, collective relaxation, which fades as the network forms, leaving only localized reorientations active. We describe these reorientations as orientational defects and quantify their energetics with the MACE-OFF23 machine learning interatomic potential, using relaxed dihedral scans of five rotational modes ($α$, $α/β$, $β$, $γ$, $δ$) of an AESO fragment. Compared with density functional theory (DFT) reference profiles, MACE reproduces the shape of all five profiles (Pearson $r=0.95$-$0.98$) and the hierarchy of barriers - from 2.9 eV for the constrained main-chain rotation, through 0.54-0.81 eV for the acrylate rotations, to 0.16-0.18 eV for the methyl and 0.06 eV for the hydroxyl rotation - while underestimating the barrier heights by 3-20%. A simple Arrhenius estimate shows that the acrylate rotations are the modes closest to the frequency window of the dielectric measurement.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: IANN: A Unified Framework for Equivariant InterAtomic Neural Networks with User-Friendly Implementation
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Changzhi Ai, Xueping Qin, Dimosthenis Sokaras, Frank Abild-Pedersen, Johannes Voss
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) now approach density functional theory (DFT) accuracy at a fraction of its cost, but the practical benefit is limited by software fragmentation: each state-of-the-art architecture is released as a separate codebase, with its own data format, configuration system, training loop and molecular-dynamics interface. Comparing two architectures on the same dataset, or moving a trained model into a production simulation, therefore requires substantial re-engineering. We introduce IANN (InterAtomic Neural Network), an open-source PyTorch framework that reimplements equivariant graph neural networks - PaiNN, NequIP, MACE, Allegro, EquiformerV2, EquiformerV3 and UMA - behind a unified data object, a unified trainer and a single deployment route, so that the architecture is a one-word change in a configuration dictionary. Forces, stresses and virials are obtained for every architecture from one analytic differentiation of the energy with respect to the edge vectors of the atomic graph, exact under periodic boundary conditions. Distributed training is configured automatically from the SLURM, PBS or MPI environment, so the same script runs unchanged from a workstation to a multi-node GPU allocation. Self-describing checkpoints serve directly as ASE calculators, as ensembles reporting uncertainties, or as TorchScript models run inside LAMMPS through bundled C++ pair styles with single- and multi-GPU inference. Trained on a common dataset of millions of structures, the architectures can be compared under identical conditions. We further release PaiNN foundation models trained on 41.9 million curated DFT structures from MPtrj, Alexandria, OMat24, MatPES, OC20, OC22, OC25, MPr2SCAN and MatPESr2SCAN, spanning the PBE, RPBE and r2SCAN functionals. Additionally, IANN provides an agent interface to facilitate integration with autonomous agents.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: Scaling laws in machine learning on non-ideal experimental data enable inverse design of radiative-cooling coatings
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Kunihiko Shizume, Jiawen Li, Yaerim Lee, Yuki Asano, Tuwei Liao, Koji Tsuda, Junichiro Shiomi
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: Materials informatics increasingly targets multicomponent materials, yet experimental datasets inevitably contain non-ideal variations arising from imperfect uniformity and reproducibility in composition, coating formation, and measurement. Whether machine-learning prediction accuracy scales with amount of data under these conditions remains unclear. Here, we develop an automated platform that produced and optically characterized 11,520 radiative-cooling coatings spanning nine material and processing parameters. Forward and inverse neural networks, and a spectrum-conditioned diffusion model were trained on subsets of 10 to 10,000 samples. All models exhibited power-law scaling, with prediction errors decreasing with dataset size. Experimental inverse-design validation showed that larger datasets produced spectra closer to a broadband-emitter target. The diffusion model generated multiple candidate parameter sets, allowing selection among alternative solutions based on ease of fabrication, cost, and scalability. These results demonstrate predictable learning-curve scaling in non-ideal experimental data and provide a quantitative basis for estimating the benefit of additional experimental data, and thus the cost-effectiveness of materials-informatics.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: A Machine-learning-aided Workflow for Sampling Small Polaron Dynamics in Energy Materials
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Tavinder Singh, Harald Oberhofer
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: One of the defining characteristics of most energy materials, used as e.g.~battery electrodes, photovoltaics, or photocatalysts, is their ability conduct charges such as electrons and holes. The exact mechanism of this conductivity depends on the material, but is often dominated by the existence of mobile small polarons, i.e.~electrons or holes strongly localised through the polarisation of their environment. Computationally, small polarons can be treated with reasonably accuracy through the use of self-interaction corrected or hybrid density functional theory (DFT) together with local geometry optimisation. Similar approaches can be employed to determine the energy barriers to movement of the polarons through hopping. Unfortunately, realistic energy materials tend have very large numbers of symmetry inequivalent polaronic configurations and correspondingly large numbers of hopping barriers, making them hard to tackle explicitly. In this work we therefore extend the computational reach of DFT calculations with machine-learned (ML) surrogate models, which then feed into a kinetic model to quantitatively estimate the conductivity of a battery anode material (Li$_4$Ti$_5$O$_12$ or LTO) at realistic, defected conditions. We calculate the conductivity at room temperature to be 6.7 $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ S/cm which lies well in the experimental range. To this end, we only needed a total of 154 polaron barrier calculations, out of 3649 symmetry inequivalent ones, achieving an over 20-fold increase of computational efficiency. Overall, our work demonstrates how DFT-trained ML surrogates can be used to quantitatively and efficiently sample the dynamics of small polarons in energy materials.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: Bridging surface dynamics and phase transitions in CsPbI 3 perovskite with machine-learning force fields and dispersion interactions
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Iryna Knysh, Anton Charkin-Gorbulin, Claudio Quarti, David Beljonne, Igor Poltavsky, Alexandre Tkatchenko
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: In the rapidly evolving field of machine learning (ML) for atomistic simulations of materials and molecules, achieving transferability across different systems remains a key challenge. In this contribution, we demonstrate a case of transfer learning in which an ML model trained exclusively on surface slab data of the cubic ( α ) phase of CsPbI 3 perovskite can reproduce the key features of the dynamic behavior for different phases of the bulk material. Using an equivariant message-passing network (MACE) architecture, we construct an efficient ML force field trained on a dataset obtained from molecular dynamics simulations of a CsPbI 3 slab. The resulting model yields stable and reliable trajectories for both slab and bulk, reproducing the experimentally observed phase transitions of CsPbI 3 . We demonstrate that pairwise dispersion methods (TS/D3) mispredict the correct phase of CsPbI 3 bulk at ambient conditions, while more advanced approaches (MBD-NL/rVV10) recover both the experimentally observed phase sequence with increasing temperature (orthorhombic–tetragonal–cubic) and the corresponding phase-transition temperatures. Through a local analysis of the rotational driving forces acting on PbI 6 octahedra, we show that this discrepancy can be traced to the strong sensitivity of Cs and I atomic forces to the treatment of van der Waals (vdW) dispersion. Overall, our results demonstrate that surface–slab datasets augmented with an accurate treatment of vdW dispersion provide a robust foundation for constructing transferable machine-learning force fields that consistently describe both surface and bulk behavior across multiple length scales.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: Machine-learning charge density for electronic materials and devices simulation
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Qingyun Zhang, Yang Hu, Aixia Zhang, Zehua Sun, Jiawei Yan, Xiaohao Zhou, Wei Lu, Youqi Ke
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: We present a machine-learning (ML) charge density model, DeltaChargeNet, integrated with the full-potential tight-binding muffin-tin orbital (FP-TB-MTO) method for electronic structure and quantum transport simulations of materials and devices. The ML model predicts electron density from atomic structures with low linear-scaling cost, while FP-TB-MTO provides an accurate tight-binding representation of the system Hamiltonian. To achieve high-fidelity ML density for complex devices with interfaces and disorder, we train an equivariant graph convolutional network to predict $Δρ$-the difference between DFT and atomic superposition densities-under a charge neutrality constraint required for inhomogeneous systems. A secondary ML residual charge model compensates for errors in the primary $Δρ$ model. The predicted density is then used within the full-relativistic FP-TB-MTO framework combined with the non-equilibrium Green's function method. We validate our method on bulk HgCdTe disordered alloys (including vacancy defects) and Au/HgCdTe/Au disordered devices. The maximum band energy error is below 10 meV for bulk HgCdTe. For devices, the charge neutrality constraint suppresses long-wavelength charge bias that would otherwise distort the electrostatic potential by 0.68-1.88 eV near the device center, while residual compensation corrects the remaining 0.16-0.46 eV potential mismatch, essential for reproducing the correct potential barrier profile. Together, these corrections reproduce the layer-resolved potential, including interface steps and bulk-like plateaus, within 0.1 eV of fully self-consistent DFT. Finally, we demonstrate quantum transport in a 11220-atom infrared detector. By combining first-principles accuracy with linear-scaling inference, DeltaChargeNet enables large-scale device simulations without the full DFT self-consistent field loop.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: High-Fidelity In Silico Dataset of Ordered Binary and Ternary MXenes with Predictive Synthesis Guidance
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Ahmed H. Biby, Charles B. Musgrave
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: Despite their promise, the targeted synthesis of novel MXenes remains challenging due to their vast structural and compositional space and the lack of reliable stability descriptors that account for synthesis conditions. To address this gap, we utilized density functional theory (DFT) with the r$^2$SCAN functional to develop a high-fidelity dataset of 1,040 ordered binary and ternary bare delaminated MXenes, including mono-transition metal MXenes, in-plane ordered double-transition metal MXenes, in-plane ordered metal-divacancy MXenes, and out-of-plane ordered double-transition-metal MXenes. For each structure, we calculated formation and decomposition Gibbs energies, decomposition products, layer symmetry groups, and energies above the hull. We find that all MXenes are thermodynamically inaccessible under equilibrium conditions. However, 115 predominantly carbide MXenes become thermodynamically stabilized at elevated temperatures (500--2000 K), and 23 are stabilized under high pressure (10 GPa). Additionally, three MXenes in the Mn--Fe--C chemical space are stabilized within an experimentally feasible range of carbon chemical potentials. These findings reveal stability trends across the MXene space and identify synthesis strategies that can guide experimental efforts. Our dataset provides a robust foundation for developing machine-learned stability descriptors and for guiding experimental efforts toward novel MXene discovery. By identifying synthesizable candidates along with their synthesis conditions, this work bridges a critical gap in data-driven approaches to MXene discovery and lays the foundation for future autonomous experimental workflows.

Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.title: A Geometry-Guided Feature-Space Framework for Interpretable Unsupervised 4D-STEM Analysis of Complex Multiphase Materials
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.authors: Arda Genc, Daniel A. Bolden, Albert Nguyen, Daniel S. Gianola, Ravit Silverstein
Machine Learning & Bayesian Optimization.abstract: Rapid, high-fidelity analysis of four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) datasets from heterogeneous materials remains challenging because coexisting phases, orientation variants, local strain gradients, and intrinsic TEM thin-foil effects produce complex, overlapping diffraction signatures. Here, we present a machine-learning (ML) framework that combines physics-informed geometric descriptors with weighted high-dimensional embeddings to identify latent structural patterns with minimal prior knowledge. By constructing a regularized descriptor space before embedding and density-based clustering, the method improves cluster stability, suppresses noise-driven fragmentation, and reduces sensitivity to embedding hyperparameters. Spatial weighting produced the largest stability gain, increasing median cluster persistence from 0.04 to 0.55 while reducing the noise fraction from approximately 22% to 0%. Rotation weighting increased DBCV from 0.80 to 0.92, although the noise fraction rose from 0.2% to 1.0%, highlighting a trade-off between improved density separation and noise rejection. We validate the framework on two benchmark systems: Si/Si$_x$Ge$_{1-x}$ epitaxial layers with continuous lattice variation and deformation, and multiphase Ti-Nb alloys containing distinct phases and orientation variants. Comparisons with a pretrained vanilla autoencoder and model-free pattern vectorization show that the physics-informed geometric descriptor provides higher cluster fidelity, greater interpretability, and substantially lower dimensionality.

Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.title: Exact Parent Hamiltonians for Partially Magnetized Chiral Spin Liquids
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.authors: Xin Shen, Guangyue Ji, Jie Wang
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.abstract: Chiral spin liquids (CSLs) are paradigmatic fractionalized phases, yet simple exact parent Hamiltonians for them remain scarce. In this work, we construct exact spin parent Hamiltonians for partially magnetized CSLs realizing various bosonic topological orders. Our construction relies on an exact Hubbard-type parent Hamiltonian for bosonic lattice fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states, valid at arbitrary repulsive interaction strengths. Taking the on-site repulsion to infinity and applying local boson-spin mappings yields exact parent Hamiltonians for the CSLs. Our two-spin construction generalizes the Kalmeyer-Laughlin spin Hamiltonian to a broader class of bosonic FQH model states, including Abelian states and non-Abelian parton states. We derive controlled microscopic realizations of these two-spin Hamiltonians via second-order superexchange in generalized spinful Hofstadter-Hubbard models with tailored hoppings and interactions. With more general local constraints and interactions, boson-spin mappings yield exact higher-spin and multispin parent Hamiltonians for partially magnetized CSLs.

Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.title: Why "quantum spin liquids" are quantum singlet liquids
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.authors: Sergey Syzranov, Arthur P. Ramirez
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.abstract: The last couple of decades have seen enormous theoretical and experimental research efforts aimed at finding quantum spin liquids (QSLs) in geometrically frustrated (GF) magnetic materials. Experimental demonstrations of QSLs are challenging due to the indirect character of possible QSL signatures and the presence of impurities in materials, which may destroy or obscure a QSL. At the same time, the theoretical literature often lacks consensus about the ground states of quantum spins on even the simplest GF magnetic lattices. We summarize experimental evidence that in the impurity-free limit, available GF magnetic materials that do not develop magnetic order at low temperatures would form {\it a quantum singlet liquid}, i.e. a disordered state of non-magnetic excitations. We further confirm with theoretical arguments the existence of such a singlet liquid and its gapless character in materials with half-integer spins per primitive magnetic cell. Such a liquid manifests itself in the thermodynamics of GF magnets while having no magnetic features at low temperatures.

Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.title: Competing Magnetic Orders and Continuously Varying Exponents in $U(1)$ Spin Liquids
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.authors: Vira Shyta, Flavio S. Nogueira
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.abstract: Unequal couplings to a common emergent gauge field provide a continuous way to tune competing magnetic instabilities in an effective description of $U(1)$ spin-liquid mixtures. We study this mechanism in quantum electrodynamics in 2+1 dimensions with two families of four-component Dirac fermions. Combining a leading large-$N$ treatment with Schwinger--Dyson equations, we obtain chiral condensates representing Néel order in the two sectors. At fixed fermion number, the coupling ratio $κ=e_2^2/e_1^2$ controls which condensates develop. Depending on $N$, the phases with a single condensate are connected through either coexistence or a finite interval in which both fermion families remain gapless. The mass-generation thresholds are reciprocal, and the fermion gaps close with Miransky essential singularities. The renormalization group flow has a circular line of fixed points parametrized by the invariant ratio $κ$. At the calculated order, gauge-invariant staggered magnetization correlations have continuously varying exponents in the gapless regime, while the exponent for correlations between the two sectors is independent of $κ$. These results connect the competition between magnetic orders to a continuous family of critical theories and identify magnetic correlation signatures of the intervening gapless regime.

Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.title: Nonlinear Interaction and Topological Selection Rules in two Skyrmion Merging: Emergence of Skyrmionium Textures
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.authors: M. Al Busaidi, T. Hakioglu, R. Sbiaa
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.abstract: The nonlinear interaction of closely spaced magnetic skyrmions remains poorly understood, particularly the conditions governing their merger into a single skyrmion or a stable skyrmionium. Here, we investigate the merging dynamics of two Néel skyrmions using analytical modelling and micromagnetic simulations based on Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics. We examine the effects of exchange, Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, anisotropy, and magnetostatic energies by varying the initial separation, polarity, winding number, and skyrmion size. Our results reveal a topological selection rule: skyrmions with identical polarity and opposite winding numbers form a stable skyrmionium at intermediate overlap, while all other configurations relax into a single skyrmion. We also identify a critical radius below which the skyrmionium collapses, showing that its formation requires both the appropriate topology and a minimum size. Energy analysis reveals that the transition involves cooperative relaxation of exchange frustration and redistribution of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya and magnetostatic energies, leading to a double-domain-wall structure. The resulting skyrmionium exhibits persistent breathing oscillations around an equilibrium radius, confirming its dynamical stability as a metastable state. These findings establish a predictive framework for controlling skyrmion merging and provide design guidelines for engineering skyrmionium textures in chiral magnetic nanostructures.

Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.title: From RuP$_3$SiO$_{11}$ to Ideal Geometry: Parallel-Face Octahedra for Kitaev-Dominated Interactions
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.authors: Do Hoon Kiem, Satoshi Okamoto, Tom Berlijn
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.abstract: RuP$_3$SiO$_{11}$ has recently been identified as a Kitaev spin liquid candidate via neutron scattering. To assess its proximity to the Kitaev limit, we perform \textit{ab initio} calculations of magnetic interactions, finding good agreement for the Kitaev and off-diagonal exchanges, while the Heisenberg exchange is ferromagnetic rather than the experimentally fitted antiferromagnetic one. We also identify a sizable antiferromagnetic out-of-plane exchange not captured in previous analyses. Extending the study to eight substitutional analogs in the $MT_3Q$O$_{11}$ family ($M$ = Ru, Os; $T$ = P, As; $Q$= Si, Ge), we observe strong variations in magnetic interactions, highlighting the tunability of this materials class. Finally, inspired by RuP$_3$SiO$_{11}$, which exhibits a near parallel-face octahedral arrangement, we compare idealized geometries and show that the parallel-face configuration yields a Kitaev-dominated regime, suggesting a new structural route to the Kitaev limit.

Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.title: Mixed-Sign Kitaev Exchange in Jahn-Teller-Distorted CrI$_2$
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.authors: Shiyan Gao, Zekuo Yang, Chuanhang Chen, Zefeng Chen, Lianchuang Li, Hongjun Xiang, Changsong Xu
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.abstract: Kitaev couplings with ferromagnetic (FM) or antiferromagnetic (AFM) character shape magnetic frustration and phases differently in real materials, yet their coexistence within a single material remains unexplored. Here, we propose Jahn-Teller distortion as a route to realizing such coexistence on inequivalent bonds. First-principles calculations identify monolayer CrI$_2$ as such a system, with AFM and FM Kitaev couplings on the short and long bonds, respectively. These opposite signs are robust against variations in Hubbard $U$, functionals, and strain. A minimal tight-binding model links this sign contrast to Jahn-Teller-split $t_{2g}$ orbitals and their hopping to $e_g$ orbitals. We further adopt the cluster expansion method and develop a realistic machine-learned spin Hamiltonian, which reproduces the experimentally observed proper-screw geometry and propagation direction and reveals highly nonuniform spin rotation, with turning angles ranging from $48.0^\circ$ to $93.9^\circ$. Both proper-screw anisotropy and strong anharmonic spin rotation arise from the mixed-sign Kitaev interaction. These findings not only establish Jahn-Teller distortion as a microscopic route to mixed-sign Kitaev exchange, but also open a new avenue for exploring novel magnetic phases.

Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.title: Potts Order Preempts Emergence of 2-Form U(1) Spin Liquidity in Three-Dimensional Spin Vorticity Models
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.authors: Michael D. Burke, Mohid U. Farooqi, Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Michel J. P. Gingras
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) spin vorticity models (SVMs) have been proposed to realize an exotic 2-form U(1) classical spin liquid (CSL), characterized by a zero-curl constraint, string excitations, and deconfined fluctuating membranes. A previous numerical study [PRB 111, 064417 (2025)] uncovered a puzzle in the pyrochlore lattice SVM: despite exhibiting pinch points characteristic of a U(1) spin liquid, it also develops weak all-in--all-out (AIAO) order. Here, we show that the emergence of the 2-form CSL in 3D SVMs is preempted by an intrinsic instability towards entropy-driven height locking. We establish this by resolving the ground state constraints using a height mapping, which we further relate to a 3-state Potts antiferromagnet. This identifies the pyrochlore's weak AIAO order as permutationally symmetric sublattice (PSS) order, albeit with an exceptionally weak locking strength. We extend the SVM to lattices of corner-sharing octahedra and cubes, where we identify the alternative broken-sublattice-symmetry (BSS) order, a hidden order without magnetic Bragg peaks coexisting with collective paramagnetism. All three models undergo a 3D Ising transition consistent with a symmetry-allowed locking potential in the coarse-grained height theory. The spin liquid persists over intermediate length and temperature scales, but a critical Coulomb ground state ensemble fails to materialize, its correlations cut off by the finite locking length. These findings illustrate how microscopic constraints can determine the ultimate stability of emergent gauge theories in frustrated spin systems.

Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.title: Optical writing of Dzyaloshinskii Néel-type skyrmions
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.authors: Dinar Khusyainov, Lukas Körber, Sheng Li, Rein Liefferink, Thibaud Denneulin, András Kovács, Fabian Kammerbauer, Robert Frömter, Mathias Kläui, Dmytro Afanasiev, Alexey Kimel, Johan H. Mentink, Rafal E. Dunin-Borkowski, Theo Rasing
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.abstract: Ultrashort laser pulses offer a route to write nanoscale topological magnetic textures for information processing. Magnetic skyrmions are prototypical examples, yet optically generating them with controlled position, type, and, in particular, chirality remains challenging. This challenge arises because magnetic dipolar interactions, which often drive skyrmion formation, preserve the degeneracy between opposite chiralities, leaving no uniquely selected spin configuration. Here, we show that in an ultrathin Co/Pt film, sequences of picosecond circularly polarized laser pulses can write Néel-type, fixed-chirality skyrmions stabilized solely by the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. Combining Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and magneto-optical microscopy, we comprehensively reconstruct their internal spin structure across multiple length scales, ranging from nanometres to micrometers. Using asymmetric skyrmion-expansion measurements, we determined the sign and magnitude of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and identified the written chirality. Our findings connect deterministic optical writing with the controlled spin structure of skyrmions, advancing optical control of topological textures for opto-spintronic applications.

Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.title: Conformal defects in a quasi-one-dimensional Kitaev chain: an exactly parametrized Ising defect line and a relevant vacancy
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.authors: R. L. Silva. R. C. Silva, A. R. Pereira
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.abstract: The quasi-one-dimensional Kitaev chain of coupled hexagonal plaquettes recently introduced by Majumder is exactly solvable in terms of free Majorana fermions and undergoes a topological transition at the exchange anisotropy $J_x=\sqrt{2}\,J$. By eliminating the two-coordinated sites of each plaquette we reduce the zero-energy problem to a uniform Majorana chain, which yields the critical point, a single Majorana cone at $k=0$ (hence an Ising critical point with central charge $c=\tfrac12$), and closed forms for every defect quantity that follows. A weakened inter-plaquette bond $λJ_x$ is an exactly marginal defect with transmission $T=4λ^2/(1+λ^2)^2$ at low energy, that is, $T=\sin^2 2φ$ with $\tanφ=λ$: the bond traverses the ferromagnetic defect line of the Ising conformal field theory from the transparent point to the cut chain, and we give its exact energy dependence on the lattice. The intra-plaquette bonds land on the same line with different parametrizations: a $y$ or $z$ bond has $\tanφ=(1+λ)/2$ and covers only $T\in[0.64,1]$, because the plaquette provides a parallel path, whereas an $x$ bond has $\tanφ=(1+λ)/2λ$ and covers the strong-link half of the line, $φ\in(π/4,π/2)$. The identification is closed by an independent observable: the coefficient of $\ln L$ in the entanglement entropy across the defect follows the conformal-field-theory function $σ(\sqrt T)/2$ of Brehm and Brunner to within $0.4\%$ along the whole line, with no adjustable parameter. A vacancy behaves in the opposite way. It never binds a plaquette flux, because plaquettes share no sites, but it leaves its singly bonded neighbor as a conserved classical spin whose dangling Majorana is a zero-energy resonance.

Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.title: Constraints on the volume enclosed by Fermi surfaces
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.authors: Subir Sachdev
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.abstract: A fundamental property of a Fermi liquid (FL) is that the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by $ρ$, the total density of electrons. In a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FL*), the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by the same expression after $ρ$ has been shifted by a quantized amount, most commonly to $ρ-1$ (we assume spin rotation invariance, for simplicity). The FL* shift is related to the quantized symmetry fractionalization data of a quantum spin liquid, whose fractionalized spinon excitations are present alongside the Fermi surface quasiparticles. In this review article, we establish the FL* Fermi volume by generalizing the original Luttinger proof for FL to parton gauge theories of the quantum spin liquid and FL*. We also discuss Oshikawa's flux insertion arguments for FL, and their extension to FL*, including a discussion of gapless spin liquids.

Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.title: Non-Abelian Hall Effects of Flavor-Waves in $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ Skyrmions
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.authors: Carlos Saji, Eduardo Saavedra, Alvaro S. Nunez, Roberto E. Troncoso
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.abstract: We investigate the collective excitations of isolated and crystalline $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ skyrmions in a two-dimensional triangular-lattice spin-1 magnet. Within an $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ coherent-state framework, fluctuations of the magnetic dipole and quadrupole moments are described by two coupled bosonic flavors. In a uniform spin-polarized state, these flavors can be identified with single-spin-flip and double-spin-flip excitations, whereas a nonuniform $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ texture mixes their character. We formulate the corresponding bosonic Bogoliubov--de Gennes problem and examine the matrix-valued gauge connection governing flavor-wave propagation. For isolated skyrmions, the calculated spectrum contains localized modes, and the scattering dynamics exhibit transverse deflection accompanied by isospin precession. For a numerically relaxed skyrmion crystal, we obtain collective-mode bands with nonzero Chern numbers and calculate the associated thermal Hall response. These findings illustrate how projective magnetic textures couple multipolar excitations to non-Abelian transport and topological band phenomena.

Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.title: Steering Skyrmion Diffusion with Chiral Molecules
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.authors: Palina Shaban, Ulrich Pototschnig, Gulnaz Rakhmanova, Mikhail Lemeshko, Ragheed Alhyder
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.abstract: Chiral molecules adsorbed on a magnetic film interact with its magnetization and can thereby alter the thermal motion of magnetic skyrmions. Here we develop a theoretical model in which an aligned layer of tilted molecules modifies the interfacial magnetic interactions according to its handedness. Within this model a skyrmion responds only to spatial variations of the coupling, so a uniform layer leaves its position unaffected, whereas boundaries and coverage gradients exert forces on it. Near a chiral region, these forces deflect the skyrmion transversely in a direction that reverses between enantiomers, which provides a direct signature of the chiral interaction. In extended periodic patterns, the same forces reshape the long-time diffusion, suppressing it in the direction in which the potential varies and enhancing it in the perpendicular direction. The net effect on the mean diffusion is set by the balance between the gyrotropic and dissipative responses of the skyrmion, as we show exactly for one-dimensional landscapes. Stochastic micromagnetic simulations and collective-coordinate calculations confirm these predictions and show how molecular orientation, spatial patterning, and skyrmion properties together determine the motion.

Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.title: Frustration-freeness is decidable but unprovable
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.authors: Naoto Shiraishi
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.abstract: The frustration-free property is valuable in quantum many-body systems, which states that its ground states simultaneously minimize all local interaction terms, even when these terms act on overlapping degrees of freedom. Prominent examples include the AKLT model and Kitaev's toric code model, which serve as paradigmatic models of symmetry-protected topological phases and topological order, respectively. A fundamental question is whether a given Hamiltonian is frustration-free for all system sizes. Here we establish two seemingly contradictory results concerning this decision problem. First, we prove that frustration-freeness is decidable for any fixed local Hilbert space dimension. Specifically, there exists a finite, Hamiltonian-independent system-size cutoff such that frustration-freeness at this cutoff size guarantees frustration-freeness at all system sizes. Second, on the other hand, we also show that there exists a frustration-free Hamiltonian whose frustration-freeness cannot be proved within the standard axioms of mathematics (ZFC). We reconcile these seemingly contradictory results by showing that the cutoff, although finite for each local Hilbert space dimension, is uncomputable as a function of that dimension. Our findings reveal an unexpected fundamental distinction between decidability and provability arising in quantum many-body physics.

Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.title: Tunable emergent gauge fields from skyrmions in a quasicrystalline lattice
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Flavia A. Gómez Albarracín, Cristian D. Batista, Pablo S. Cornaglia

Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.title: One Measurement, Many Fronts in Kitaev and Cluster Chains
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.authors: Nicholas Musat, Stephan Haas, Rishabh Jha
Quantum Spin Liquids & Exotic Magnetic S.abstract: A projective measurement of one site in the ground state of a quantum chain disturbs the chain in two ways: learning the outcome shifts distant expectation values at once, through ground-state correlations, and the measurement erases the correlations between the measured site and the rest. Both changes travel outward. We solve this problem exactly for the Kitaev chain, the cluster chain in a transverse field, and the Kitaev chain with power-law couplings, and we find that far from the measured site every quadratic observable responds through a front. Where the front is and how fast it broadens depend only on the quasiparticle dispersion. How strong it is depends on two operators: how strongly the measured one creates the fastest quasiparticles and how strongly the observed one detects them; if either factor vanishes, the front is weaker and decays faster. One measurement therefore launches many fronts, one per observable, with a common position and width but different decay laws. In the Kitaev chain the density and the bond energy, the two terms of its nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian, respond to one density measurement with decay laws that trade places between the topological and the trivial phase; in the cluster chain, measuring a symmetry-odd spin instead of a symmetry-even one changes the critical decay law at a fixed Hamiltonian; and with power-law couplings the width law itself changes. All decay laws and profiles are obtained in closed form.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Thermally Activated Magnetic Switching in Antiferromagnetic Van der Waals Trilayers Resolved by Single-Spin Diamond Magnetometry
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Fabian A. Gerritsma, Roland W. Mulder, Balázs Nagyfalusi, Pieter C. J. A. van Zweeden, Samer Kurdi, Francisco Machado, Jaime Ferrer, Samuel Mañas-Valero, Toeno van der Sar
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Van der Waals magnets provide a versatile platform for exploring magnetic phenomena that emerge from reduced dimensionality, including layer-dependent magnetic ordering.
