Here, we use scanning nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond magnetometry to measure the magnetization of a trilayer of the A-type antiferromagnet CrPS$_4$, resolving its zero-field bistability between the up-down-up ($\uparrow\downarrow\uparrow$) and down-up-down ($\downarrow\uparrow\downarrow$) layer magnetization configurations. The coercive field decreases approximately linearly with temperature, consistent with the Néel--Arrhenius model. Density Functional Theory calculations capture the temperature dependence of the magnetization and determine the coercive field in the coherent-rotation case. The measured coercive fields are lower, identifying thermally activated domain nucleation as the reversal mechanism. Spatial magnetic imaging supports this picture, revealing independently switching regions likely pinned by structural inhomogeneities. Our results highlight the power of scanning NV magnetometry for the quantitative investigation of magnetization reversal in two-dimensional magnets, unraveling the magnetic phenomenology that emerges in low-dimensional systems.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Interaction-Induced Sign Reversal of the Orbital Magnetic Susceptibility in Chern Insulators
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Ke Huang, Xiao Li
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: It has been well established that the orbital magnetization of interacting electrons can be simply evaluated by applying the single-particle formula to self-consistent Hartree-Fock (HF) bands. However, we show that such a procedure fails qualitatively for orbital magnetic susceptibility, especially in topological systems: in a Chern-insulating phase of twisted MoTe 2 , the interaction-induced correction reverses the sign of the susceptibility. This result follows from an algebraic framework that solves the HF problem at finite magnetic field, where noncommuting canonical momenta obstruct a direct calculation: a maps every magnetic-translation-invariant operator to a unique bivariate function, converting the finite-field self-consistency into a function equation that can be expanded systematically in B . At first order, this yields a linear equation for the field-induced change δ X of the Fock potential, leading to an intrinsically interaction-induced susceptibility in addition to a single-particle-like one. The framework reproduces the Středa formula for insulators, and an auxiliary-Hilbert-space construction carries it to periodic and moiré systems. Finite-field HF calculations in a gapped Dirac model and in the twisted MoTe 2 Chern insulator confirm the theory quantitatively.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Unconventional Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect beyond Magnetization Scaling Driven by Pulse-Field-Induced Metamagnetism in Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Soichiro Yamane, Sota Nakamura, Shuya Suzuki, Atsutoshi Ikeda, Masaki Kondo, Takashi Kurumaji, Kentaro Ino, Keisuke Matsuura, Fumitaka Kagawa, Yoshinori Tokura, Masashi Tokunaga, Shingo Yonezawa
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: First-order phase transitions often proceed through metastable states and complicated phase coexistence, yet such nonequilibrium processes are obscured in bulk measurements. The magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) probes the local off-diagonal optical response, offering access to local magnetic dynamics beyond bulk measurements. Here, we investigate the magnetic-field-induced antiferromagnetic (AFM)-ferrimagnetic (FRM) transition in the polar insulator Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$ using pulsed-field MOKE measurements extended for the first time up to 60 T and down to 1.4 K. The MOKE response exhibits unexpected and huge nonmonotonic transient behavior across the metamagnetic phase transition. The MOKE behavior does not show any scaling with the bulk magnetization, pointing to an MOKE analogue of the unconventional anomalous Hall effect. This is a new class of off-diagonal response emerging exclusively at the boundary between competing magnetic orders. At low temperatures, MOKE profiles are highly reproducible in detail, whereas at elevated temperatures they depend strongly on magnetic-field history and pulse protocol, suggesting changes in the driving mechanism of the phase transition. We infer that the excess MOKE anomaly originates from AFM-FRM phase interfaces in real space. Our results, extending MOKE into the 60 T regime, establish pulsed-field magneto-optics as a novel probe capable of uncovering transient and hidden field-induced phenomena through unconventional off-diagonal optical responses.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Axis-selective AC magnetic-field imaging in the tens-of-megahertz regime using RF-dressed continuous-wave scanning NV magnetometry
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Shuntaro Komuro, Ryusei Okaniwa, Kazuma Okura, Kunitaka Hayashi, Toshu An, Junko Ishi-Hayase
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Spatially resolved magnetic-field imaging reveals material properties and local currents in microelectronic devices. Conventional pulsed scanning nitrogen-vacancy (NV) magnetometry (SNVM) faces increasingly stringent microwave (MW) pulse-control requirements for detecting radio-frequency (RF) magnetic fields at frequencies ranging from tens to hundreds of megahertz. To address this challenge, we implement an RF-dressed continuous-wave (CW) sensing scheme for SNVM and demonstrate AC magnetic-field imaging at 33.5 MHz. The method exploits electron-spin double resonance in the NV spin-1 three-level system: the target RF magnetic field coherently couples two spin eigenstates, forming RF-dressed states whose splittings are detected in continuous-wave electron-spin double resonance (CW-ESDR) spectra under continuous laser, MW, and RF excitation. This approach avoids short, high-power MW pulses and synchronization between the RF field and a pulsed sensing sequence. Using an NV-ensemble diamond probe integrated with an atomic force microscope (AFM), we image the Oersted field of an RF-driven L-shaped microcircuit. Successively selecting three crystallographic NV axes by static bias-field control yields maps of RF magnetic-field projection magnitudes, with distinct distributions qualitatively reproduced by Biot-Savart calculations. Transverse bias-field control also tunes the RF-coupled spin-state transition frequency from 14.4 to 89.3 MHz, as characterized by spectroscopy and Hamiltonian analysis, with RF-dressed resonances directly observed in CW-ESDR spectra at 89.3 MHz. Together with previous RF magnetic-field detection up to 632 MHz using the same RF-dressed CW sensing principle in a confocal NV setup, these results support extending AC magnetic-field imaging with SNVM toward the hundreds-of-megahertz regime and, with additional phase information, vector magnetic-field reconstruction.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Probing Spatiotemporal Quantum Correlations with Two-Qubit Relaxometry
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Christina Psaroudaki
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Quantum impurities and spin qubits are powerful local probes of magnetic fluctuations, but conventional relaxometry reduces their information to a local relaxation rate at a single frequency. Building on advances in two-qubit sensing of spatial correlations, we show how two complementary protocols probe finite-time correlations in interacting quantum matter. Phase-cycled Bell-state relaxometry isolates the signed contribution of correlated relaxation to the joint ground-state population. To second order in the probe-environment coupling, the resulting population contrast measures a finite-time integral of the energy-ordered cross-correlator. In the longitudinal regime, XY8 covariance probes the complementary symmetrized cross-correlator within a tunable frequency window. For a gapless quantum spin chain, the signals reveal interaction-dependent algebraic scaling and ballistic propagation. Luttinger-liquid theory links sign changes as the qubit frequency is swept to the propagation time between the probes. It also predicts distinct spatial power laws for the Bell signal before the correlation front and at late times, when the sensing window resolves the qubit frequency. Matrix-product-state calculations for the spin chain test the pre-front scaling at zero and finite magnetization and extract the propagation velocity from Bell oscillations at zero magnetization. The probe coupling geometry determines which spin and momentum sectors contribute to the measured signals.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: High-Volume Wurtzite MnSe in MnSe/CdSe Superlattices: Structure, Magnetism and Optical Response
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Michał J. Grzybowski, Katarzyna Gas, Jaroslaw Z. Domagala, Serhii Kryvyi, Łukasz Gondek, Soumik Das, Jan Suffczyński, Oleksii Liubchenko, Anna Kaleta, Sławomir Kret, Maciej Sawicki, Wojciech Pacuski
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Polymorphism in Mn-based chalcogenides offers access to magnetic semiconductors with distinct crystal symmetries, polar structures, and different magnetic orders. In particular, wurtzite MnSe exhibits an appealing interplay of electric polarization and several competing magnetic phases including altermagnetic order. However, stabilizing metastable polymorphs, such as wurtzite MnSe, in experimentally useful volumes remains challenging. Here, we show that a nanoscale-period MnSe/CdSe superlattice stabilizes wurtzite MnSe over micrometer-scale total thickness while suppressing the formation of the thermodynamically favored rock-salt phase. The increased magnetic volume enables bulk-sensitive characterization of this polar polymorph. The room-temperature lattice parameters of wurtzite MnSe are studied by independent experimental techniques and determined to be $a = (4.18 \pm 0.03)\,\mathring{A}$ and $c = (6.78 \pm 0.03)\, \mathring{A}$. SQUID magnetometry reveals antiferromagnetic ordering with $T_N = 62\,\text{K}$, which is accompanied by an anomaly of the MnSe lattice parameter, as oberved by temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction. Optical measurements reveal excitonic transitions pointing to the band gap at around 3.4 eV. These results highlight the utility and importance of heterostructure engineering for detailed studies of metastable phases of magnetic semiconductors, in particular wurtzite MnSe.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Good Practices for Measuring the Interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction by Brillouin Light Scattering and Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Marco Madami, Silvia Tacchi, Adriano Di Pietro, Alessandro Magni, Giovanni Gandini, Christian Rinaldi, Giovanni Carlotti, Gianfranco Durin, Johannes Hertel, Maximilian Lederer, Christopher H. Marrows, Vito Puliafito, Michaela Kuepferling
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: The interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (iDMI) is a key ingredient for stabilizing chiral magnetic states, such as skyrmions and chiral domain walls, which are key building blocks for next-generation spintronic technologies. Despite its importance, the quantitative determination of the iDMI constant, $D$, is often plagued by significant discrepancies. This paper establishes a set of good practices for measuring iDMI using two primary techniques: Brillouin Light Scattering (BLS) and the Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect (MOKE). Through the analysis of Co/Pt-based heterostructures, this work provides a comprehensive roadmap for measurement procedures, data evaluation, and uncertainty analysis. Our analysis highlights the crucial role of magnetic parameters used to extract the iDMI constant and propagation of their uncertainties, and the measurement model for enhancing measurement reliability. The proposed methodology provides a practical framework for improving the consistency and reproducibility of iDMI measurements across different laboratories and experimental techniques.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Antiferromagnetic semiconductor NdAsTe: a new member of LnAsTe (Ln = Lanthanoids) compounds
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Prabuddha Kant Mishra, Sandip Guchhait, Aarti Gautam, Haribrahma Singh, Ramesh Nath, Rie Umetsu, Ashok Kumar Ganguli
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Rare-earth-based intermetallic compounds are at the forefront of materials science, providing valuable insights into the interplay among magnetism, topology, and structural correlations. The interesting properties of these materials, driven by localized 4 f -electrons, strong spin–orbit coupling, and crystal electric field effect, make them a focal point in solid-state physics for designing advanced functional materials. We have synthesized NdAsTe using the solid-state reaction route and explored the temperature and field-dependent magnetic properties, which demonstrate long-range antiferromagnetic (AFM) ordering below T N ≃ 2.4 K. The low-temperature Curie–Weiss temperature θ CW ≃ − 1.89 K implies a net AFM interaction between the N d 3 + ions. Furthermore, the isothermal magnetization data exhibit signatures of spin-reorientation of the AFM-aligned spins at T < T N , corroborated through magnetic entropy studies. The signature of AFM transition is also manifested as a peak at T N in the temperature-dependent specific heat which gradually shifts towards lower temperatures at higher applied fields. The derived parameters from specific heat data suggest the presence of strong electronic correlations in NdAsTe. The magnetic susceptibility and specific heat data suggest that the magnetic ground state is a Kramers’ doublet with effective spin J eff = 1 / 2 at low temperatures. The electrical transport study revealed the semiconducting nature with a band gap of 70 MeV. Furthermore, the low temperature ( T < 20 K) magnetotransport studies unfold a crossover from positive to negative magnetoresistance behavior.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Interplay of Ni Order and Local Moments in Intercalated NixNbS2
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Gaurav Pransu, Naveen Singh Dhami, Wojciech Sas, Yuki Utsumi Boucher, Bruno Gudac, Ana Smontara, Davor Tolj, Victor Balédent, Mario Novak, Neven Barišić, Ivo Batistić, Mirta Herak, Petar Popčević
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Magnetic ions intercalated into the van der Waals gaps of layered transition metal dichalcogenides provide a system where local moments interact strongly with a metallic host. How the order of the intercalant sublattice affects their magnetism is important but rarely addressed, although disorder is hard to avoid, in particular in thin films and heterostructures. Here this question is examined in single crystals of Ni$_x$NbS$_2$ with $0.10 \leq x \leq 0.57$, whose composition and Ni order were determined by energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy and synchrotron x-ray diffraction. Anisotropic magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal three regimes. Long-range antiferromagnetic order appears only for $0.25 \leq x \leq 0.33$, where the Ni ions form the $2 \times 2$ and $\sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3}$ R$30^\circ$ superstructures, and $T_\mathrm{N}$ reaches 96 K at $x = 1/3$. In this range the effective moment, $\approx 2.5 μ_\mathrm{B}$ per Ni, agrees with DFT+$U$ calculations, in which the Ni spin is partly delocalized onto the surrounding S ligands. For $x \leq 0.18$ the dilute, randomly distributed Ni ions remain paramagnetic down to 2 K with a reduced moment. For $x \geq 0.37$, where Ni-Ni contacts are unavoidable, long-range order gives way to a short-range ordered state below 10-15 K with a further reduced moment. As calculations for ordered Ni arrangements find the Ni state nearly independent of $x$, even at $x = 1/2$, the reduction of the moment is attributed to a disorder-enabled reduction of the charge transfer from Ni to the NbS$_2$ layers. The magnetism of Ni$_x$NbS$_2$ is thus governed by the (dis)order of the Ni sublattice rather than by the Ni concentration alone.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Efficient time-dependent dynamics of matrix product states using average Hamiltonians
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Belal Abouraya, Jirawat Saiphet, Fedor Jelezko, Ressa S. Said
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Simulating quantum many-body systems (QMBS) is one of the long-standing, highly nontrivial challenges in condensed matter physics and quantum information due to the exponentially growing size of the system's Hilbert space. To date, tensor networks have been an essential tool for studying such quantum systems, owing to their ability to efficiently capture the entanglement properties of the systems they represent. One of the well-known tensor network architectures, namely, matrix product states (MPS), is the standard method for simulating one-dimensional QMBS. Here, we propose a simple, yet efficient, method to augment the already available MPS algorithms to simulate the dynamics of time-dependent Hamiltonians with better accuracy and a faster convergence rate, giving a second-order convergence compared to the first-order convergence of the Riemann method available in standard software packages. We apply our proposed method to simulate the dynamics of a chain of single spins associated with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) color centers in diamond, which has potential applications for practical and scalable quantum technologies, and find that our method improves the average error for a system of a few NV centers by a factor of about 1000 for moderate step sizes. Additionally, we compare our method to the midpoint rule, which has second-order convergence as well, and show some of the trade-offs between the two methods. Our work paves the way for efficient simulation of QMBS under the influence of time-dependent Hamiltonians.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Thermodynamic signatures of a nearby quantum critical endpoint in UTe$_2$ under intense magnetic field
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: M. Gen, K. Somesh, A. Miyake, D. Li, Z. Yang, A. Miyata, Y. Kohama, M. Kondo, M. Tokunaga, D. Aoki, W. Knafo
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Several unconventional superconducting phases have been discovered in the vicinity of metamagnetism in the heavy-fermion paramagnet UTe$_2$ under magnetic field. To describe the mechanism of magnetic-field-induced superconductivity, a challenge is to characterize the quantum critical magnetic properties at the metamagnetic transition. In this work, we investigate the thermodynamic properties of UTe$_2$ under magnetic fields up to 60~T applied in the crystallographic $\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{c}$ plane. Magnetization and magnetostriction experiments have been performed under magnetic fields tilted by an angle $θ\lesssim42^\circ$ from $\mathbf{b}$ toward $\mathbf{c}$. They support that a quantum critical endpoint at the field angle $θ_{QCEP}\simeq(70\pm10)^\circ$ and magnetic field $μ_0H_{QCEP}\simeq(75\pm10)$~T terminates the metamagnetic transition line. A pseudo-gap in the magnetic susceptibility is related with the metamagnetic transition observed in magnetic fields for $θ<θ_{QCEP}$. The possible relation between the quantum critical endpoint and the development of magnetic-field-induced superconductivity is discussed.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Quantum sensing-enabled deuterium NMR spectroscopy with nanoscale sensitivity at low magnetic fields
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Dileep Singh, Riley W. Hooper, Christoph Findler, Utsab Banerjee, Dominik B. Bucher
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy provides unparalleled access to molecular structure and dynamics but is traditionally limited by weak signal strength, requiring large sample volumes and high magnetic fields. Here, we demonstrate nanoscale deuterium ( 2 H) NMR spectroscopy using nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, yielding characteristic quadrupolar powder line shapes that are present in conventional bulk NMR spectra. By detecting statistical spin fluctuations from nanometer-scale detection volumes, our approach delivers a sensitivity enhancement of seven to eight orders of magnitude in terms of spin sensitivity over inductive detection, while operating at magnetic fields two orders of magnitude lower than those used in conventional NMR. Temperature-dependent measurements of a deuterated polymer and a molecular solid reveal distinct motional averaging and phase transitions with nanoscale sensitivity. Powder-like NV-detected 2 H NMR establishes a powerful tool for probing molecular dynamics on the nanoscale - capabilities beyond those of most existing spectroscopic techniques.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Magnetic anisotropy in the near-stoichiometric van der Waals ferromagnet Fe 3 GeTe 2
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Riju Pal, Joyal John Abraham, Satyabrata Bera, Mintu Mondal, Atindra Nath Pal, Bernd Büchner, Vladislav Kataev, Alexey Alfonsov
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Quasi-two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) ferromagnets such as the series Fe 3 − x GeTe 2 , with a relatively high Curie temperature and robust metallicity, offer an ideal platform for investigating itinerant magnetism in reduced dimensions. Here, we present a comprehensive electron spin resonance (ESR) investigation of single-crystalline, almost stoichiometric Fe 3.03 ± 0.03 GeTe 2 across wide ranges of frequencies, temperatures, and magnetic fields to gain quantitative insights into its magnetic anisotropy and spin dynamics. Frequency-dependent ESR measurements establish Fe 3 GeTe 2 as an easy-axis ferromagnet. Temperature-dependent high-field ESR reveals a large internal field that gradually decreases at higher temperatures. Remarkably, this internal field persists even above T C , indicating short-range spin correlations in Fe 3 GeTe 2 . Analysis of spin-wave modes yields a strong uniaxial magnetocrystalline anisotropy K int ≈ − 5 × 10 6 erg cm − 3 at 3 K and a large magnon gap Δ ( 3 K ) ≈ 87.8 ± 13.7 GHz ( ≈ 0.363 ± 0.057 meV ). Our study highlights that small variations in Fe content in Fe 3 GeTe 2 lead to substantial changes in the magnon gap at low temperatures, indicating the sensitivity of spin dynamics to the chemical composition. These results establish Fe 3 GeTe 2 as a model vdW ferromagnet for exploring tunable anisotropies and magnon excitations in metallic 2D magnets.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Tailored magnetic domain-wall ratchet effects through density gradients in triangular-hole arrays
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Julia Herrero-Albillos, María Ángeles Laguna-Marco, María Vélez, Xabier Zubizarreta-Iriarte, Daniel Arechavaleta, Aurelio Hierro-Rodriguez, Carlos Quirós, Michael Foerster, Cristina Bran, Arantxa Fraile-Rodriguez, José Ignacio Martín
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: We investigate domain wall (DW) dynamics and morphology in amorphous Co$_{0.86}$Zr$_{0.14}$ thin films patterned with engineered, density-graded triangular-hole arrays. Using Kerr microscopy and high-resolution XMCD-PEEM imaging, we demonstrate that DW propagation is governed by the interplay between hole orientation, density gradients, and local magnetostatic interactions. In cooperative configurations, the density gradient reinforces the geometric ratchet effect, whereas in competing configurations, the two mechanisms oppose each other, leading to an inverse ratchet and enabling experimental access to backward DW propagation. Remarkably, density-graded arrays substantially reduce the stochastic variability of depinning fields observed in periodic arrays, resulting in highly reproducible DW motion. The depinning fields are described by a rigid DW model and an empirical scaling law incorporating both inter-hole spacing and array periodicity. These results demonstrate that engineered density gradients provide an effective route to deterministic control of DW propagation, with potential applications in spintronic and neuromorphic devices.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: The de Haas--van Alphen effect in a two-dimensional nematic Fermi fluid
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Luís E. Leite Macêdo, Daniel G. Barci
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Quantum oscillations are widely used to probe the Fermi surface of metals, but their behavior becomes more complex when electronic interactions can spontaneously deform that surface. We investigate this interplay in a two-dimensional model of interacting electrons capable of developing nematic order, using a uniform mean-field approximation in a perpendicular magnetic field. We show that Landau quantization can favor or suppress nematic order as the field varies, producing alternating isotropic and nematic regions near a Pomeranchuk instability, with both continuous and first-order transitions. Conversely, the evolving nematic order modifies the de Haas--van Alphen oscillations in ways that depend on the thermodynamic conditions. At fixed chemical potential, the oscillation frequency can change significantly even when the cyclotron mass varies only modestly. At fixed particle density, conservation of the Fermi-surface area preserves the leading Onsager frequency, while the cyclotron mass and harmonic amplitudes remain sensitive to nematic order. The magnetization and magnetic susceptibility provide additional signatures of the nematic transitions. These results show how quantum oscillations can both reveal and influence electronic order, offering a framework for interpreting experiments in strongly correlated metals.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Electrostatic screening and nitrogen-vacancy charge states in boron-doped/nitrogen-doped diamond junctions
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Masato Koga, Haizen Cho, El Mustapha Mansouri, Eikichi Kimura, Ryo Matsumoto, Yoshihiko Takano, Keigo Arai
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Boron-doped diamond (BDD) enables the integration of electrical functionality with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers, but the influence of junction electrostatics on NV charge-state stability remains unclear. In this study, we investigate the equilibrium electrostatics of BDD/nitrogen-doped diamond junctions using self-consistent Poisson-Fermi calculations. The results reveal two distinct electrostatic length scales in the nitrogen-doped substrate: a near-interface region of ionized donors that produces dominant band bending and determines the NV$^{0/-}$ charge-state boundary, and a much longer screening tail associated with weak donor ionization in the neutral bulk. The resulting NV$^-$ depletion depth depends strongly on the nitrogen concentration but exhibits a more moderate dependence on boron doping. At $N_B = 10^{21}$ cm$^{-3}$, varying the interface grading scale $w$ from 0.5 to 8 nm changes the depletion depth by approximately 22 nm, whereas variations in the modeled bulk BDD charge response produce a shift of only 1.27 nm. These results indicate that, under the conditions studied, the nitrogen donor concentration and local interface structure primarily govern the equilibrium NV charge-state profile, rather than the bulk electronic response of BDD alone.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Extending qubit lifetime beyond break-even and enhancing quantum sensing by autonomous quantum error correction
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Zhongchu Ni, Ling Hu, Yanyan Cai, Libo Zhang, Jiasheng Mai, Xiaowei Deng, Pan Zheng, Song Liu, Shi-Biao Zheng, Yuan Xu, Dapeng Yu

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Erratum: Ultracold mechanical quantum sensor for tests of new physics [Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 180802 (2026)]
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Andraž Omahen, Simon Storz, Marius Bild, Dario Scheiwiller, Matteo Fadel, Yiwen Chu

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Collective Many-Body Dynamics in a Solid-State Quantum Sensor Controlled through Nanoscale Magnetic Gradients
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Piotr Put, Nathaniel T. Leitao, Haoyang Gao, Christina Spaegele, Oksana Makarova, Lillian B. Hughes Wyatt, Andrew C. Maccabe, Mathew Mammen, Bartholomeus Machielse, Hengyun Zhou, Szymon Pustelny, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, Federico Capasso, Leigh S. Martin, Hongkun Park, Mikhail D. Lukin
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Coherent collective dynamics of strongly interacting qubits are a central resource in quantum information science, with applications from quantum computing and simulation to metrology. While electronic spins interact strongly via dipolar couplings in dense solid-state ensembles, imperfections and positional disorder pose major obstacles to coherent correlated behavior, limiting their usefulness. Here, we realize collective many-body dynamics by combining time-dependent magnetic field gradients with global coherent control of dense electron spin ensembles in diamond. We control and probe the dynamics of nanometer-scale spin spirals, and, by exploiting Hamiltonian engineering that enhances the microscopic symmetry of the interactions, we observe a disorder-resilient collective spin evolution. Our results establish a pathway to interaction-enhanced quantum metrology and nanoscale imaging of materials and biological systems under ambient conditions.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Photoelectrical readout and Ramsey interferometry of single shallowly implanted NV centers in diamond
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Ilia Chuprina, Christoph Findler, Johannes Lang, Petr Siyushev, Fedor Jelezko

Topological Materials.title: Tunable giant anomalous Hall effect in bilayer magnetic topological insulator
Topological Materials.authors: Basavaraja G, Mukul Kabir
Topological Materials.abstract: In the two-dimensional limit, the intrinsic magnetic topological insulator MnBi 2 Te 4 offers an exceptional platform for probing novel quantum states and their response to external perturbations. Using first-principles calculations and classical Heisenberg Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that electrostatic gating and surface chemical functionalization trigger a remarkable crossover from the topological to the conventional anomalous Hall regime. This transition is governed by the simultaneous shift of the Fermi level and an antiferromagnetic-to-ferromagnetic reversal of interlayer coupling. Notably, hole doping drives the Fermi level deep into the valence bands, unlocking Berry curvature hot spots that generate an exceptionally high anomalous Hall conductivity of 1380 S/cm. Conversely, surface chemical functionalization preserves a Chern band manifold coexisting with metallic states, where intrinsic σ xy is reduced from e 2 /h to ∼ 0.86 e 2 /h due to the spectral coexistence of a chiral edge mode with the metallic bulk states of the two-dimensional film. Critically, both tuning strategies significantly strengthen in-plane exchange interactions, driving a substantial increase in the magnetic ordering temperature compared to the pristine bilayer. These findings establish a powerful, versatile strategy to concurrently tailor the topological, magnetic, and transport properties of ultrathin MnBi 2 Te 4 , advancing the design of reconfigurable quantum devices.

Topological Materials.title: Magnetization-free quantum anomalous Hall effect in altermagnetic weak topological insulators
Topological Materials.authors: Yanmiao Han, Yu-Hao Wan, Peng-Yi Liu, Rundong Zhao, Qing-Feng Sun
Topological Materials.abstract: The quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) effect is usually realized through ferromagnetism or magnetic dop ing, which limits material choices and often results in low mobility, disorder sensitivity, and low operating temperatures. Here, we propose a mechanism to achieve the QAH phase without net magnetization, using altermagnetic exchange on a weak topological insulator (WTI). The altermagnetic order selectively gaps the Dirac cone at the Z point, while hybridization between the top and bottom surfaces of the WTI thin film opens a trivial gap at the point, generating a Chern number C = 1 phase with a single chiral edge channel. We verify the topological transition through both a minimal thin-film model and a slab geometry, and compute the associated Hall response. As altermagnets and layered WTIs already exist experimentally, this mechanism offers a promising and experimentally accessible route to realizing QAH phases without magnetic doping or global magnetization. The results indicate that altermagnetic surface engineering may provide a clean and controllable pathway for realizing dissipationless edge transport in layered quantum materials.

Topological Materials.title: Multiple electronic phase transitions in room-temperature second-order topological insulator
Topological Materials.authors: Chaosheng Hao, Fei Wang, Li Deng, Hanghui Li, Xianmin Zhang
Topological Materials.abstract: Two-dimensional magnetic materials with coupled valley and topological properties provide an attractive platform for next-generation spintronic and valleytronic applications. Here, using first-principles calculations, the novel monolayer SeVPH is predicted as a dynamically, thermally, and mechanically stable magnetic semiconductor. Its Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless transition temperature is 382 K. Spin–orbit coupling generates a valley splitting of 68 meV in the valence band with magnetization oriented along the +z direction, resulting in the anomalous valley Hall effect. Moreover, the monolayer SeVPH is identified as a second-order topological insulator (SOTI) hosting robust corner states. Biaxial tensile strain modulates the valley degree of freedom to induce successive topological phase transitions, driving the system from the SOTI to valley-polarized quantum anomalous Hall phase and then to a trivial normal insulator. These findings demonstrate that monolayer SeVPH is a promising multifunctional quantum material for tunable ferrovalley, spintronic, and topological devices.

Topological Materials.title: Intertwined Spin Chirality and Weyl Topology Driven Giant Hall Responses in Nd$_{4}$Sb$_3$
Topological Materials.authors: Anu, Subhasmita Kar, Bhagyashree Pol, Debarghya Dutta, Aftab Alam, P D Babu
Topological Materials.abstract: Magnetic Weyl materials offer a unique platform for coupling magnetic order with real- and momentum-space topology, yet their simultaneous manifestation in a single material remains uncommon. Here, Nd$_4$Sb$_3$ is established as a highly spin-polarized magnetic Weyl semimetal exhibiting intertwined anomalous and topological Hall responses. Nd$_4$Sb$_3$ orders ferromagnetically below $T_{\mathrm{C}}\sim72$ K and undergoes spin reorientation near 42 K into a non-coplanar magnetic state. A large topological Hall resistivity of $\sim3.9 μΩ$ cm and anomalous Hall conductivity reaching $\sim1170$ S cm$^{-1}$ are observed. First-principles calculations identify an energetically preferred non-coplanar state with finite local scalar spin chirality, providing a microscopic route to the real-space Berry phase underlying the topological Hall effect. Calculated exchange interactions reveal dominant ferromagnetic exchange together with anisotropic exchange and finite Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions, while Monte Carlo simulations yield a magnetic transition near 78 K, close to the experimental $T_{\mathrm{C}}$. Concurrently, magnetic reconstruction profoundly reshapes the reciprocal-space topology, increasing the number of Weyl-point pairs from 42 in the collinear ferromagnetic state to 115 in the non-coplanar state. Berry-curvature calculations yield an intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity of $\sim983$ S cm$^{-1}$ at the experimentally determined carrier concentration, closely reproducing the experimental intrinsic contribution of $\sim990$ S cm$^{-1}$. These results establish Nd$_4$Sb$_3$ as a compelling platform where magnetic reconstruction intertwines real-space spin chirality with momentum-space Weyl topology.

Topological Materials.title: Discovery of Kondo-Kramers Nodal Line Topological State in strongly correlated material CeAuAl$_3$
Topological Materials.authors: Hari Bhandari, Kevin Allen, Kuan-Sen Lin, Yuan Fang, Arushi, Karthik Rao, Mounica Mahankali, Sanu Mishra, Jian-Xin Zhu, Christopher Lane, Qimiao Si, Emilia Morosan
Topological Materials.abstract: Kramers nodal lines (KNLs) are predicted in all achiral, non-centrosymmetric crystal structures, and yet there are very few experimental realizations of KNLs, only in weakly correlated systems. Especially, their realization in strongly correlated systems remains unexplored. Here we investigate KNL topology in the non-centrosymmetric, achiral Kondo lattice CeAuAl$_3$, using magnetotransport, thermodynamic measurements, density functional theory (DFT), and tight-binding toy model calculations. We find that CeAuAl$_3$ hosts KNLs in the $\mathitΓ\text{-}Z$ and $X\text{-}P$ directions, protected by time-reversal and mirror symmetries. Breaking of these crystalline symmetries, along with time-reversal symmetry via spin polarization, lifts the KNL degeneracy, which, in turn, generates Berry curvature resulting in an intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (AHE). More importantly, CeAuAl$_3$ shows large AHE not only below the magnetic ordering temperature $T_N$ but rather below the Kondo temperature. This underscores the role of the Kondo correlations in bringing the KNLs at the Fermi surface rather than at accidental energies, as would be expected without correlations. Our work identifies a new topological state, Kondo-Kramers Nodal Line, with CeAuAl$_3$ being the first compound explicitly identified to host this new correlated topological state, and demonstrating the expected AHE associated with it. More generally, our work outlines the pathway for finding Kondo-KNL systems in all compounds that combine achiral, non-centrosymmetric structure with Kondo correlations.

Topological Materials.title: Half-integer quantum anomalous Hall effect in MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ via non-magnetic extension
Topological Materials.authors: Igor P. Rusinov, Tatiana V. Menshchikova, Evgueni V. Chulkov
Topological Materials.abstract: Within an ab-initio approach, we study the electronic structure and Hall response of the antiferromagnetic topological insulator film of MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ in contact with non-magnetic GeBi$_2$Te$_4$ (Bi$_2$Te$_3$) overlayer. The proposed junction design eliminates the exchange splitting one of the Dirac cones of the MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ (0001) thus manifesting a half-integer quantum anomalous Hall phase. The described recipe allows to enlarge temperature of the effect observation, enriches the diversity of topological properties of the MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ compound and is appropriate for other layered antiferromagnetic topological insulators. Applying the proposed heterostructure design, the half-quantized Hall phase can be established with employing other overlayer and magnetic topological insulator films.

Topological Materials.title: Topological magnons and large orbital Nernst effect in a zigzag Kitaev antiferromagnet
Topological Materials.authors: Shreya Debnath, Saurabh Basu

Topological Materials.title: Molecular-orbital origin of weak orbital ferromagnetism and anomalous Hall effect in a trimerized kagome antiferromagnet
Topological Materials.authors: I. V. Solovyev
Topological Materials.abstract: We reveal the molecular-orbital origin of weak orbital ferromagnetism and the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) induced by noncollinear spin order in a trimerized kagome lattice. By transforming to the molecular-orbital basis of an isolated trimer in the double-exchange regime, we derive an effective low-energy model for the states with opposite orbital angular momenta $m= \pm 1$ subject to an effective Zeeman field arising from spin chirality and spin-orbit (SO) coupling. In this representation, the kagome-lattice problem maps onto a triangular lattice of trimers, while the nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor hoppings of the original lattice generate complex hopping amplitudes between neighboring trimers. This formulation provides a transparent picture of how spin chirality and SO coupling can be recast as an effective Zeeman field that lifts the degeneracy of the $m= \pm 1$ states, breaks time-reversal symmetry, and thereby gives rise to weak orbital ferromagnetism and the AHE. The resulting phase diagram includes metallic phases, topologically trivial insulating phases, as well as several topological phases characterized by nonzero Chern numbers and the quantum anomalous Hall effect. We further identify an alternative route to time-reversal-symmetry breaking and orbital magnetization, driven by an emergent gauge field arising solely from complex inter-trimer hoppings and requiring no effective Zeeman field.

Topological Materials.title: Pressure and Magnetic Field Control of Topology in Antiferromagnetic Bilayers
Topological Materials.authors: Narsimha Rao Elaprolu, Marco Gibertini
Topological Materials.abstract: Controlling band topology in magnetic semiconductors requires strategies that couple electronic structure to experimentally accessible degrees of freedom. Here we propose a cooperative approach based on pressure and magnetic reorientation in A-type antiferromagnetic bilayers. Antiparallel layer magnetizations suppress hybridization between exchange-polarized band-edge states, limiting their response to interlayer compression. A magnetic field that aligns the layer moments removes this spin mismatch, enabling pressure-enhanced hybridization to drive a band inversion. The magnetization direction then controls the symmetries of the inverted bands and whether spin--orbit coupling produces a Chern-insulating gap or symmetry-protected nodal crossings. First-principles calculations for bilayer CrSBr illustrate this mechanism within a compressed orthorhombic structural model. Out-of-plane magnetization yields a Chern insulator with a chiral edge state, whereas in-plane magnetization supports a two-dimensional Weyl semimetal with node-connecting edge states. Continuous spin canting further demonstrates how magnetic reorientation can drive the transition and stabilize the Chern phase before full magnetic saturation. Although material-specific transition conditions depend on electronic correlations and structural stability under compression, the underlying strategy identifies interlayer hybridization as a link between magnetic order and band topology. These results provide a design principle for externally tunable topological phases in layered antiferromagnetic semiconductors.

Topological Materials.title: Probing the Dirac Quantum Geometry in Quantum Magnets from Polarized Raman Spectroscopy
Topological Materials.authors: Yuki Yamazaki, Doh Young Kim, Takahiro Morimoto, Bohm-Jung Yang
Topological Materials.abstract: Magnetic Raman spectroscopy is sensitive to quasiparticle quantum geometry, yet microscopic Raman vertices generally prevent a direct geometric interpretation. Here we establish a symmetry-based extraction principle for two-dimensional quantum magnets with two-band quasiparticle excitations. Opposite circular-polarization spectra separate vertex-weighted quantum-metric and Berry-curvature contractions. Near a $C_3$-symmetric massive Dirac valley, symmetry fixes the leading Raman and velocity doublets up to a common scale, allowing the unknown Raman strength and intensity normalization to cancel from their spectral ratio. For an inversion-related pair of massive Dirac cones, the normalized counter-circular Raman asymmetry at frequency threshold $Ω_{\rm th}$ is fixed by the Chern number and follows a universal near-threshold frequency scaling. This yields a local spectroscopic readout without absolute-intensity calibration or frequency integration. We demonstrate the principle for Majorana fermions in the field-induced honeycomb Kitaev spin liquid and for topological magnons in a honeycomb ferromagnet, and identify the conditions for resolving it experimentally.

Topological Materials.title: Chiral magnetism and quantum anomalous Hall effect in a low-energy Kondo model on the triangular lattice
Topological Materials.authors: Kai Vylet, Xingkai Huang, Leon Balents

Topological Materials.title: Peierls Transition and Magnetism in a Dirac Semimetal: CaMnBi 2
Topological Materials.authors: Aashish Sapkota, Niraj Aryal, Xiao Hu, Masaaki Matsuda, Yan Wu, Guangyong Xu, John M. Wilde, Andreas Kreyssig, Paul C. Canfield, Cedomir Petrovic, John M. Tranquada, Igor A. Zaliznyak
Topological Materials.abstract: Dirac semimetals of the form A Mn X 2 ( A = alkaline-earth or divalent rare earth; X = Bi , Sb) host conducting square-net Dirac-electron layers of X atoms interleaved with antiferromagnetic Mn X layers. Hypervalent pnictogen square nets have long been predicted to host an electronically driven Peierls instability, whereas low-temperature anomalies in CaMnBi 2 near T * ∼ 50 K have previously been discussed in terms of possible magnetic canting, time-reversal symmetry breaking, and a resulting Weyl-semimetal state. Here we use polarized and unpolarized neutron diffraction, x-ray diffraction, and density functional theory to investigate this transition in single-crystal CaMnBi 2 . We observe a structural symmetry-lowering transition at T * = 46 ( 2 ) K from a tetragonal lattice with C -type antiferromagnetism to an orthorhombic phase with unit-cell doubling along the c axis, minimal impact on magnetism, and no measurable uniform spin canting ( ≲ 2 ° ). Superlattice peak intensities and the lattice distortion reveal a continuous second-order transition governed by a single primary order parameter. The refined displacement pattern corresponds to a zigzag bond-order-wave (BOW) modulation of in-plane Bi–Bi bonds, providing direct diffraction evidence for a Peierls-type instability of the Dirac-electron Bi layer anticipated by Hoffmann and co-workers [; ]. These results identify the T * anomaly as an intrinsic Dirac-electron-driven Peierls-BOW transition of the Bi square net.

Topological Materials.title: Reversal of the Anomalous Hall Effect by Directional In-Plane Electric Field in Strained Bilayer MoO
Topological Materials.authors: Wenpeng Wang, hang Shi, Xiangru Kong
Topological Materials.abstract: Layered magnetic materials with tunable valley and spin degrees of freedom hold promise for multifunctional spintronic devices. Here, we demonstrate that the orientation of an in-plane electric field enables selective switching of single-valley spin splitting and reversal of the anomalous Hall conductivity in strained bilayer MoO. In particular, electric fields along the a and b directions selectively lift the spin degeneracy at the X and Y valleys, respectively, while preserving it at the other valley. This valley-selective switching is accompanied by a redistribution of Berry curvature with opposite signs, giving rise to a reversible anomalous Hall response. These effects are realized in the energetically and dynamically stable AC2 stacking configuration, where biaxial strain induces Dirac-like band crossings that enable subsequent electric-field control. Meanwhile, the AC1 stacking configuration, which is also energetically and dynamically stable, exhibits rich strain-driven phenomena, including a transition from metal to topological insulator with quantized spin Hall conductivity, as well as valley polarization and piezomagnetism. Our findings reveal a combined effect of strain and electric fields for controlling valley-selective spin splitting and anomalous Hall responses, highlighting bilayer MoO as a promising platform for multifunctional spintronic and valleytronic devices.

Topological Materials.title: Direction-Selective Anomalous Quantum Transport from Saddle-like Topological Surface States Coupled to an Electronic Instability in YbSb$_{2}$
Topological Materials.authors: Rudra Dhara, Pritesh Srivastava, Jack Tregidga, Rahul Sharma, Shivani, Shankhadip Bhattacharjee, Danilo Ratkovski, Shikhar Gupta, Kartick Biswas, Shivesh Yadav, Nilesh Kulkarni, Sarthak S. Gandhi, Pavan Nukala, Surajit Saha, John W. Harter, Bahadur Singh, Shouvik Chatterjee
Topological Materials.abstract: We report direction-selective anomalous quantum transport in epitaxial YbSb$_{2}$ thin films associated with an interplay between anisotropic topological surface states and an electronic instability. Quantum oscillations reveal a quasi-two-dimensional orbit with a non-trivial Berry phase and Dirac-like dispersion, observable for current along the $a$-axis but absent along the orthogonal in-plane $c$-axis. Together with first-principles calculations, these observations support its assignment to a saddle-like topological surface state. Its oscillation amplitude exhibits a field-dependent, non-monotonic temperature evolution that departs from conventional Lifshitz-Kosevich behavior. Raman and coherent phonon spectroscopy reveal additional low-temperature modes consistent with a density-wave instability. Their pronounced polarization anisotropy and colossal field-induced Raman enhancement suggest a strongly anisotropic, field-enhanced electronic susceptibility associated with the density-wave modes. Our findings point to dynamical coupling between anisotropic topological surface states and a field-responsive density-wave instability as a route to direction-selective anomalous quantum transport.

Topological Materials.title: Digitally-alloyed magnetic topological insulator nanostructures grown via stencil mask molecular beam epitaxy
Topological Materials.authors: Jan Karthein, Max Vaßen-Carl, Lars Maier, Abdur Rehman Jalil, Gion Toehgiono, Josua Thieme, Julian Feldewerth, Benjamin Bennemann, Joscha Domnick, Taizo Kawano, Sosuke Otsubo, René Heller, Jun Ishihara, Detlev Grützmacher, Makoto Kohda, Peter Schüffelgen, Thomas Schäpers
Topological Materials.abstract: Magnetic topological insulator nanostructures are a promising platform for the realization of fault-tolerant quantum computation. For this, such nanostructures need to be embedded into the necessary superconducting architectures. In this study, we demonstrate a method for the growth of magnetic topological insulator nanostructures via molecular beam epitaxy, utilising digital alloying and defining their shapes in-situ by stencil mask technology. Cr-doped (Bi$_y$Sb$_{1-y}$)$_2$Te$_3$ micro- and nanometer-sized Hall bars are fabricated and the magneto-transport properties for various Cr doping amounts and different Hall bar dimensions are investigated at low temperatures. We find indications that the Fermi energy is located inside the bulk band gap, while disorder and charge puddles affect the transport behaviour. Furthermore, we investigate the magnetic properties and discuss the transition from ferromagnetic to paramagnetic behaviour.

Topological Materials.title: MagBerry: A Julia package for modeling magnon and phonon topology and transport
Topological Materials.authors: Xiaonong Shen, Wei Ren
Topological Materials.abstract: We present MagBerry, a Julia package for studying the topology and transport of magnons, phonons, and their hybrid excitations. It combines magnetic models and linear spin-wave Hamiltonians from Sunny.jl with native modules for harmonic phonons and magnon--phonon coupling. These excitations are treated within a common bosonic Bogoliubov--de Gennes formulation. The package calculates bulk and boundary spectra, Berry curvature, and Chern numbers, and resolves the spin and phonon angular momentum carried by each mode. Transport calculations include thermal Hall, spin and orbital Nernst, and phonon angular momentum Hall responses. The package also evaluates the extended Berry curvature dipole contribution to nonlinear magnon thermal Hall transport. Relaxation-time Boltzmann theory gives heat and angular momentum currents. Examples based on published models reproduce topological magnon boundary spectra and illustrate phonon geometry and nonlinear transport. For an altermagnetic hybrid model, we extend a published study of the d-wave phonon angular momentum texture by calculating its Boltzmann transport coefficients. The resulting tensor describes how the longitudinal and transverse angular momentum currents vary with temperature and the direction of the temperature gradient.

Topological Materials.title: Theory of anisotropic magnetotransport beyond the constant relaxation-time approximation in multi-Weyl semimetals
Topological Materials.authors: Azaz Ahmad, Shantanu Mukherjee, Mohd Hashim Raza, Gautham Varma K., Takami Tohyama
Topological Materials.abstract: Multi-Weyl semimetals, characterized by Weyl nodes carrying higher monopole charges, provide a platform for exploring topological magnetotransport beyond the conventional Weyl paradigm. Here, we develop a generalized semiclassical Boltzmann framework for multi-Weyl semimetals with arbitrary monopole charge $N$, incorporating the orbital magnetic moment (OMM) into the quasiparticle dispersion and Berry-curvature-modified dynamics, together with a momentum-dependent collision integral accounting for intra- and intervalley scattering. We investigate the longitudinal magnetoconductivity (LMC) and planar Hall conductivity (PHC) for $N=1$, $2$, and $3$, considering both nonmagnetic and magnetic impurity scattering. In the absence of OMM, the LMC remains positive and quadratic in the magnetic field throughout the investigated scattering regime, consistent with conventional chiral-anomaly-assisted transport. Including OMM, however, leads to a sign reversal of the LMC under sufficiently strong intervalley scattering for the $σ_0$ and $σ_z$ impurity channels. Remarkably, the critical intervalley scattering strength decreases systematically with increasing monopole charge, indicating an enhanced tendency toward negative LMC in higher-charge Weyl systems. Furthermore, we find that the PHC also undergoes a sign reversal for $N=2$ and $N=3$ in the same impurity channels, while remaining positive for $N=1$ within the investigated parameter range. The angular dependences retain their characteristic $\sin^2γ$-like and $\sin2γ$ profiles for LMC and PHC, respectively, even across the sign reversal. Our results demonstrate that the interplay of Berry curvature, OMM, monopole charge, and impurity scattering can produce qualitatively distinct weak-field magnetotransport responses beyond the conventional chiral-anomaly picture.

Topological Materials.title: Nonvolatile ferroelectric control of quantum anomalous Hall phases in van der Waals multiferroic heterostructures
Topological Materials.authors: Yuntao Jie, Meiling Xu, Xiaodong Zhou, Xiuxian Yang, Sheng Wang, Yinwei Li
Topological Materials.abstract: The quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) effect offers a promising route toward dissipationless, low-power electronics, but achieving its nonvolatile and reversible control remains a major challenge. Here, we propose a van der Waals multiferroic heterostructure that integrates a QAH layer with a ferroelectric substrate, enabling electric-field control of topological phases through ferroelectric polarization switching. Using CrVI6/In2Se3 as a representative system, we show that polarization reversal reconstructs the interfacial band alignment and drives a reversible transition between a metallic state and a QAH insulating phase with a sizable topological gap of ∼92 meV. The heterostructure retains robust perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and exhibits an enhanced Curie temperature of ∼164 K, thereby improving the thermal stability of the QAH phase. In addition, reorientation of the magnetization transforms the system into a topologically trivial phase, providing an independent magnetic degree of freedom for topological-state control. These results establish a van der Waals platform for electrically writable and magnetically reconfigurable topological phases, with potential applications in nonvolatile topological memory and low-power quantum electronic devices.

Topological Materials.title: Spin-resolved nodal line, spin-orbit-coupling-induced Weyl points, and associated intrinsic spin-Hall response in altermagnetic Mn 2 (PO 4 )O
Topological Materials.authors: Xiang-Feng Yang, Jun-Tao Ma, Kai-Yuan Zhang, Hua-Hua Fu

Topological Materials.title: Magnetic-Field-Tuned Critical End Point and High-Field Phases in HoMn6Sn6
Topological Materials.authors: Joanna Blawat, John Singleton, Junho Seo, Charles Mielke, Tyler J. Slade, Paul C. Canfield, Philip J. W. Moll, Ross D. McDonald, Robert J. McQueeney
Topological Materials.abstract: Topological Kagome RMn6Sn6 materials, where R is a rare-earth, exhibit a rich variety of magnetic phases which provide an opportunity to understand how different spin textures affect topological and transport properties through the application of magnetic field H. In this work, we report experiments on single-crystal HoMn6Sn6, made possible by pulsed magnetic fields of up to 60 T, that permit high-field features of the field-temperature phase diagram to be studied in detail using magnetometry. Complementary, sensitive transport experiments over the same field range employ focused-ion-beam fabrication of novel strain-relieved HoMn6Sn6 devices. In agreement with meanfield calculations, we find a metamagnetic transition at 45 T with H||c between canted phases that ends in a critical end point at about 90 K. As far as we are aware, this is the only critical endpoint that is observed within the RMn6Sn6 kagome metals, and its temperature and field far exceed those of analogous phenomena in other materials. In the low-temperature metamagnetic region, HoMn6Sn6 shows large magnetoresistance, reaching 900 % at 60 T, in concert with Shubnikov de Haas oscillations that suggest a slight Fermi-surface contraction as the metamagnetic transition is crossed. A phase analysis of the oscillations suggests non-trivial band topology, although a firmer attribution must await detailed bandstructure calculations. Near the critical end point, we find deviations from Fermi-liquid behavior in the temperature-dependent magnetoresistance. In the metamagnetic region, the anomalous Hall contribution is not proportional to magnetization, and peaks at about 40 K, suggesting the role of enhanced spin fluctuations near the critical point. At higher temperatures, the anomalous Hall effect reappears at low fields, showing that the magnetization provided by the Ho and Mn sublattices independently affect the conductivity.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Optical spin Edelstein response of d-wave altermagnets
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: M. A. Mojarro, R. Carrillo-Bastos, Jesús A. Maytorena
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: The momentum-dependent spin splitting and compensated magnetic order in altermagnets offer opportunities for electrical control of spin polarization. We explore the spin Edelstein effect in the frequency domain of a two-dimensional d-wave altermagnet with Rashba spin-orbit coupling. We calculate the spin-velocity susceptibility response function beyond the intraband response regime and find that the interband longitudinal and transverse Edelstein responses are governed by the Zeeman quantum metric and Zeeman Berry curvature, respectively. The density of states presents a logarithmic van Hove singularity at exactly the negative value of the energy below which four disconnected Fermi contours emerge. This defines three distinctive regions for the position of the Fermi level, through which the Edelstein susceptibility tensor displays characteristic spectral features, reflecting the topological change of the Fermi surface. The resulting spin magnetization shows a strong dependence on the driving frequency and on the orientation of the in-plane external electric field. Our results highlight new possibilities for electrical and optical control of the spin Edelstein effect in altermagnets that could find spintronic applications.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Altermagnetism-induced magneto-optical effects
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Jun Ōiké, Robert Peters, Koki Shinada
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Altermagnets break time-reversal symmetry despite their zero net magnetization, enabling time-reversal-odd responses while retaining the advantages of antiferromagnets. However, magneto-optical (MO) effects are not universal among altermagnets because MO effects typically arise from magnetic dipole order (ferromagnetism), which is generally absent in altermagnets. In this work, we address this limitation by establishing octupolar MO effects, which arise from magnetic octupole order through spatial dispersion. Owing to this distinct origin, octupolar MO effects do not necessarily require spin-orbit coupling even in collinear magnets and can arise without an external magnetic field in antiferromagnets where conventional MO effects are symmetry-forbidden. Such antiferromagnets include $d$-wave altermagnets such as RuO$_2$ and KV$_2$Se$_2$O, certain $g$- and $i$-wave altermagnets, including CrSb, as well as noncoplanar antiferromagnets such as MnTe$_2$ and pyrochlore iridates with all-in-all-out magnetic order. From an experimental perspective, octupolar MO effects can reach detectable magnitudes and offer potential for magnetic-domain imaging, as supported by numerical calculations showing $μ$rad-scale Faraday rotation for a 100-nm-thick sample in the visible-light range and a sign reversal between opposite domains. Furthermore, octupolar MO effects are linked to an $f$-sum rule, enabling a quantitative estimate of the spin magnetic octupole moment from optical measurements. These results extend the scope of MO effects to a broad class of antiferromagnets, including altermagnets, and open a field-free optical route to exploring magnetic octupole order.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Altermagnetism in moiré quasicrystals
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Zi-Ming Wang, Rui Chen, Dong-Hui Xu
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Altermagnetism is a collinear compensated magnetic phase with zero net magnetization and momentum-dependent spin polarization. Quasicrystalline altermagnetism extends altermagnetism beyond periodic crystals, with noncrystallographic symmetries allowing high-order spin polarization patterns. Here, we propose a symmetry-based approach to realizing quasicrystalline altermagnetism by twisting collinear magnetic layers. Specifically, we demonstrate that the $30^{\circ}$-twisted honeycomb lattice bilayers form the dodecagonal quasicrystals supporting an $i$-wave altermagnetic phase. We further find that $45^{\circ}$-twisted bilayers preserving fourfold rotational symmetry support a mirror-driven $l$-wave phase with eight nodal lines. We characterize these altermagnetic patterns through plane-wave-projected spin-resolved spectral functions and spin-resolved conductances. Our work provides a systematic route to high-angular-order quasicrystalline altermagnetism through twist engineering.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Higher-order topology induced by altermagnetism in quasicrystals
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Xingmin Huo, Xingchuan Zhu, Xingyu Ma, Shiping Feng, Huaiming Guo
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Altermagnetism (AM), a novel magnetic phase featuring zero net magnetization and momentum-dependent spin splitting, provides a compelling platform for exploring exotic quantum phenomena. While recent studies have extended the concept of AM to quasicrystals, the momentum-dependent spin splitting in the absence of translational symmetry remains inadequately understood. Here, we investigate the emergence of higher-order topological phases (HOTPs) in Thue-Morse and Ammann-Beenker quasicrystals, driven by the coupling between $d$-wave quasicrystal AM orders and a two-dimensional topological insulator. We reveal that the $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave AM exhibits a ferromagnetism-like aspect in opening edge gaps and inducing zero-energy higher-order topological corner states. In contrast, conventional antiferromagnetic and $d_{xy}$-wave AM configurations are unable to induce the higher-order topological gaps. These findings highlight the pivotal role of altermagnetic symmetry and its alignment with lattice corners in the realization of HOTPs and establish that the emergence of HOTPs can serve as a signature for identifying altermagnetic orders in aperiodic systems.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Noise spectroscopy of insulating and itinerant altermagnets
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Lucas V. Pupim, Mathias S. Scheurer
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: One of the central goals in the emergent field of altermagnetism is the unambiguous experimental identification and characterization of altermagnetic order across a variety of compounds. This motivates exploring tools that can clearly distinguish altermagnets from antiferromagnets, based on symmetry signatures, and offer access to the dominant orbital character (e.g., d -wave versus g -wave) of the magnetic order parameter. In this work, we theoretically explore the potential of noise magnetometry for this task, studying contributions from both magnons and itinerant electrons in different regimes and scenarios. While altermagnetism and antiferromagnetism also lead to different noise spectra for magnons, we find the most striking and symmetry-sensitive signatures in the charge fluctuations of itinerant altermagnets. Both for the homogeneous bulk case and in the presence of strain and/or around domain walls, we identify noise contributions that are only permitted by symmetry in the altermagnet and, thus, provide a unique signature of altermagnetism. Furthermore, the angular dependence of noise around domain walls also offers access to the orbital character of the altermagnet. On a more technical note, we discuss the role and relevance of lattice effects related to the dipole tensor. We hope that our work will help pave the way toward the clear experimental identification of altermagnetism across a wide range of candidate materials.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Ligand-mediated origin of altermagnetic spin splitting
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Luigi Camerano, Federico Bisti, Gianni Profeta
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Altermagnets host spin-split electronic bands despite zero net magnetization, opening new routes for spintronics beyond conventional ferromagnets. Going beyond symmetry-based classifications, which specify allowed terms but not their hierarchy, here we use first-principles calculations and Wannier Hamiltonian engineering to uncover the microscopic bonding contributions of altermagnetic spin splitting in the g -wave altermagnet Co 1 / 4 NbSe 2 . We show that the splitting is captured by a short-range tight-binding model, establishing its local origin. By selectively controlling hopping channels, we demonstrate that the dominant contribution arises not from direct magnetic-ion hopping, but from ligand-mediated hybridization that transfers anisotropy to itinerant states. This identifies ligand-assisted coupling as a dominant mechanism driving altermagnetic spin splitting in intercalated metals, providing a microscopic bridge between minimal models and material-specific electronic structure calculations in altermagnets.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Magnetic circular dichroism of terahertz modes and selection rules of Raman-active optical phonons in the polar altermagnet candidate Mn 2 Mo 3 O 8
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: F. Schilberth, K. Vasin, M. Knauft, M. Kondákor, M. Vuckovic, N. Herrmann, K. Penc, M. Minola, B. Keimer, V. A. Martinez, K. Panda, A. A. Sirenko, L. Prodan, V. Tsurkan, A. A. Tsirlin, I. Kézsmárki, J. Deisenhofer
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: We investigated the magnetic and vibrational excitations in the collinear altermagnet candidate Mn 2 Mo 3 O 8 by temperature-dependent Raman scattering and magneto-optical THz time-domain transmission spectroscopy. By comparison to calculations accurately capturing the eigenfrequencies of the vibrational eigenmodes, we identify all optical phonons, including the lowest-lying Raman modes of A 1 and E 2 type, which had remained elusive in a previous Raman study. Moreover, we compare the selection rules for optically active phonons in the paramagnetic and the magnetically ordered phases of Mn 2 Mo 3 O 8 and analyze the Raman selection rules with respect to pseudoangular momentum conservation. No splitting of the degenerate paramagnetic E 2 optical phonons into circularly polarized modes could be resolved below T N , indicating negligible morphic effects of optical phonons upon magnetic ordering. In contrast, we observe strong magnetic circular dichroism at a broad THz excitation band, emerging in the magnetically ordered state. This band, potentially originating from two-magnon excitations, is only electric-dipole active and features a field-dependent two-component fine structure. Its magnetic circular dichroism vanishes above the spin-flop transition at 4 T.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Exotic superconducting states in altermagnets
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Kirill Parshukov, Andreas P. Schnyder
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: The interplay between magnetism and superconductivity is one of the central topics of condensed matter physics, which has recently been put into new light by the discovery of altermagnets. Here, we study this interplay from a fundamental symmetry perspective using irreducible co-representations of the altermagnetic spin-point groups. We construct and tabulate all symmetry-allowed pairing functions for altermagnets, which uncovers numerous exotic pairing states. We focus on three of them, namely, (i) a nonunitary altermagnetic superconductor with different spatial anisotropies for the spin-up and spin-down condensates, (ii) a half-and-half metal-superconductor where only electrons with one of the two spin components form Cooper pairs, and (iii) a spin chiral superconductor with spin-polarized chiral edge states. Interestingly, the first of these three superconductors exhibits an unusual fractional ac Josephson current for only one of the two spin polarizations, even though the two condensates are symmetry related. We present phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau theories for these unconventional superconductors and show that they correspond to stable minima of the free energies. We examine their topological properties, study the effects of small spin-orbit coupling, consider possible material examples, and investigate their topological responses.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Probing Chern Topology through Hall-Sensitive Photonic Spin Hall Shifts in a d-wave Altermagnet
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Mahnoor Sajid, Maha Siddiqui, Muzamil Shah
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the photonic spin Hall effect in a two-dimensional Rashba-coupled $d$-wave altermagnetic Chern system subjected to a uniform out-of-plane exchange field. We first analyze the energy-band structure and the Dirac mass distribution at the high-symmetry points, where $m_Γ=m_M=Δ_x, m_X=Δ_x-4 t_J$, and $m_Y=Δ_x+4 t_J$. Band inversions at high-symmetry points generate both a topologically trivial regime $(C=0)$ and Chern-insulating phases $(C= \pm 1)$. Employing the Kubo formalism for the optical conductivity together with the reflection matrix for a substrate-supported conducting sheet, we compute helicity-dependent finite-waist displacements of a reflected Gaussian beam. The resulting optical response exhibits a minimum interband absorption threshold, a Van Hove-type spectral feature, and distinct transitions at the $X$ and $Y$ points arising from the momentum dependence of the exchange field. Under the specified Hall-tensor and polarization sign conventions, the longitudinal helicity half-separation is odd upon reversal of the optical Hall conductivity and correspondingly changes sign between opposite-Chern phases, whereas the transverse half-separation is even in the Hall response. The maximal spin-dependent splitting occur in the vicinity of the pseudo-Brewster reflectance minimum. The longitudinal spin splitting reverses sign between opposite Chern phases, reflecting the exchange-controlled optical Hall response, while its pronounced spectral variations reveal the influence of inequivalent interband transitions induced by the $d$-wave altermagnetic exchange. These findings establish polarization-resolved photonic beam shifts as a sensitive probe of Hall-active topological phases and their characteristic optical spectra.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Disentangling Spin and Orbital Contributions in the Search for Altermagnetic Terahertz Conversion in RuO2
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Jiahao Liu, Yuxiao Mo, Tongyang Guan, Wenhui Fang, Yongwei Cui, Wentao Qin, Zhe Yuan, Lishu Zhang, Zhensheng Tao, Yizheng Wu
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Rutile RuO2 has emerged as a prominent candidate altermagnet, yet the microscopic origin of its reported charge-angular-momentum conversion remains unsettled. Recent theoretical and experimental advances have highlighted a potentially dominant role of orbital transport, raising a fundamental ambiguity between spin- and orbital-mediated conversion in RuO2. Here, we report the first experimental disentanglement of the spin- and orbital-to-charge conversion channels in RuO2 heterostructures using terahertz emission spectroscopy. We identify Fe as a predominantly spin-current injector, whereas Ni and permalloy predominantly inject orbital currents, revealing a substantial orbital contribution to ultrafast terahertz emission. Under controlled spin-current injection, we find no evidence for inverse altermagnetic spin-splitting effect. Instead, the observed anisotropy is consistent with an anisotropic inverse spin Hall response that is strongly conditioned by the near-interface environment. Under orbital-current injection, the anisotropy is markedly weaker, indicating that orbital-to-charge conversion is largely isotropic in RuO2. Our results establish orbital transport and interface-conditioned spin Hall conversion as key to terahertz emission from RuO2, underscoring the need to disentangle spin, orbital, and interfacial contributions before assigning anisotropy to altermagnetism.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Nonlocal multipolar spin accumulation in altermagnets beyond d-wave
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: J. W. Gonzalez
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: In spin-conserving models of $g$- and $i$-wave altermagnets, the uniform longitudinal conductivity has no spin-odd component. A point injector reveals higher moments of the Fermi velocity through the nonlocal spin accumulation. Boltzmann theory predicts that the rank $m=2,4,6$ of the first nonzero spin-odd velocity moment sets the leading angular harmonic, its asymptotic radial dependence $r^{2-m}$, and its amplitude scaling $τ^{m-3}$ at fixed distance and injected current. For $g$-wave order, the fourth moment produces a fourth angular harmonic with an asymptotic $r^{-2}$ tail. Quantum transport simulations support the radial profiles predicted by finite-geometry Boltzmann theory without an amplitude fit. Across the three symmetries, the quantum amplitudes exceed the Boltzmann predictions based on the Born scattering time by $15-65$\% in the windows analyzed. In a two-contact ribbon, we detect the $g$-wave fourth harmonic at $6.8\,σ$ in an independent set of 1800 disorder realizations using a preselected radial window. Its amplitude decreases when the altermagnetic splitting is reduced.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Bichromatic light-induced electronic torques on the Néel vector in Rashba magnetic multipoles from $p$-wave magnets to $i$-wave altermagnets
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Mohsen Yarmohammadi
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Light can control magnetic order on ultrafast timescales, but for a two-dimensional magnet with an out-of-plane order parameter $\boldsymbol N\parallel\hat z$, the inverse Faraday field is collinear with $\boldsymbol N$ and gives no transverse torque. Here we show that bichromatic $(ω,bω)$ light generates electronic torques perpendicular to $\boldsymbol N$ in Rashba-coupled magnetic multipoles, from $p$-wave ($n=1$) magnets to $i$-wave ($n=6$) altermagnets. Beyond high-frequency effective fields, we evaluate the exact Floquet response and the generalized torque per occupied electron, for prescribed occupations. The momentum-dependent exchange terms dominate this Fermi-sea torque and remove the leading-order zeros (amplitude-ratio blindspots) of the momentum-independent field in the channels tested. For out-of-plane $\boldsymbol N$, rotational symmetry permits a transverse torque only if $\gcd(n,b+1)=1$ for counter-rotating beams or $\gcd(n,b-1)=1$ for co-rotating beams. For in-plane $\boldsymbol N$, the Fermi sea also gives a torque component along $\hat z$ that the momentum-independent field cannot produce. We classify the active channels, with $n=1,\dots,6$ and $b=1,\dots,7$, by frequency scaling and origin (cycle-averaged versus oscillating exchange). As a control, a Rashba ferromagnet ($n=0$) has one symmetry-allowed out-of-plane channel and a weak in-plane response without a selection rule. Finite-momentum occupied-state physics is therefore essential for light-driven torques in unconventional magnets, and the exact Floquet calculation validates and extends the high-frequency description.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Narrow-Band Magnetism Allowed by Quantum Geometry: Altermagnetism and Beyond
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Minxuan Wang, Pei-Han Lin, Yang Ge, Jiabin Yu
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Quantum geometry plays a central role in shaping correlated phases in narrow bands, yet its influence on the competition between distinct magnetic orders, especially the emergence of altermagnetism, remains largely unexplored. To address this question, we study the quadrupole insulator model with strictly onsite generalized Hubbard-Kanamori interactions, in which both Néel antiferromagnetism and altermagnetism are symmetry-permitted. Depending on the parameters, the isolated narrow lowest band of the model can either be obstructed atomic with strong quantum geometry or trivial atomic with weak quantum geometry, while the dispersion is identical in the two cases. By partially filling the lowest band, our Hartree-Fock calculations show only conventional ferromagnetic phases for the weak quantum geometric case, while we find two collinear altermagnetic phases, as well as nematic phases, for the strong quantum geometric case. Such a dramatic difference can be understood by the distinct characters of the projected interaction: the projected interactions acquire sizable longer-range channels only for the strong quantum geometric case, while they are dominated by the on-site Hubbard channel in the weak quantum geometric case. These results establish the essential role of quantum geometry for altermagnetism to emerge from interacting narrow bands where crystalline symmetries cannot sufficiently constrain the magnetic order.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Magnetoelectric paramagnets: exchange-driven s-wave spin splitting in compensated magnets
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Daniel D Rivera, Gustavo Martini Dalpian, Carlos Mera Acosta
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: In conventional antiferromagnets, local electric environments remain equivalent and combined inversion and time-reversal ( PT ) symmetry enforces spin-degenerate bands, whereas altermagnets and related compensated phases realize this inequivalence as long-range order electric environments. Materials with zero net magnetization can, nevertheless, exhibit spin-split electronic bands when the local electric environments associated with opposite magnetic moments are inequivalent. Here we investigate this regime in which electric inequivalence arises locally from a polymorphous magnetic configuration, represented by a static, globally compensated arrangement of nonzero local moments with distinct spin neighborhoods. These neighborhoods self-consistently generate site-dependent electric offsets through the exchange-correlation potential. The correlation between these offsets and the local moments produces a finite potential-weighted Néel vector even though the net magnetization vanishes, providing a route to exchange-driven, s-wave-like spin splitting without chemical substitution, structural relaxation, heterostructures, or long-range-ordered electric inequivalence. Using spin-density functional theory for EuB 6 , for which previous calculations identified spin-polymorphism-induced on-site electric inequivalence, we contrast an electrically homogeneous antiferromagnetic reference with polymorphous representations of the paramagnetic state. The former remains spin degenerate, whereas the polymorphous configurations develop environment-dependent charge redistribution and finite spin splitting in the unfolded spectral function. These results establish magnetic polymorphism as an additional design axis for spin-resolved electronic structures beyond ferromagnetism, ferrimagnetism, and altermagnetism.
